- Dr. Urelix: I will give you a substantial amount of emeralds and a piece of quality iron armor in return for your silence on my little operation here.
- Dr. Urelix: I'll advise you to take my deal. Imagine what will happen if you should report my operation to the police. Yes, you'll save a few folk here, but how will the golems be made?
- Dr. Urelix: Without them, both Gavel and Wynn would struggle under the weight of our wars. Is this operation so immoral, then? Sacrifices must be made in order to survive.
- Dr. Urelix: I'll give you some time to consider my proposition. Take from my chest if you wish to take up my offer, otherwise get out of here and do not return.
Either take the bribe or return to Detective Hart
If you take the bribe:
Dialogue:
- Dr. Urelix: Ahh, a wise choice. Production will continue then...and you've earned yourself a pocket full of emeralds at the same time.
- Dr. Urelix: Whether you truly see things my way or simply understand that my work is necessary, I couldn't care less. What matters is not your morality, but your choice.
- Dr. Urelix: Enjoy your armor and money, and please escort yourself to the exit.
If you return to Detective Hart:
Dialogue:
- Detective Hart: You've returned, I see. Any news on the situation?
- Detective Hart: Yes, we're aware of the Golem factory. Were the criminals using it as a base?
- Detective Hart: Wha...fleshcrafting?! Golems are powered by suspended villagers?! Is this true, soldier?
- Detective Hart: We'll need to round up reinforcements immediately, and storm this factory! This cannot go on a moment longer!
- Detective Hart: Don't think you'll go unrewarded, soldier. There will be justice for this grave defilement of our people.
Talk to Javier in the Pirate Cove at [-640, 53, -3117]
Dialogue:
- Javier: Garh, you look like a mighty fine adventurer, lad. But perhaps your pockets are a little lighter than you want, eh?
- Javier: Perhaps we be making a deal, lad, and it'll make us both rich!
- Javier: Ye see, lad, me treasure has been lost for quite some time, I kept it in a ocean village named Sarnfic, in a secret room.
- Javier: Argh, but lad. The village vanished out of nowhere! Like some kind of dark magic! I swears to ye, I tell no lies!
- Javier: So ye see, in me old age I could use a spot of me lawful gold to see me through me final years.
- Javier: Don't fret though, chuck, old Javier always kept a back up plan.
- Javier: I left me old sea fearin' map in me old hideout, it'll tell ye where we can find me old gold.
- Javier: So, lad. Are ya willin' to make ye'self mighty wealthy? Good.
- Javier: Me old hideout's hidden inside that there skull at the entrance to our mighty fine establishment, Bring me that map, lad!
Find Javier's map, hidden in the skull tomb at the entrance of the island

lines.title: finding Javier's map
lines.text:
The entrance to the skull Javier mentions is at [-672, 44, -3195]. Once you reach it, head inside, and follow the path until you reach a four-way intersection. Go straight across the intersection, then turn left and continue to follow the path. You will reach a large open treasure room, and the following dialogue will play:
*Deceased Buccaneer: Halt it there, laddy! The wind has told us that yer looking for treasure map. Ah, ye'll not get it so easily.
*Deceased Buccaneer: Ye see, us spirits are as greedy as our physical selves were. 'ere's no foolin' 'round there. We want yer money, and only then will we open the paths to the map.
*Deceased Buccaneer: One full stack of emeralds will satisfy our needs. Go to the front of this tomb if ye have what we want.
As the buccaneer says, walk to the tomb at [-682, 19, -3205]. This will open a new tunnel out of the treasure room and trigger more dialogue:
*Deceased Buccaneer: Good luck on that petty journey of yers. Just find the whole path, and yerself'll be just fine...
*You go on as you can hear laughter spreading through the walls...
Go into the newly opened tunnel, and follow it through. It will connect back to the main path, but another new tunnel will open across from it; follow this one as well. You will be stopped at one point and a figure will fall from the ceiling, spawning a level 60 Deceased Trespasser which you can either kill or simply avoid.
Very shortly afterwards, a hole in the floor will appear beneath you - if you fall through, you will have to go through the tunnels again. You will then pass through a "minefield" in which stepping on any of the pressure plates damages you, and can progress by going to the right. Avoiding the constantly firing cannonballs in the next hallway will allow you to progress to a tunnel that leads straight to the map. Once you have the map, you can exit and return to Javier.
Dialogue:
- Javier: Argh, yer talented aren't you lad! Many thanks indeed, now we can see where me treasure be buried.
- Javier: Hrmm, well, garr, blast it all
- Javier: I canne read me own darn map, lad! What'dya do with it? Scratch off the ink with yer pennies?
- Javier: Gar, sorry lad. It be the test of time that failed old Javier, not you.
- Javier: Fear not, lad. There be an old friend of Javier's that can help decipher this old rag.
- Javier: Go to the old Mage Island, there be a man by the name of Dalben who can restore me map to its former glory. Get it done lad, and bring me treasure back!
Talk to Dalben on Mage Island about restoring the map
Dialogue:
- Dalben: What's this? A traveller? How might we assist you?
- Dalben: Ah, I see, you wish to explore the ocean depths? But for what possible reason?
- Dalben: This map... How did you acquire it? This is enchanted by our people.
- Dalben: You... You seek Sarnfic, don't you?
- Dalben: Alas, that place has history. We, the Mage Council, banished that city long ago to hide the horrific power hidden within a treasure a pirate hid there.
- Dalben: A pair of boots, made from a black material fashioned from the stone of an evil place, incredibly dark magic. But we do not believe the filthy idiotic pirate knew what he'd found.
- Dalben: I must say, we, the council regret having to lay waste an entire village over a pair of boots. There was no other way.
- Dalben: Who knows why he even kept the boots. If he had known about their power, I'm sure he would have used it for evil. But we sense no evil in you, so as such we will aid you in your quest.
- Dalben: We hope that you will use the boots for good, despite the dark intentions. We will lift the enchantment once lain upon the charts, but it will cost you.
- Dalben: Give me [5 Emerald Blocks], that should cover the cost.
Bring back 5 Blocks of Emerald to Dalben
Dialogue:
- Dalben: Brilliant. That seems in order. Here you go.
- Dalben: We only hope that the treasure will never fall into the hands of that pirate again, we'd much rather they fall into yours.
- Dalben: Well? What does it say? Go to that location! Find the treasure!
Explore the cave in the ocean, located at [-187, 16, -3452]
The fastest way to get to the cave in the ocean is to swim or use a boat from Selchar.
Find [1 Ocean Treasure] and bring it back to Javier in Pirate Cove

lines.title: how to find the Ocean Treasure
lines.text: Once you enter Sarnfic, there will be a long pathway going to the south, which you should follow. When you reach an intersection, go straight/to the right, then continue following the path. Eventually, you should reach a large room with a few houses - the Treasure Guardian is in a section of this room, through the small tunnel at [-87, 14, -3038]. Kill it to get the Ocean Treasure, then leave and return to Javier.
Dialogue:
- Javier: Gnar, you did it lad! Ye brought back old Javiers gold! And as I promised, heres yer share of the loot.
- Javier: I threw in something extra for ye. It's an old key I salvaged a few years back, from the shipwreck of a legendary pirate.
- Javier: Who knows what it leads to? Maybe a treasure hoard, or maybe the ol' swashbuckler wanted to lead someone into a trap.
- Javier: Me bones are too old for a grand adventure like that, guess ye'll have to figure it out for yerself.
Speak to Piere in the Llevigar Plains at [-1851, 56, -4959]
Dialogue:
- Piere: Oh sweet baby bovine, my house, what am I going to do? Wait, who are you?
- Piere: Oh, a Human. Did the Llevigar authorities send you?
- Piere: Detective Jackson has already been here. Not that he's doing anything useful.
- Piere: An Orc managed to find some fire-imbued magical axe and burned down my house! Jackson didn't even call a firefighter!!
- Piere: I don't know what to do, but maybe if you find Detective Jackson, you can kick his sorry rear into gear...
- Piere: The Orcs are already savage brutes. If they really have their hands on magical weapons, we're all in trouble!
- Piere: I believe Detective Jackson is by his cart "planning his next move." He's not far from here. Just continue past my farm!
Report the attack to Detective Jackson at [-1731, 53, -4836]
Dialogue:
- Detective Jackson: How can I go about this...? I can't get involved myself, and they won't let me near... Wait, a human?
- Detective Jackson: ...what do you MEAN "what am I doing?" This is a delicate situation! I need to- wait...actually, you might just be the help I need.
- Detective Jackson: I'll give you the lowdown- we believe the orcs stole magical weaponry from within Llevigar, particularly a flaming axe.
- Detective Jackson: However, that's a loophole in the ceasefire we had enacted with the Orcs. Theft isn't considered an act of aggression...
- Detective Jackson: And that means my hands are tied. Humans, however, were not mentioned in the notes, so you'll need to retrieve it.
- Detective Jackson: Our only saving grace is that it'll be impossible for them to replicate its power- Orcs are hilariously inept at magic.
- Detective Jackson: But, to the primary problem- You've probably seen how many orc camps are around here. Searching will take a long while...
- Detective Jackson: My only leads are that the "Sablestone" and "Loamsprout" camps seem to be celebrating recently. Best to start there, yes?
- Detective Jackson: Just to review- You need to search those two camps for the Axe of Llevigar, and then return it to me if you find it.
- Detective Jackson: Sablestone is to the north, and Loamsprout to the south. They will be guarded, so don't be afraid to knock some heads.
Look for the stolen weapon at the Sablestone and Loamsprout Orc camps
- This does not seem like the weapon. It's just a heavy-looking wooden stick.
- This does not seem like the weapon. It's just a potato..?
Once you have inspected both camps:
- This camp doesn't seem to have the weapon either. Maybe Detective Jackson knows what to do next?
Return to Detective Jackson with the news
Dialogue:
- Detective Jackson: I see no axe in your hands, so I should assume neither Sablestone or Loamsprout had it.
- Detective Jackson: Wait, really? A stick was the most powerful weapon they had? And Loamsprout...threw their dinner at you...?
- Detective Jackson: I can't believe this! How are those...those THINGS outsmarting us?! Are they shuffling the axe between camps?
- Detective Jackson: There are over a dozen camps between the Orcs and Goblins that they could be swapping it between!
- Detective Jackson: What if the GOBLINS get a hold of it?! They're the cleverest by half of all of them, so that could actually be a threat!
- Detective Jackson: Searching all the camps one by one will be far too slow, gah!! How am I going to fix this?!
- Detective Jackson: There's Earthpit, and Cliffhearth, Shineridge and Stonecave, Sunspark, Mudspring, Holehold, I-
An Orc named "Poxper" will run by the cart, chasing a "Runefire" while holding a blue axe.
- ???: Fire! Stop!! I hold magic cutter! LISTEN TO POXPER!!
- Detective Jackson: I- I can't believe it, that has to be the one! AFTER THAT ORC, NOW!!
Find the hidden camp in the water near Piere's house at [-1822, 49, -4903]
Dialogue:
- ???: GRRRH!! What 'Uthniiazek' mean?!

As you approach the exit at [-1861, 23, -4920] (not the one labelled "EXIT" at [-1850, 23, -4920]), an Orc Builder will spawn and cover up the exit. You must the kill the Orc Gatekeeper to break through the wall covering the exit and progress through the hidden camp.
Kill Orc Leader Poxper
There are three keys at the north, east, and south walls of the next room, easily reachable through parkour. Use all three keys on the door to the west to continue.
Dialogue:
- Poxper: Uthniiazek! Uthniiazek!! WHY NO LISTEN TO Poxper?
- Poxper: Stupid Villager magic thing! Why fire no listen?
- Poxper: Poxper say thing and make fire...what else axe say? 'Azektoluth?'
- Poxper: Hraahah! Poxper control fire! Fire- kill human with Poxper! Uthniiazek! Azektoluth!
Return the Magic Axe to the Detective
Dialogue:
- Detective Jackson: That looks like the axe of Llevigar to me! Blue finish, hot to the touch- well done! What Orc boss had stolen it?
- Detective Jackson: Poxper? That...hm. This could be bad. I've head that name, and he's a fairly prolific Orc chief. You killed him, right?
- Detective Jackson: Mmm... Hopefully that Veretel won't catch wind of it. Regardless, you've done a great service for Villager-kind!
- Detective Jackson: Here's your compensation for that. Thank you for the aid!
Talk to Tarod in Nesaak's Forest at [-7, 68, -793]
Dialogue:
- Tarod: You're one of those soldier types, right? My name is Tarod, and I could really use your assistance here.
- Tarod: Years ago, I met a very powerful and legendary warrior by the name of Bob. Yes, that Bob.
- Tarod: It's safe to say he was a very, well, admirable man. Him and I slowly became close friends over the years.
- Tarod: That is, until one night, he vanished without a trace. The accepted story is that he was murdered by a pack of ravenous wolves...

- Tarod: Now, I don't buy that story, but... look, the point here is that he's gone now, and I want to find out where the hell he ended up. That depressing zombie lumbering around Ragni clearly isn't him.
- Tarod: I believe he died in this area, and I have been looking for his body for quite a while now, with... less than success.
- Tarod: Rumors have spread that a tomb lies somewhere east of Nesaak, but I've never been able to find it. This is where I need you to help me out, yeah?
- Tarod: Do you think you could help me out here? Search around that area, and report back to me if you see anything noteworthy.
- Tarod: I'd be eternally grateful if you could help me uncover my old friend's true story.
Find Bob's Tomb

lines.title: how to find Bob's Tomb
lines.text: Bob's Tomb is a cave in the mountainside.  If you head directly east from the watchtower on the Southern side of Nesaak, it should be plainly visible as you reach bottom of the mountains.
A strange force prevents you from entering. You can hear some soft laments in the distance...
Report what you've found to Tarod at [-7, 68, -793]
Dialogue:
- Tarod: Welcome back. Did you find anything worthwhile?
- Tarod: Oh? Yeah, that definitely sounds like the tomb! Were you able to see what's inside?
- Tarod: No? There's... a magical barrier? Great... just GREAT...

- Tarod: I have a feeling whoever made that tomb didn't want anyone attempting to get to him, but... Forget it, we have no other options. This is the only way we can place Bob's soul to rest for good.
- Tarod: Listen, I have a guy who can help us out. His name is Wedyf, a sorcerer type. If anyone could get rid of that barrier, it would be him.
- Tarod: He lives in Bremminglar, a small town close to Almuj. Go meet him, I'll wait for your return.
Talk to the sorcerer Wedyf in Bremminglar.
Dialogue:
- Wedyf: Welcome traveler. Are you looking for something?
- Wedyf: Ooh, it has been a long time since I've released an undead...
- Wedyf: The spirit of your dead friend must still be somewhere in this world. This is why we are unable to get close to his body. Soul magic works in mysterious ways.
- Wedyf: Don't worry, I can do it. I've heard a little bit of Bob's story before. What a tragedy. His own infallible protection used against him...
- Wedyf: ...Anyways, there's no need to lament on the past. Now, we need two items. The first is something from Bob himself. The other is the last thing that made his blood drop.
- Wedyf: Out past the other side of Detlas there are two farm houses with an old cave inbetween then. An old florist used to live there, she has a rose that Bob had once cut himself on.
- Wedyf: I will warn you, though; she was corrupted some time ago. It may not be that easy to take the rose, so do be prepared.

- Wedyf: Secondly... something of Bob's. I've heard rumors of a visage of him wandering around Ragni, perhaps you can find something of use from it? Killing enemies in the Nesaak region may be worth your time, as well.
- Wedyf: Bring me [1 Rose] and [1 Bob's Tear].
Bring 1 Bob's Tear from Ragni and 1 Rose from the house in the Nesaak forest around [160, 73, -1012] to Wedyf

lines.title: how to get the items
lines.text: Bob's Tear can be acquired by killing Bob the Zombie, a rare mob spawning in Ragni, loot chests in Ragni, or as a rare drop from mobs in Nesaak Forest. The Rose can be found in a house at (160, 73, -1012) by killing the Rose Florist there. Alternatively, both items can be bought off of the Trade Market.
Dialogue:
- Wedyf: Great, you got everything.
- Wedyf: Although... I might have forgot to tell you about something else too...
- Wedyf: We also need a part of the soul of your dead friend.
- Wedyf: This is something I unfortunately cannot do myself. There is a blacksmith close to Ternaves who does this kind of stuff.
- Wedyf: He can extract the soul from someone's weapon. Very useful in those situations. Go talk to him.
- Wedyf: Bring me the soul, and I'll be able to remove the spell preventing you from entering the tomb.
Talk to the blacksmith in the small settlement southwest of Ternaves at [725, 61, -1468] about Bob's lost soul
Dialogue:
- The Blacksmith: What can I do for ya?
- The Blacksmith: Oh yes! I can extract the soul from weapons!
- The Blacksmith: Bring me the weapons of your friend, and I'll see if I can do something with it!
- The Blacksmith: Oh it's... those weapons. Well, if you know what you're doing...
- The Blacksmith: [1 Depressing Stick], [1 Depressing Spear], [1 Depressing Bow] and [1 Depressing Shears] will do the trick.
- The Blacksmith: Be careful with the weapons, you will only get [ONE] of each. If you lose one, you will have to ask around if anyone has a spare.
- The Blacksmith: Maybe someone will be selling one on the Trade Market in Detlas, who knows.
- The Blacksmith: My apprentice over there has traveled around a lot, they might know where the items are, but I warn you, they are a little bit quirky.
- Apprentice: Weapons of the depressed kind? Oh, of course, of course, I know of the set! Around Nesaak, I hear they are kept.
- Apprentice: An army of Linx you must clear, in a cave you shall find this spear!
- Apprentice: To a skilled archer you must go, best her in a lumberyard and you will have her bow!
- Apprentice: On an altar, effervescence leers, complete the sacrifice and you will gain your shears...
- Apprentice: In the forest, a house frozen in spikes thick, outsmart the contraption and be gifted a stick!
- Apprentice: But beware, beware! Danger lies ahead, and will try to halt you in your stead!
Bring [[Depressing Items#Depressing Weapons|[1 Depressing Stick], [1 Depressing Spear], [1 Depressing Bow] and [1 Depressing Shear]]] to the Blacksmith.

lines.title: how to get the weapons
lines.text:
- You can get the Depressing Stick in by entering a cave underneath the frozen house at (20, 68, -901).

**Dialogue:
**Markque The Wizard: Yo, what's up, bud?
**Markque The Wizard: I've just been hangin' down here working on my teleportation device. The teleporters got partially frozen over, but I'm pretty damn sure they still work.
**Markque The Wizard: Hey, if you want to test it out, be my guest! You can use the teleporter core next to me to start it.
**Markque The Wizard: Right click with it while on the center of the iced over teleporter chamber, and it will teleport you in a direction over to the next chamber.
**Markque The Wizard: It will then teleport you again in a direction 90 degrees clockwise, and it will keep doin' that forever.
**Markque The Wizard: Some of the ice walls have holes in them, and I believe if you use the teleporter core correctly you will be able to make it to the other side where the gold platform is.
**Markque The Wizard: The core is unstable, though, and it will break if you run too far away. Keep that in mind, yeah?
**Markque The Wizard: Oh, and I left an old wand of mine down at the gold platform. The thing was very depressing, though, so it ain't too much of an issue. But hey, if you can get to it, it's all yours, bud, free of cost!
Pick up the teleporter and use it to get to the gold platform at (-12, 50, -860), where you can pick up the depressing stick.
*You can get the Depressing Spear by killing enough Lynx to drop 5 Lucky Lynx Foot items in a large cave at (161, 65, -931), and then right-clicking on the spear at (209, 48, -923) with them.
**The Lucky Lynx Foot items have a description that reads "Bring to the alter of the Depressing Spear".
*You can get the Depressing Bow by fighting a miniboss in the Abandoned Lumber Yard at (-205, 69, -920). When you kill it, the Depressing Bow will be placed in your inventory.
*You can get the Depressing Shear by taking the Effervescent Dagger at (-35, 70, -655), and doing the parkour to reach the tallest pillar. Once you stand on top of it, the Dagger will be taken and you will be given the Depressing Shears.
Dialogue:
- The Blacksmith: ... Hi again. I see you got the weapons.
- The Blacksmith: These weapons emanate so much sadness... I'm sure you heard about Bob's story...
- The Blacksmith: Here is the soul. It's a little bit crushed, but it can do the trick.
- The Blacksmith: Good luck on your quest. Bob was a great hero, anything to help him is good in my book.
Bring back 1 Bob's Crushed Soul to Wedyf.
Dialogue:
- Wedyf: I'm glad to see you again.
- Wedyf: I only need a part of the soul, you can keep the rest.
- Wedyf: Give me a minute, I need to concentrate...
- Wedyf: It is done. You should be able to enter the tomb now. Be careful.
Find Bob's corpse in his tomb.
As you open the door, you feel some soft wind running past you. The lamentations have stopped...
Note: Bob's corpse is in a room underneath the stairs, you will need to open a door to it by standing on a pressure plate.
Report back what you've seen to Tarod
Dialogue:
- Tarod: You're back... Has he... has he finally been put to rest?
- Tarod: It's... hard to hear, knowing that my old friend is really gone, this time, but... I'm happy he won't have to suffer on this war-torn world for another second.

- Tarod: ...I want you to have something. This is his old battle chesplate; he gave it to me a few days before he vanished. I think if he were still here, he'd want you to have this. Please, take good care of it for me...
Talk to Captain Kymer outside Llevigar at [-1991, 34, -4658]
Dialogue:
- Captain Kymer: Aha, another Ragni soldier, eh? Well, a warm welcome to you.
- Captain Kymer: Did you hear about the requests from the Villagers we've gotten? They say these "Orcs" and "Goblins" are threatening their towns and cities.
- Captain Kymer: Primitive, brutal creatures, apparently little better than the zombies we're used to, at least according to the Llevigar military.
- Captain Kymer: So, we figure if might makes right with them, then defeating their leaders should scare them into submission.
- Captain Kymer: Our scouts have identified three "chief" orcs in the area- Elisu, Ceifko and Veltu. Though, strangely Veltu is always surrounded by goblins...

- Captain Kymer: Well,  whatever the case, we're needed to defend Llevigar here. Can you handle the chiefs? They seem to hide in the camps with green flags- search the plains, return once they're dealt with!
Find and kill Orc Chieftains Elisu, Veltu, and Ceifko in the camps around Llevigar- look for green flags

lines.title: finding Elisu
lines.text: Elisu can be found standing right in the middle of a camp northwest of Captain Kymer.

lines.title: finding Ceifko
lines.text: Ceifko is found at the end of a camp inside a cave east of Captain Kymer. You must get 10 Beating Sticks by killing the Earthpit Orc Drummers to open a doorway to Ceifko. The chief themself is accompanied by two Earthpit Orc Revelers. Ceifko moves very quickly by charging around the arena and deals a fair amount of damage, so glassier players should be careful.

lines.title: finding Veltu
lines.text: Veltu is located in a goblin-filled camp north of Captain Kymer. The spot is often overlooked, as it is very muddy and different than the other camps. You must break a mud floor in one of the houses to be able to enter Veltu's room under the house.
Report back to Captain Kymer once you have the three heads.
Dialogue:
- Captain Kymer: Ah, the soldier from earlier! You're back, I see. Any luck defeating those- ...yeesh. Are those their heads?
- Captain Kymer: That's...harsher than I intended, but it works... Not like the Villagers care if they're dead of alive, as long as they're dealt with. I have your share of the reward here.
- Captain Kymer: This kind of surgical strike should help prevent an all-out war with the Orcs. Not sure we'd want a full-scale war to deal with in each province, hah!
- Captain Kymer: You saw that the creatures in Gavel aren't akin to Wynnic fare while you were out, yes? They're a bit, ah...livelier than usual. Better get used to it.
- Captain Kymer: The next major settlement is Olux, in the swamp up north, but I hear the swamp ogres are a lot tougher than the plains' fare. I'd stick around here and train up, first.
Talk to Lanu at [-628, 74, -868].
Go over to the wall with a bunch of ancient runes on it and right-click it.
Talking to Lanu again after finishing the dialogue:
- [1] Yes
Use the Mage's riddle to figure out where it leads

lines.title: solving the mage's riddle
lines.text:
* 
* 
* 



Go to [-530, 65, -670] to find the Cursed Slingra Sheep. The sheep will only last for 120 seconds before exploding.

The door made of leaves can be opened by pressing a button on the floor. Follow the slime path while guiding the sheep and reach the slime cave at [-650, 61, -669]. The correct cave also has the Dropped Journal outside of it.






* 
* 
* 
*
Explore the temple for a way to break the barrier.
An experiment will then occur as a parrot and ocelot are fused together in some way.
Experiment Notes =
The Experiment Notes can be found within the temple, at [-1627, 75, 610].
- Experiment Notes: Project "Slingra"
Vial Chest =
The Vial Chest can be found within the temple, at [-1627, 76, 591].
Entering the room at [-1668, 49, 602] will cause the machine in the room to activate. It will create a slime monster that must be killed to progress.
Right-click the key into the door lock to progress.
The Strange Invitation can be found on the floor at [-1690, 49, 604]. Its description gives the next location for the quest: Slykaar's house near Troms.
Go to Slykaar's residence at [-732, 65, -974] to find out what is hidden there.
A journal is found on a bookshelf at [-721, 50, -965].

lines.title: finding the hidden room
lines.text: The button to open the secret door is at [-726, 49, -970], on the north wall.
What appears to be Slykaar and two shadowy creatures will appear in a shadowed area. The figure who appears to be Slykaar will pound his Relik.
Journey through Slykaar's dimension.
You need 25 Slime Globs to create a bridge to the next island. Note: It asks for Slime Chunks, but the Globs will still create the bridge.
There is an invisible maze. The path is revealed with close proximity to the player.
There is a parkour section where you must bounce across slime blocks. Slime platforms with purple will bounce you higher.
Continue up the path to the altar.
Exit Slykaar's Dimension.
Report back to Lanu about what you've learned.
Talk to Anast in Olux, at [-1834, 62, -5557]
Dialogue:
- Anast: Grr...that no-good, lying, cheating, thieving...graaah!
- Anast: You! Help me out over here! You aren't doing anything important right now, and this is urgent!
- Anast: I got a few questions for you, see? Question one: D'you think crops are supposed to look like THIS?
- Anast: Look at them. I don't think there's a way for 'em to look any more sorry than this.
- Anast: Wha- You think the Oats over there look fine?! Pff. Yeah, right.
- Anast: If that's the case, go grab a scythe and try harvesting those Oats yourself!!
- Anast: Go on, do it! I dare you! See how good they really are!!
Gather [3 Oats] from around Anast.
Harvesting the Oats there will give you Rotten Oats instead of Oat Grains or String
(The oats are in a melon patch at [-1827, 62, -5562].)
- Anast: See? What'd I tell ya? Rotten to the roots! Nothing here is ANY good!!
- Anast: They were growing pretty slow this year, all my crops, and then some salesman walks into town with some "MiracleCure" fertilizer.
- Anast: I shoulda known it was too good to be true, but he said everyone else tried it too, so I bought some and tried to salvage this mess.
- Anast: And here we are- me out half my savings and my fields as smelly and dead as an actual CORPSE!
- Anast: Just to prove this ridiculous phony Doubiss is a fraud- Here. I see some roots over here. Watch this, and tell me if this is a "miracle!"
- Anast: Here we go, here comes the big phenomenal growth he promised me!
- Anast: WOW, INCREDIBLE! AMAZING! It's almost like this is actual poison or something!!
- Anast: That Doubiss won't budge for my refund. I spent... so many emeralds... on this tripe! So that's where YOU come in.
- Anast: He's in that blue and gray tent by the bank. I don't care how you do it, but get my money back and we'll split it half-and-half, deal?
Find Doubiss the salesman in Olux near the bank at [-1769, 66, -5539].
Dialogue:
- Doubiss: Good day to ya! What is it ye be needin' from ol' Doubiss' stock?
- Doubiss: Oh. Oh, goodie. That idiot farmer's sendin' ya to get his money back, ain't he? Sweet baby bovine, this is ridiculous...
- Doubiss: Since he obviously ain't gonna be listenin' to me anytime soon, lemme tell ya what the issue is with my fertilizer...
- Doubiss: Nothing! My fertilizer really does work! He probl'ly exaggerated how good I said it'd work, too! What'd he say, twice, three times the growth? More?
- Doubiss: All the other farmers are usin' it right now and look at their fields! Heck, the only reason these crops ain't dead is because of my product!
- Doubiss: Y'know why? Next time ya' pass a farm, take a good whiff o' the water, maybe a sip or two if you can manage. It'll be smelly and bitter.
- Doubiss: The crops, when I got here, were lookin' as pathetic as ya get. I ain't a gamblin' man, but I'd be willing ta bet something's up with the water here.
- Doubiss: The smell gets worse the closer ya get to the crypts in town, and while I ain't a native Oluxer, I've heard enough to know the wellspring is in the cave hear there.
- Doubiss: It'll prob'ly be best fer everyone if ya took a looksee. Maybe if ya find some evidence, ya can show that to the crazy farmer, have 'im quit pesterin' me, eh?
- Doubiss: The cave is on a little hill, next to the crypt. Careful ya don't go trippin' over a gravestone, now!
Search the aquifer at [-1781, 85, -5598] for the problem with the water.
- Doubiss: Oi, bucko! Took my advice, eh? I'd figured I'd join ye, 'n see for myself what was goin' on.
- Doubiss: And boy am I glad I bring me water in bottles. This stuff's rancid, full a' swamp slimes. No idea why they're here, though.
- Doubiss: The buggers stick to mountain caves. They don't come down this far, usually... suppose there's an exception fer everything.
- Doubiss: 's no wonder that Anast's crops ain't growin'. This is right under his farm! But we got some clear proof now, ain't we?
- Doubiss: Howzabout ya take care o' this? I ain't a fighter, but if ya mulch these slimes the water oughta clear up, I figure.
Kill the slimes in the aquifer and bring back [Polluted Slime] to Anast.
- Something huge is dropping from the ceiling!
Dialogue:
- Anast: Pyyyyeww! Yeesh, kid! You smell worse than a pig's sty! What the heck happened to you, where've you been?!
- Anast: Ugh, eww! I don't want any of this sludge! I demand an explanation, now!!
- Anast: ...mhm, mhm...you went into the well cave...and found what, slimes?! Why would SLIMES be there?
- Anast: I wouldn't believe you if you weren't... well, uh... covered in the stuff. But that's definitely rancid.
- Anast: So... that means I've been... oh dear lord I'm an idiot.
- Anast: I guess I owe you some thanks anyway for trying to clear the sludge out. Suppose this year's harvest is just a bust.
- Anast: Can't sell what little I have, so I figure you can take it, and a bit of cash too, since you basically did an exterminator's job.
- Anast: Just... do me a favor and use that money to buy some good soap and wash up. I'm thankful and all, but you stink to high heaven!
Talk to Telvu the mage at [136, 76, -688].
Find Theorick's stave at Nesaak bank.

lines.title: finding the wand
lines.text: In order to get the wand, use the surroundings to get on top and drop into the display case at 99, 77, -780 which will give the player the wand and teleport them outside, allowing them to leave.
Enter the portal the mage made.
While the player can enter the portal and save a lot of time, they can also manually travel to the Door of Time themselves.
The portal is 6 blocks on the left side of the mage, indicated by blue particules.
Enter the Gate of Time at [-583, 72, -1175] and travel back in time.
Right-click the altar with  Theorick's Staff.
Explore Past Nesaak.
Talk to Psern to continue.
Find Theorick in the forest west of Nesaak [3652, 72, 1208].
Several Zombies will appear behind the player and Theorick.
Theorick will cast an ice spell against a small group of zombies.
- Theorick: Whuh! That's her voice! Where is she?! I just cleared this area!
Theorick will cast another ice spell against the zombie following the girl.
Head to the base of the operation south of Nesaak [3738, 69, 1265].
Theorick will teleport his crew to the Roots of Corruption.
Protect the portal.

lines.title: protecting the portal
lines.text: After Theorick's dialogue, a Corrupted Hellbeast will spawn, break the bridge, and push you away from the portal. Press the button on top of an emerald block to start the fight. Survive against the attacking monsters until the time limit runs out, and kill the Corrupted Hellbeasts whnever they spawn. Then, right-click three molten cores (dropped from the Corrupted Hellbeasts) into the bridge hologram.
- You successfully protected the Portal!
- The bridge has been fixed!
Theorick appears in Past Nesaak.
Theorick will start his freezing spell.
Tell Telvu the mage what happened.
Find Eppo at [-207, 37, -531]. The entrance to his cave can be found at [-198, 37, -520].
Dialogue:
- Eppo: Let's give it another try!
- Eppo: Ready the drill, men!
- Eppo: Darn. The drill just won't start.
- Eppo: Hey, Guard! Do you know anything about Electromagic? Come up here to the drill, maybe you can take a look?
Walk up next to the drill.
- Eppo: Oh! Never mind, it lit up, back up!
The drill will spark, then move a little into the ice wall and blow up without damaging the ice.
- Eppo: For the love of Bob... Why won't you just break?
- Eppo: This ice was created by Theorick, a Twain who defended this area many many years ago.
- Eppo: When the corruption got too much... He froze everything, including the people. Do you see them in there?
- Eppo: We've tried desperately to get them out, but we've tried all the equipment we had, including this Corkian drill.
- Eppo: Maybe we should get more destructive... The demolition expert, Rhudya, is further down the cave.
- Eppo: It's a long shot, but worth a try. Would you be able to get it while I clear this space?
Go deeper into the cave and speak to Rhudya.
Dialogue:
- Rhudya: Whup! You're on private property, y'know! Oh, Eppo sent ya? That's fair enough.
- Rhudya: You'll be needing this TNT then, make sure not to drop it though, whup!
- Rhudya: Just travel through this cave and you'll be returned to Eppo easy-peasy!
Parkour across the ice platforms in the cave.
Return to Eppo with the tnt.
Avoid the mobs in the cave to reach the exit and return to Eppo.
Dialogue:
- Eppo: Very nice, this might do the trick.
- Eppo: Back up, I'll ignite the explosive.
- Eppo: ...
- Eppo: NOTHING? Not even a scratch. I don't understand Theoricks ice.. It's not real.
- Eppo: I'm not sure what else we can do then...
Rhudya will blow open another entrance to the cave.
- Rhudya: HEY. Eppo, over here! Near the cave!
- Rhudya: Did the explosive not work? I found this old mineshaft on the way back from the cave, it leads to an old lava cavern.
- Rhudya: Might be a long shot, but this lava looks different. Why not give it a try?
Travel to the lava springs through the mineshaft.
- You should return to Eppo with the lava after you've completed the puzzle.
Complete the puzzle and bring the lava back to Eppo.
- Move the pieces so that they form a path from the start to the finish. There are two solutions below, but there are other solutions that also work.
- Spaces that are already taken/can't be moved are marked as "-".
Upon completing the puzzle:
- [+1 Bucket of Blazing Lava]
You can simply ride the nearby minecart at [-432, 39, -545] to get back to Eppo quickly.
Dialogue:
- Eppo: I don't understand how you can hold lava in a bucket.. But here we are.
- Eppo: Truth is.. We're not retrieving these bodies for no reason.
- Eppo: We believe one of these people worked for Theorick, and has a key to his mansion
- Eppo: We in Nesaak think Theorick has a lot to answer for. We want to redistribute his wealth among those he hurt.
- Eppo: Right, I've dipped this stick in the magical lava. Just hold the rod and walk into the ice to melt it.
- Eppo: Look for the corpse with a key, it might be above you. Good luck!
Melt the ice and find the Servant's corpse.
You can follow the packed ice, which will not be melted by the stick, to reach the Servant's corpse at [-5575, 22, -21835]. Once you do, Eppo will call you back down.
Dialogue:
- Eppo: Is that the right one? You got it? Brilliant! Now come back down.
- Now you've obtained the key, you can enter Theoricks mansion
- Eppo: Lets travel to the mansion together. Here, lets take my horse.
- Eppo: While we ride, let me explain a little more about what we're doing. Let's go.
- Eppo: As I mentioned before, there is a reason this land is frozen, and it's not natural.
- Eppo: Many years before Bob was around, Wynn was in ruins due to the corruption war.
- Eppo: In those times there used to be a group of naturally gifted individuals called the Twains. They defended us all with elemental magic.
- Eppo: Theorick was one of those Twains. He harnessed unnaturally powerful ice based magic. He used it to protect the land surrounding the mansion.
- Eppo: Theorick.. Wasn't like the other Twains. He wanted the people he protected to pay and feed him as way of thanks.
- Eppo: After years, Theorick was rich while the people he protected lived in poverty and fear - not only of the monsters, but in fear of Theorick himself.
- Eppo: He punished those who disobeyed his curfews and would get angry if anyone tried to move away. The people felt trapped.
- Eppo: Eventually, just like the other Twains - Theorick fell to the corruption. Not before he had the last word.
- Eppo: He froze the land entirely, killing almost everything and everyone left outside in it. Hundreds of lives were lost.
- Eppo: It turns out the ice slowed the spread of corruption across the land to almost a standstill. It's been this way ever since.
- Eppo: Now that we can get in his mansion we hope to uncover the secrets of his ice magic so we may undo it, and share the wealth he hoarded from the people. Ah, we're here.
Enter Theorick's Mansion.
Dialogue:
- Eppo: This place looks frozen in time.. The grandure.. Well he did just take and take from everyone around him.
- Eppo: So, I'm not sure where to start, but I'm guessing he has some protection in place.
- Eppo: This is unbelievable.. He was such a greedy- AAAAH.
Eppo will fall through a hole that opens in the floor.
- Eppo: ... I don't think we should insult him..
Find the riches in Theorick's mansion.
Walk upstairs to the library.
Eppo will get shot up from another hole that opens in the floor.
Dialogue:
- Eppo: Oof! Wasn't expecting that. That just proves everything I said about him. Punishing people who insult him.
- Eppo: Anyway, we should look around for some kind of secret entrance.
- Eppo: Trust Theorick to booby trap his own house the paranoid frozen gro-
Eppo will fall down another hole in the floor.

lines.title: How to solve the puzzle and get to Theorick's secret room
lines.text:
At [-170, 35, 577] there is a sign saying "When the young Face the old Then the key Shall be sold".
To solve the puzzle make the 4 smaller silver statues (the "young") on both sides face the middle statue between them, and make the big gold statues (the "old") face each other. This will open a hole in the middle of the room that you can jump into to progress.
Dialogue:
- Eppo: That really isn't fun at all. I can't see a thing. Where are we now, a dead end?
- Eppo: Well we know that insults result in punishment. Maybe a compliment will make him happy?
- Eppo: Oh Theorick, strongest of all the Twains, you really are a hero.
- Eppo: Maybe n-
A staircase will open to the next room.
- Eppo: Looks like we finally found his private quarters, look at that vault door.
- Eppo: There must be a way to open it. Look around and see what you can find.
Find your way into the vault.

lines.title: How to get into the vault
lines.text: Get 3 bottles of water. Then go upstairs and right click each fireplace to freeze the water streams and open the vault door mechanism. Try re-selecting your class if right-clicking does not work.
Dialogue:
- The water is freezing to ice, maybe it opens something?
- Eppo: You did it! We have access to the vault.
- Eppo: Wow, even by today's standards, this is a huge amount of money. Just think how much this was hundreds of years ago.
- Eppo: Grab a little for yourself, too, we wouldn't have been able to get here without you.
- Eppo: Wait, look at this. It seems to be a piece of Theoricks armour.
- Eppo: Surprised it even managed to fit over his fat head.
Eppo will get shot up through the ceiling as the quest finishes.
Find Zenam in the Llevigar power control center at [-1872, 55, -4593]
Dialogue:
- Zenam: Aaah, no no no! This doesn't make any sense, what in the world is going on?! Nothing's working!
- Zenam: Gweh, a visitor? Get out of here! The plant is shut down for maintenance- wait, are you the electromagic expert we're paying for?
- Zenam: You are, right? Right?! Cause we can't wait any longer! This system was supposed to be unbreakable, a flawless design!
- Zenam: We didn't even need to get Corkian consultation on this, we had this system all figured out ourselves, but now nothing's working right!
- Zenam: You're seeing all these sparks and hearing all this crackling? We have no idea what could possibly be going wrong with this! That's why you're needed here!
- Zenam: We don't have much time until full meltdown! There is an entrance to the power plant opposite the bank, go there and meet with the Head Engineer!
Enter the sewers opposite of the bank of Llevigar.
Press the button to drop all the way down into the sewers.
Find the head engineer at the Llevigar power plant
- The crackling and huming gets louder..
Dialogue:
- Head Engineer: Whew, finally Zeman found a guy for the job. I told him weeks ago this was a two-person task...
- Head Engineer: Wait, it's Zenam? Eh, what does it matter? You knew who I was talkin' about. Lemme give you the lowdown real fast.
- Head Engineer: About a month ago, there was a big blackout, and the generator here started acting up. Power surges, appliances overloading...heck, some of our lights turned purple!
- Head Engineer: My grandfather and his engineers jury-rigged the whole system. A reset should fix all this, but as a security measure, I need to be here to oversee the reset.
- Head Engineer: So that's your job- get through the system and find the reset button. These holes'll lead you around the generator rooms. Better get going!
Try to find a way into the machine

lines.title: how to get into the machine
lines.text: Right next to the Head Engineer, there is a short staircase with colored carpets on it leading to a hole in the wall. Go through the hole to get on top of the machine, then drop down to another hole with gray and blue carpets leading to it, and go through that one as well. You will be dropped into a tube; go all the way through it to reach the next section.
Find a way to proceed to the inner parts of the machinery
- You can hear a soft humming coming from the walls.

lines.title: 2=the first puzzle
lines.text:
1=
Moving block puzzle:
* Try to get an iron block to the bottom center, and a gold block on the top center.
* Make sure to get the gold block on the bottom right.
* Once you have that, try to shift the blocks around until you get the pattern.
* The colored buttons correspond to the sticky pistons on each side.
* See this [https://youtu.be/oLmJoRoeuuw?t=4m35s guide].

The steps:
# RED
# GREEN
# RED
# YELLOW
# GREEN
# YELLOW
# RED
# GREEN
# RED
# GREEN
# YELLOW
# GREEN
# YELLOW
# RED
(credit to Red-Eyed-Knight)
- A door has been opened
Reach the center of the restricted area
- You feel powerful electricity rushing through your body as you enter the room.
Tip: Look up and follow one of the colored glass lines to get to the center.
Find the reset button.

lines.title: the second puzzle
lines.text:
The Second Puzzle:
*This requires planning ahead like in the game, Flow. 
*Use the buttons on the walls to change the color of the wire
*See the picture below for the solution:
- A door has been opened
Go through the opened door and jump on the large red button.
- The system has been restarted
Report back to the Head Engineer
Dialogue:
- Head Engineer: Alright, that should do it- Ah, you're back. The system reset just fine, like I said. Everything should be winding down now.
- Head Engineer: It's purging the excess energy now- might have a few more power surges and crackles for a while, but it'll go back to normal soon enough.
- Head Engineer: Hm? What, there was a bug in the system? ...what, are you asleep or something? Of course there was a bug, we just fixed it!
- Head Engineer: Well, anyways, Zebra should have our payment all settled. You go on ahead- I still need to stay down here to make sure everything stays smooth.
- Head Engineer: ...oh, it's Zenam? D'you really care about getting his name right, or what? Anyways, the exit's through the water cooling system, it hooks up to the sewer exit.
Ask Zenam for your reward
Dialogue:
- Zenam: Whew...welcome back. The power is back online- Everything is running at full capacity again. I think the system is just running excess through right now.
- Zenam: Glad you got here when you did though- some phony came through saying he was the expert. Clearly he was just here to take your contract money...
- Zenam: Though, I was panicking so much I probably would've believed him... Speaking of which, here's your cut of the pay, and something extra for the trouble.
- Zenam: Here's to hoping that the system won't run into any more trouble in the future. I don't want to be faced with an impending cataclysm like that again...
Talk to Adigard on the Ice Islands at [806, 59, -3353]
Dialogue:
- Adigard: Welcome traveler, to our humble island...
- Adigard: My people and I landed here many years ago. Unfortunately, our ship didn't make it...
- Adigard: We tried to build a nation on these islands but became divided through the years.
- Adigard: Because of this, we are fighting a useless war with our neighbours.
- Adigard: I believe we should try to pass a peace treaty, but I am afraid of getting killed if I leave the island...
- Adigard: Would you mind helping us? Talk to Hallfred about this treaty. He lives on another ice island nearby.
Talk to Hallfred about the peace treaty
Dialogue:
- Hallfred: Welcome traveler! What brings you to our island?
- Hallfred: Oh, I see that Adigard now sends strangers through his cowardice! Worried he'll get killed?
- Hallfred: This is the last time I'll repeat it: We will sign the peace treaty the day Adigard and his nation will return to us... the treasure.
- Hallfred: The one that they kept and hid from us after the shipwreck.
- Hallfred: Pure gold, very valuable and rare! Tell him I'll be waiting for it. And none of that silly story again.
Talk back to Adigard about Hallfred's response
Dialogue:
- Adigard: I should have expected that. Hallfred was always very greedy...
- Adigard: We tried to make him understand that we do not have the treasure, without much success.
- Adigard: ... You see, the reason why we became shipwrecked wasn't natural cause. We were attacked...
- Adigard: By whom? The undead. Ghosts and demons navigating a monstrous ship. They got us by surprise.
- Adigard: I believe they also stole our treasure during the attack.
- Adigard: Would you help our nation come back together? Find this ship, and bring the treasure back to Hallfred so we can finally live in peace.
- Adigard: Sail north. That is where they attacked us many years ago. It should be easy to find, I'm sure they are anchored there in glory... Thank you.
Find the ghost ship and bring back Ancient Treasure to Hallfred
The entrance to the Captain's Room, where the treasure is being held, is at [731, 33, -3775].
Dialogue:
- Hallfred: Incredible! He actually delivered the treasure!
- Hallfred: I suppose that means the end of the war between our nations!
- Hallfred: This is a great day! Here, take this as a reward for helping our nation.
- Hallfred: I'm sure you'll find a use for this helmet one day!
Talk to Worid in the jungle village at [-760, 79, -666]
Dialogue:
- Worid: Oh, I am so happy to see you! *cough*, I caught a very bad fever, and I really need help! *cough*
- Worid: The only cure against this fever is to drink Liquid Emeralds! Yes, exactly! *cough*
- Worid: Do you think you could ask the Banker at Detlas if he could give me, oh I don't know, [64 Liquified Emeralds]?
- Worid: If he has the audacity to *cough* say no... you will have to use brute force...
- Worid: Break into *cough* to the emerald storage, but don't take anything... come back to me immediately after, if you make it out alive, heheh...
- Worid: Oh, uh... I mean *cough* *cough*
Talk to Detlas's Banker about the cure for Worid at [497, 67, -1559]
Dialogue:
- The Banker: [64 Liquified Emeralds]? He is crazy! Liquified Emeralds cannot cure anyone from anything, except being poor!
- The Banker: I will not participate in this pathetic fraud attempt!
Enter Detlas' Emerald Stash at [494, 67, -1553]
Dialogue:
- Worid: Oh no! How will I ever cure my sickness without any Liquified Emeralds?... *cough*
- Worid: We'll have to change our strategy, we won't ask for permission. It's to help me after all.
- Worid: First, I need to make sure you can easily break into a bank. Try to enter Detlas' Secret Stash.
- Worid: When you're done, talk to me again. Be careful too, they might have some Guards.
Return to Worid
Dialogue:
- Worid: What? You're here already. I thought you would take too long so I just went myself.
- Worid: My sickness? RIGHT. *cough* You should feel bad for forcing a sick man to do your job.
- Worid: Anyway I see you proved yourself, we can start the real thing now.
- Worid: You see, Almuj has a very well guarded emerald vault named "The Emerald Labyrinth".
- Worid: It is guarded with tons of well trained Guard Golem, who can easily kill any adventurer.
- Worid: The Banker in the secret vault must be completely bored out of his mind, and won't mind if you find him.
- Worid: Good luck with that. Haha.. I mean, *cough*.
Infiltrate Almuj's Secret Emerald Labyrinth at [1019, 84, -1976] underground and find the Banker in the Emerald Room

lines.title: finding the Almuj Banker
lines.text: To reach the coordinates provided, enter the Almuj Bank and go down one of the ladders leading to the emerald storage. Once you go down the stairs and enter the main labyrinth, drop any item (usually an emerald) on the pressure plate at [998, 21, -2030]. This will open the door at [1019, 21, -1991], allowing you to reach the Almuj Banker.
Dialogue:
- Almuj Banker: Oh, uh! Somebody! It has been so long since I've seen someone!
- Almuj Banker: Liquified Emeralds? Of course, of course! I've got tons! Here, take them.
Talk to Worid at [956, 75, -1960].
- It appears Worid followed you here, he seems to be near the market..
Dialogue:
- Worid: You are back! Wonderful!
- Worid: That is a lot of money, thank you very much, I will finally be able to... *cough* to cure myself!
- Worid: Here, take this part, you deserve it. I have to use most of the... *cough* money so I can heal, so I've instead paid you with a key.
- Worid: I stole- *cough* I mean, borrowed it, from our tribe's leader. Apparently it was used to lock up a great evil.
- Worid: Good ridda- *cough* Er... luck. Yes, good luck, adventurer!
Talk to Caissop the artist, in his tent at [-1802, 55, -5190]
Dialogue:
- Caissop: ...hm...mh!
- Caissop: Oh sorry, I didn't notice you. Did you want an autograph?
- Caissop: Wait, no? Don't you know who I am?! It seems like you have no taste in art... I am Caissop, the legendary artist!
- Caissop: Though, since you are not a fan... Perhaps you can help me? I am looking for a new assistant.
- Caissop: Excellent... I need your help to find three legendary creatures that are hiding in caves around the swamp.
- Caissop: I actually know their location, but unfortunately, I am...blind.
- Caissop: For me to do my work I need to imagine them! That's where you come in. I need you to find them and describe them to me!
- Caissop: Would you turn your back on a blind man?! I need you to give me an accurate description of them! Once you have found one, come back and describe it to me exactly!
- Caissop: The first cave is up a hill with tall, thin-leafed flowers. They smell pink to me, and of this I am certain.
Search for the first mythical creature in the cave at [-1833, 69, -5144]
Dialogue:
- This is...just a normal cow. This is supposed to be legendary?
- ...Caissop seemed to be looking forward to this painting a lot...
- ...well, if he's blind, maybe you can fudge the details a bit to give him something better.
- It's brown all over...
- It has a large snout...
- That sounds like a villager to you.
- Time to head back to Caissop. Hopefully he'll buy it.
Report back with the description of the brown, large-snouted creature to Caissop
Dialogue:
- Caissop: Quick! Describe it to me! Go on!
- Caissop: Brown...big-nosed... A Villager Cow, you say!?
- Caissop: ...OH, YES! ......... INSPIRED.
- Caissop: ...MH, NO, A LITTLE MORE RED!..... YES!
- Caissop: Haha! This is WONDERFUL! I'm not going to show it to you before it is finished!
- Caissop: Savor the ideas! So now, I need you to go to the second cave...
- Caissop: It is down a road, with short, round-cupped flowers. Those ones smell orange to me!
- Caissop: Hurry! I'll finish this animal while you are gone. OH, YES. MUY MACHO.
Search for the second mythical beast in the cave at [-1761,55,-5112]

lines.title: finding the second mythical beast
lines.text: In this cave, simply follow the path down at the entrance. You will reach an area containing a large open underground pond, which you can either parkour over or simply swim through. Once across, climb up the stairs and go through the passage out the back of the open room to find the mythical beast of this cave.
Dialogue:
- This is just a normal sheep! Are none of these supposed creatures really legendary?
- You'll need to lie about something to make a mundane sheep seem special...
- It has large horns- no, say it's just one.
- Clean white wool, instead of black...
- A pure white sheep with one horn...?
- Time to head back to Caissop. Hopefully that's good enough for him.
Report back with the description of the white, big-horned creature to Caissop
Dialogue:
- Caissop: You're here! Quick! Don't look at me, describe it!
- Caissop: Snow white, a large horn... A Unicorn Sheep, you say?!
- Caissop: ...OH YES, THE WOOL IS REAL... MORE SWIPING... OH YES, BIEN!
- Caissop: ... THIS IS UNIQUE, REMARKABLE, YES. SUPERNATURAL!
- Caissop: The last creature! Red-smelling flowers, prickly thorns, hurry, mucho inspired!
- Caissop: ... OH, NO, NO. YES! MORE COLOUR, MORE PAINT! I'M OUT OF RED!
- Caissop: I'LL JUST USE MY BLOOD! OH! YES! ...INSPIRED! REMARKABLE! Huh? Why are you still here? Go! I need that last description!
Search for the third and last mythical animal in the cave at [-1763,54,-5167]

lines.title: finding the third mythical animal
lines.text: Follow the path down into the cave, until you reach a room covered by a fence. You must kill the alligator leader in order to break through the fence, which will reveal the room containing the third animal.
Dialogue:
- The creatures guarding these animals seem more legendary to you.
- No way you can describe a pig fantastically. You'll have to outright make something up...
- Pink is fine, it's a rare color...
- ...what if you say it has wings?
- Will he believe a flying pig?
- Time to head back to Caissop. Hopefully he won't be able to tell something's amiss.
Report back with the description of the pink, flying creature to Caissop
Dialogue:
- Caissop: You're finally back! I just finished the last one. Go! Describe it!
- Caissop: ...Oh, yes... YES. I LOVE IT.
- Caissop: It's...A Pigasus! WHAT A NAME!
- Caissop: ...OH YES, WINGS! EYES FROM HEAVEN! OH, YES.
- Caissop: Och, Perfect. The final touch and, done! You were so inspiring that I made two! One for you, and one for me!
- Caissop: You might want to hold onto that, big-town upper class Villagers pay through the roof for Caissop's work!
- Caissop: Thank you for your assistance, what a rush! Good luck on your Gavel adventure!
Talk to Damiral, outside Llevigar at [-1937, 38, -4260]
Dialogue:
- Damiral: Lo, adventurer! Welcome to the great province of Gavel, home of the villager race, and yours truly. You'll be headed into the grand citadel of Llevigar soon!
- Damiral: But enough with the pleasantries. Tell me... have you ever heard the tale of the great pirate, Captain Hastor? Sailed the seas a long time ago.
- Damiral: Legend says that when Llevigar was rebuilt all those years ago, he hid his fortune within the walls someplace!
- Damiral: I'm a retired sailor now, but I could still do with a few extra emeralds from that treasure. Perhaps, if you're up to it... we could come to an agreement?
- Damiral: I have a riddle, the first of a number of clues that are supposed to lead to where Hastor hid his fortune, but I can't for the life of me figure it out.
- Damiral: Maybe you'll be able to solve it. If you can, I'll make sure to split the treasure with you!
- Damiral: This first riddle goes like so: “Toward the sunset, among the northern flowers shaded by quartz”.
- Damiral: I do wish you good luck, adventurer! Remember, everything you need to solve the clues should be found somewhere inside Llevigar.
Clue I: Toward the sunset, among northern flowers shaded by quartz

lines.title: 2=the First Clue
lines.text:
1=
First Clue 
*Toward the sunset: this means west because that's where the sun sets. 
*Among the northern flowers shaded by quartz: this could only mean the northern gardens.
Combining these two directions, you get the north-western garden-bed.
Right-click the pedestal at [-2073, 35, -4607] to get the next dialogue:
*A message is carved into the pedestal: In a place of identity, above the leaves and between the glass
Clue II: In a place of identity, above the leaves and between the glass

lines.title: 2=the Second Clue
lines.text:
1=
Second Clue 
*In a place of identity: this signifies the identifier's house.
* Above the leaves and between the glass: the identifier's place has a tree, so the stone is above the tree but under the glass. 
When you enter the identifier's house take a left. Attempt to climb the tree seen when you turn left, climb the stairs in the southeast corner of the building, or follow the green carpets.
Right-clicking the pedestal at [-1905, 103, -4502] will trigger the next hint:
*A message is carved into the obsidian: In an emerald fountain, surrounded by the wealth of the villagers
Clue III: In an emerald fountain, surrounded by the wealth of the villagers

lines.title: 2=the Third Clue
lines.text:
1=
Third Clue 
*In an emerald fountain, surrounded by the wealth of the villagers: this clue's pedestal is found on top of the fountain in the plaza outside the Llevigar bank, above the door to Gavel.
Right-clicking the pedestal at [-1997, 90, -4470] will trigger the following dialogue:
*A message is carved into the obsidian: Beneath the cowl of an eastern titan, keeping watch over our heads
Clue IV: Beneath the cowl of an eastern titan, keeping watch over our heads

lines.title: the Fourth Clue
lines.text:
Fourth Clue 
*Beneath the cowl of an eastern titan: there are two big stone villagers who sit by the gate, holding weapons. There is something beneath the eastern titan's 'headwear', so climb onto the eastern titan, and into its western eye.
Entering the treasure room at [-1972, 71, -4538] will trigger a short cutscene with the dialogue below.
Dialogue:
- [+100000 Emeralds]
- Damiral: Aha! I'd come to ask how it was coming when I saw you jump over here!
- Damiral: Phenomenal work, my compatriot. Though, do remember our deal?
- Damiral: You find the treasure, I give you a cut. I'll just take my part and be on my way!
- [-99850 Emeralds]
Join Elphaba on a mission in the Temporary Camp at [-1499, 47, -5349]
Dialogue:
- Elphaba: Oh, a Wynnic soldier out here in the boondocks? Honestly, you're just what we need- I could use your help, if you're able?
- Elphaba: Good, thank you. Let me lock down the camp before I give you the briefing, though.
- Elphaba: My name is Elphaba. I've been working with the Gavellian army for a good few years now.
- Elphaba: I'm the commander of the Olux Outpost down ahead. It's a strategic fortress, placed to monitor the Orcish capital.
- Elphaba: It was safe for a long while, but especially in the past while the Orcs have gotten far bolder, more aggressive.
- Elphaba: They overwhelmed the outpost- we had to retreat and set up this camp to watch over the place we used to watch over them with!
- Elphaba: I need more firepower if I'm going... to get...
- Elphaba: ...oh no. See, this is what I mean! The orcs are coming!
- Elphaba: Brace yourself, soldier! Protect the camp!
Kill the mobs raiding the Camp.
Dialogue:
- Elphaba: This is the third attack in three days! How many reinforcements have they got?!
- Elphaba: Gah! Their casters are strong, careful!
Talk to Elphaba for information on the upcoming attack.
Dialogue:
- Elphaba: Ugh, I think that was all of them... Come here now, I'll start up where we left off.
- Elphaba: Not sure I could have done that myself. I'm lucky you came around when you did, soldier.
- Elphaba: Anyway, it's clear I'm going to need more firepower if I'm going to have a shot at reclaiming that outpost.
- Elphaba: You've certainly got the fighting chops, so I'd appreciate the aid, but we've got to come up with a plan, fast.
- Elphaba: There's an old tower near the outpost- some old storage silo. It was built taller than the fort, so we might be able to spy on them from there.
- Elphaba: It's a risk though, since it's so close by, but we have no other options. Meet me at the tower southeast of here so we can survey the situation.
Go to the watch tower at [-1384, 42, -5273] to plan the attack.
Dialogue:
- Elphaba: Soldier! I'm right behind you. You can see our outpost- and the tower I mentioned.
- Elphaba: We need to find a way in. A lot of soldiers were caught unaware during the Orcs' assault, too.
- Elphaba: If there's any survivors in there, we should make rescuing them a priority.
- Elphaba: After all, it means more manpower for us. We can't count on that being the case, though...
- Elphaba: Come on, hurry inside before one of the orcs spots us!
Enter to the watch tower at [-1384, 42, -5273] to plan the attack.
Dialogue:
- Elphaba: Alright, this is a pretty clear view. Let's see what's going on in there...
- Elphaba: Wh- I'm shocked! In the middle there- they just caged the soldiers instead of killing them? That's... kind of a relief.
- Elphaba: There's definitely too many orcs in the plaza for us to take down on our own...
- Elphaba: ...but that cage is held up by those ropes. If we can cut them, the other soldiers should be able to help!
- Elphaba: Alright, now I just need to figure out how we can both get in... There's sentries on the perimeter, so going over may no be an option...
- Elphaba: Maybe we can keep an eye out on their sentry patterns and look for an opening-
- Orc: Humans on old tower! Junhur will shoot! This our place now, get out!!
- Elphaba: Aw, not now! I knew this was a risk, no time to get out... Brace for impact!!
- Orc: Old tower fall! Junhur is best cannon shooter!!
- Elphaba: Agh, soldier!! Are you alright, where'd you fall?!
- Elphaba: Ah... Wow. You barely look scratched, you must've gotten really lucky.
- Elphaba: Not so much here... I'm pretty battered after that. At least one of us is in good condition...
- Elphaba: Unfortunately, that means figuring a way in is up to you. We can't examine their sentry patterns from down here.
- Elphaba: I'll survive, sure, but I won't be able to walk around and defend myself for a while.
- Elphaba: I hate leaving you on your own like this, but if it's any consolation, you should be tough enough, or lucky enough, to get through.
- Elphaba: Explore the perimeter of the outpost. Try to find a way in, but be careful, okay?
Explore the outpost's surroundings to find another way in.

lines.title: finding a way in
lines.text: Go to [-1411, 45, -5168] and watch the muddied orc be let in.
Follow the trail of mud left by the orc. It leads to the cave at [-1522, 47, -5152]
Dialogue:
- Without the orcs to bother you, you should be able to concentrate and break this barricade with a spell...
- The orcs are taking a mud bath, it looks like. Some of them you can barely even tell are orcs underneath it. Maybe you can disguise yourself!
- They didn't see you before you covered yourself in mud... and they aren't hostile! The disguise is working!
- You should be able to trick the guard orcs into letting you enter the outpost now!
Enter the outpost while covered in mud.
Dialogue:
- Orc Guard: More muddy orcs? In, now!
Cut the ropes to free the guards from the cage.
You can avoid being seen by looking out for the exclamation marks above the orc's heads. Only press when there are no exclamation marks available
Dialogue:
- You can't let the orcs see you cutting the ropes, or they'll see through your disguise.
Kill the Orcish Overtakers.
Dialogue:
- Soldier: Good thinking with the mud disguise, soldier! They never suspected a thing, now come help us out over here!
- Soldier: Kill the Orcish Overtakers, we'll help keep the other ones off you!
Open the gate with a spell
Dialogue:
- Soldier: The Overtakers are down, the other Orcs are flailing! Open the outpost's entrance with a spell now, we've got this under control!
Talk to Elphaba.
Dialogue:
- Elphaba: Phew... That's some fine work there, soldier! The outpost is back under our control!
- Elphaba: Glad to see some more capable Wynnic hands over here. Though, I didn't catch your name. Would you mind?
- Elphaba: , huh? I'll remember that. You barely even needed my help, heh... Wish I hadn't been such a burden, but at least it worked out.
- Elphaba: Here- it's some of my own personal spending money, as a thank-you gift.
- Elphaba: Alright everyone, let's get this place ship-shape! Everything needs to be repaired in case of another attack!!
Talk with Marston in the ocean at [-570 40 -3543]
- Marston: Ah, ahoy matey! Are ye here to get a glimpse of ol' Redbeard's sunken galleon as well?
- Marston: A fine ship it once was, aye? Accordin' to the stories, it sank in one o' the greatest sea battles in history! The cap'n sank beneath the waves, ne'er to be seen again!
- Marston: ...Say. Have ye ever wanted to go on a real treasure hunt? Ye look like someone with an eye for treasure, aye?
- Marston: Good for ye then! I bought meself a real treasure map on Pirate Cove, a fine deal if ye ask me. And, if the jack wasn't fibbing, it leads to the feared Redbeard's real treasure!
- Marston: I ventured 'round, spied some fine jacks at the island, and I collected a crew to join me on me grand, fantastic voyage!
- Marston: O' course, there always be room for another! Ye joinin'? We could use another hand.
- Marston: Aye! Let's find the booty and bring back some doubloons! Here be that map I snagged. Swim or whatever you landlubbers do to
Find Marston's crew on Pirate Cove at [-659, 43, -3154]
- Martim: And that be when ye will...
- Karkun: Cor lad...ye don' look like a pirate ta me, and I be but a young lass!
- Martim: 's right, bucko. Who be ye, bargin' into our home in yer fancy armour 'n whatnot?
- Argus: Ah, ye be accompanyin' Marston, eh? Well if ye insist on that, where be the man 'himself?
- Karkun: Comin' later? Hm. Well, more hands always be helpful. Let us go down to me ship, the Black Ring.
- Martim: So he told ye about the plan? We'll bathe in doubloons when we get back! Ah, me fair lass will be so happy.
Hop aboard the Black Ring down at the dock of Pirate Cove.
Find the treasure.
- Karkun: Aha, quick on yer feet, lad! Ye got 'ere before us!
- Argus: No trace o' Marston yet?
- Martim: How's about we wait up fer him? He's the one who's givin us the opportunity fer this hunt, anyways.
- Argus: I be getting impatient... The whole crew is 'ere, 'cept fer him!
- Karkun: Argh! Where be our mate? It be getting dark out! We will have to leave Marston at land.
- Karkun: Do ya have the map Marston bought?
- Martim: Let us take a looksie at the map and see where to go.
- Argus: It seems like one of these islands have the treasure... A'ight, yer in charge, landlubber! Set us on a course fer an island!
In order to find the treasure you have to go to all three islands and get a map piece from each one.
Looking towards the islands from your starting point in the ocean, there are three islands. One is to the left, one in the middle, and one is to the right.

lines.title: the left island
lines.text: On the left island, which you can enter at [8705, 11, 6886], you have to climb to the top of the mountain, avoiding a rockfall and doing a bit of parkour part of the way up. At the very top, at [-7866, 131, -3488], there is a red "X" with a button in the middle; press the button to get the map piece.

lines.title: the middle island
lines.text:
On the middle island, which you can enter at [8742, 12, 6920], you will be taken to the water next to the island. Do not attempt to climb it, you get the map piece from the watery cave near where you spawn. you have to press buttons to get the map piece. Press the buttons 2, 5, and 6 to solve the riddle. This will open a door that takes you to a small room with a red "X" and a button in the middle; press the button to get the map piece.

:

lines.title: the right island
lines.text: On the right island, which you can enter at [8703, 11, 6939], you have to fight multiple waves of mobs. In the first wave, a swarm of mobs will spawn, which occasionally drop Magical Thunder Shards when you kill them. You can use two Shards to spawn each of three minibosses underneath the crystals around the arena. Once you have killed all three, put all of their drops into the hopper that will appear at [-7916, 64, -3806]. This will give you the map piece.
Once you have all three map pieces, the following dialogue will play:
- All 3 map pieces seem to fit together...
- The 3 pieces form a map of an island...
- [+1 Treasure Map]
- It looks like the island with the crystals. Maybe there is a way to the tallest part of the island on the side?

lines.title: getting the treasure
lines.text: After getting the new treasure map, you have to enter the right-side island, the one on which you fought the mobs. When you are teleported to it, turn to the left and follow the path to the top of the island shown on the new map. You will reach a portal-like structure at [-7918, 112, -3756], enter it to be taken to the final island.
- Karkun: Ahoy, this must be the booty. Fret not, Argus is keepin' the ship prepared so we can leave.
- Martim: A'ight, let's us dig it up, jacks!
Martim will start digging at the red "X" on the island.
- Karkun: Aha, I see somethin' gleaming in there! Methinks we hit gold, lads.
- Karkun: Now Martim, knock the lubber out.
- You are not able to move but you still hear the ongoing conversation.
- Karkun: What? Another clue! The be just a wild grook hunt, where be the real booty?! No one ever got rich off a heap o' keys!! Maybe this 'ere jewel attached will sell...
- Martim: Wait, there be a clue on the key! Presented to the ruined Galleon, a true path forward will arise.
- Martim: Garh...I be losin' my patience. Argus arrived, let's ditch the lubber before they awake, hm? This island be hidden by magic, ain't no way they're gettin' found.
- Karkun: Arright! This key... We might be able to bring Redbeard 'imself back to life... He'll strike terror in the seas again, and we will be 'is crew!
Leave the hidden island and stop the pirates from stealing Redbeard's Booty.
- It seems your crew's long gone. You'd better figure out a way off the island, and follow them to the Galleon's Graveyard.
Head over to the boat at [25, 38, -15260].
- Maybe you can fix this boat and get off the island?

lines.title: leaving the island
lines.text:
You have to fix the boat with 4 Wood Planks and 3 Strings.
The strings are located in a cave.

The planks can be found underneath a tree on the island.
Talk to Marston about his crew at [-570, 43, -3543].
- Marston: Can't say I expected all that... Those dogs are quick, eh?
- Marston: Fer a landlubber, ye sure are quick. When I got ta Pirate Cove, ye were already but a speck on the horizon.
- Marston: Speakin' of, what'n the name o' Davy Jones' Locket happened out there?!
- Marston: Ye look a bit bruised! Reckon ye ran aground o' trouble with 'em too, eh?
- Marston: Well, lad! Methinks ye oughta go in after 'em! We may be a rowdy lot, but a mutiny's somethin' ye don't tolerate.
- Marston: They don't deserve that treasure, lad! It ain't be mine either, since I missed ye. That gold be yours fer the takin...so take it!
- Marston: Speakin' of...I ain't got much a penny ta my name, but I found this fish while ye were gone. I hear it sells for a decent haul, so here.
Talk to Nasea in the Karoc Quarry.
Dialogue:
- Nasea: Shipment 3A and 4B, fully accounted for... shipments 5C and 6A...missing 50% of quartz content?!
- Nasea: Agh, this is getting worse! There's never been so much loss...whoever this is, thy're getting bold...
- Nasea: Ugh, go AWAY! Quit hovering over my shoulder like that- wait, a Human? Since when did you get here?
- Nasea: What, you like listening to the melodious sound of my voice or something? Or do you intend to help out?
- Nasea: Well, I'm flattered either way, and I could certainly use the help. Quartz is going missing from my shipments.
- Nasea: Obviously one of the laborers is siphoning it to someplace, and I can't have that happening. So, be a private eye, humie.
- Nasea: This is actually pretty dire- quartz has some magicality to it, see. It likes to soak up magic power, which means it can be weaponized.
- Nasea: We tend not to use it for weapons since it can overcharge, but that's neither here nor there, is it?
- Nasea: Every siphoned shipment has gone through Dado. Interrogate him! He hangs out past the big red tent, near the house with red flags.
Talk to Dado and see if he is the culprit.
Dialogue:
- Dado: Okay, these go to division P, and...look, I'm busy allocating these deliveries to Llevigar. Go pester someone else, okay?
- Dado: ...what. You...think I... Pfff... Pffhahaaaah! Ohhh, that's RICH coming from a human of all things!
- Dado: "Oh, me, the hired gun species that kills for money, will accuse you, a storied worker of seven years, of illegal activity!" Wow, you HYPOCRITE!
- Dado: I'm hardly even angry about this! But, yeah, you freak. You got the wrong guy, surprise! Your brain workin' right in there?
- Dado: I bet you got some wires crossed in there, huh? Go scuttle on back to town and kill someone's Wybel for pocket change or something.
- Dado won't budge about the topic. Maybe Nasea has an idea to get him to confess.
Go back to Nasea and tell her about Dado’s response.
Dialogue:
- Nasea: I'm just going to take a wild guess and say that asking him nicely whether he committed theft didn't bring up any answers.
- Nasea: What, he brushed you off like THAT? Jeez, I knew he was a jerk, but really? That's just uncalled for.
- Nasea: We have to make him talk...if shipments keep going missing, my contractors are going to look elsewhere!
- Nasea: We need to prove that he's guilty...wait, you came to ME for ideas? This is why I asked you for help! Am I really back to square one?
- ???: Aah, Nasea!
- Nasea: I...what are you doing here, uh...Larry? Were you missing quartz too??
- Lari: Ah, it's...Lari. No, the quartz shipment found its way fine...
- Lari: But, there was hardly an effect. Your idea was, unfortunately, a dead end.
- Nasea: Well, I did warn you that it was only an idea. I manage the mine, I don't practice purification magic. Don't pin anything on me for that.
- Lari: I did not intend to imply that. Your help was appreciated, fate simply had opposing plans...
- Lari: ...is this human a part of your operations, miss?
- Nasea: Well, in a sense. Someone's siphoning quartz, but our suspect wasn't intimidated by the ten tons of armor, so we're at a loss. Any ideas?
- Lari: ...as a matter of fact, I do have a solution. Elven botany describes a flower that grows decently close by, the "Tattytale" flower.
- Lari: It weakens the will of those who catch a whiff of its petals, making them pliable to questions. It's...unpleasant, but if it is needed, I suppose.
- Lari: There is a cave infested with spiders, and covered with webs in the western mountain. It is the only place it grows outside of Aldorei, unfortunately.
- Lari: Nasea, since it didn't help, I've returned the quartz. I thank you for your help...and I shall bid you both adieu.
Find the Tattytale Flower.
Dialogue:
- You should head back to Dado with the flower.
Make Dado confess by using the Tattytale Flower.
Dialogue:
- Dado: Hey, everyone's least-favorite attack dog! Here boy! You want the emerald? Go kill all the flies in my house! Come on boy!
- Dado: Aw, flowers. How sweet of you! Sorry, but I don't cave to psychopaths or flattery, hehehee!
- You press the flower up against his nose while he's laughing. Dado gets a big whiff of the petals, and immediately his expression goes slack.
- Dado: I...huff... What was THAT for?! Are you offended that I don't like your flo- What? What am I doing with the quartz?
- Dado: Uh, isn't it obvious? I'm working overtime and sending it up to Popo, duh. Where else would I be sending it?
