- A festival attendee claims that they saw a group from the Kalkalrah clan with bottles of fuel bring it to the . They were paid to stay silent about what they saw.
- There is a group from Kalkalrah clan hanging out on the second floor of Aldwell, but they claim to only be hanging out.

- An old woman claims to have seen the group of Kalkalrah clan members throw a bottle of gas down  but only after the fire had already started. She thinks they're acting as security for the festival. Maybe you could ask  if that's true?

lines.title: Final Investigation Part
lines.text:
Talk to the Festival Organizer to confirm what the Elderly Woman said.



* Festival Organizer: You look like you have something on your mind, what is it?
* Ask your question.
** 
* Player: Is there hidden security at this festival?
* Festival Organizer: Ah, I see your investigations have borne fruit.
* Festival Organizer: Yes. As you have seen, people tend to let their guard down at the festival in a way they normally wouldn't.
* Festival Organizer: They are a necessity to ensure any unexpected guests are swiftly taken care of.
* Ask your question.
** 
* Player: They caused the small fire that almost burnt down the wickerman!
* Festival Organizer: I suspect you're probably right. And yet, that is irrelevant.
* Festival Organizer: You will tell me they are reckless and a danger to others. I don't disagree, but I encourage you to look at the wider picture.
* Festival Organizer: If we let up our vigilance for even a moment, we have already lost our war. Our clans and families will be infiltrated within the day.
* Festival Organizer: Their recklessness prevents this. In a case where the smallest failure would be a catastrophe, recklessness becomes necessity.
* Festival Organizer: Imagine they had not acted rashly in throwing the bottle of fuel onto the already lit flame.
* Festival Organizer: They did not create the flame, someone else must have been hoping to gain from it.
* Festival Organizer: Their actions, while dangerous, prevented any fiends from exploiting the opportunity. We took it out of their control.
* Festival Organizer: Whatever risk their actions created was worth the price.
* Festival Organizer: Apologies for rambling, I assure you though that safety is our top concern. Whatever the price.
* You've updated your notes with this new information.

After speaking with the Festival Organizer, the stage will update to stage 8, although it will not mention looking into the suspects more.
- You found a broken bottle in the embers where someone attempted to burn the wickerman. Maybe  will recognize it.
- The festival's food merchant informed you that the bottle , something not to be sold by any stalls. He advised you to  to see if anyone knows anything.
- A festival attendee claims that they saw a group from the Kalkalrah clan with bottles of fuel bring it to the . They were paid to stay silent about what they saw.
- There is a group from Kalkalrah clan hanging out on the second floor of Aldwell, but they claim to only be hanging out.

- An old woman claims to have seen the group of Kalkalrah clan members throw a bottle of gas down  but only after the fire had already started. She thinks they're acting as security for the festival. Maybe you could ask  if that's true?
- The festival organizer has confirmed to you that the group of Kalkalrah clan members on the second floor of Aldwell is acting as  for the festival.
Return to the festival organizer at [-1278, 50, -713] or look into the suspects a bit more.
After getting all three confessions from the suspects, the following message will play:
- You have enough confessions that the festival organizer should be happy now. You can  or .
Talking to the Festival Organizer:
- Festival Organizer: You think you know who the changeling is?
- Yes
- Festival Organizer: You've dug into them all and have found something? Excellent.
- Festival Organizer: So, who do you think tried to burn down the wickerman?
- Arris
- Festival Organizer: Suspect 1? Very well. I will take care of things from here.
- Festival Organizer: Again, thank you so much for your help. I cannot emphasize enough how much you assisting in this matter for us allowed the festival to be a success.
- Festival Organizer: Enjoy the rest of the festival, and make sure to watch the wickerman burn! I'll save a special seat for you near the front as a sign of our appreciation.
- Burick
- Festival Organizer: Suspect 2? Very well. I will take care of things from here.
- Festival Organizer: Again, thank you so much for your help. I cannot emphasize enough how much you assisting in this matter for us allowed the festival to be a success.
- Festival Organizer: Enjoy the rest of the festival, and make sure to watch the wickerman burn! I'll save a special seat for you near the front as a sign of our appreciation.
- Cerisa
- Festival Organizer: Suspect 3? Very well. I will take care of things from here.
- Festival Organizer: Again, thank you so much for your help. I cannot emphasize enough how much you assisting in this matter for us allowed the festival to be a success.
- Festival Organizer: Enjoy the rest of the festival, and make sure to watch the wickerman burn! I'll save a special seat for you near the front as a sign of our appreciation.
- None of them.
- Festival Organizer: I understand your reticense to pick one. We don't have anything close to the information required to make a proper judgement.
- Festival Organizer: But you cannot allow that to stop you. We do not have the luxury to close our eyes and pretend it didn't happen.
- Festival Organizer: Please, from the inevitably incomplete investigation you conducted, tell me who you think lit that flame.
- Really, nobody
- Player: Really, I don't think any of them did it.
- Festival Organizer: Very well then. I am disappointed, but understand.
- Festival Organizer: I will take care of things from this point forward.
- Festival Organizer: In thanks for saving the wickerman, there will be a seat saved for you when you are ready to watch it burn.
- Festival Organizer: Enjoy the rest of the festival.
- No
- Festival Organizer: Keep looking then. Return here once you've made a decision.
Watch the wickerman burn at [-1256, 49, -707].
This is the last chance to participate in and of the festival activities. See Stage 4 for the full list of interactions.
Interacting with the seat:
- Do you want to watch the wickerman burn and end the festival?
- Yes (Begins the wickerman burning cutscene.)
- No
Watch the wickerman burn.
A cutscene will play with the Festival Organizer burning the wickerman.
- Festival Organizer: You children of the Mistwoods gather round
- Festival Organizer: To gaze upon this relic from years past,
- Festival Organizer: This effigy, of ancient foes we fought—
- Festival Organizer: In memory, we will again ignite!
- Festival Organizer: An ancient beast, rebuilt with plant and straw,
- Festival Organizer: What once was flesh, reconstitute as wood;
- Festival Organizer: All monsters, old and new, must meet their end—
- Festival Organizer: All fiends must burn! Must broil and char and melt!
- Festival Organizer: Substance beside, all that remains persists...
The camera zooms in to the accused changeling. If no suspects were accused, then all of them burn inside the wickerman.
- Festival Organizer: ...as blackened corpse, no threat there can exist!
Attend the meeting to prepare for the plan in the Steel Feather at [-2087, 6, -697].
The fast travel to the Steel Feather hideout is found at [-1801, 28, -520].
Upon reaching the destination:
- Quill: Hello, everyone. Let us begin.
- Quill: I trust everyone has taken the time to process last night's announcement? I will let Syndra take over shortly, but first, I would like to thank each and every one of you.
- Quill: I won't mince words. This is dangerous work. What we are planning puts us at great risk. But this is what it takes to change Fruma, to put an end to the crown's oppression!
- Quill: We will kill a God! And we will all be free. Now, Syndra?
Syndra gets onto the table.
- Syndra: Thank you, Quill. To begin, allow me to give each group their assignment.
- Syndra: Mora and Yuman, you will be infiltrating the guards' outpost in Timasca to retrieve their schedules. Get in, note down the formations, and get out.
- Syndra: Mora, you're familiar with military structure, and Yuman knows his way around Timasca. I expect you two should be able to make it work.
- Yuman: Yes, ma'am!
- Mora: Understood. However, I have a few concerns with the overall plans... I'll speak with you later.
- Syndra: Yusanu and Sui, you'll be constructing explosives that we can use as distractions during the festival to draw guards away from the main stage.
- Syndra: I trust Yusanu knows what he's doing, so Sui, you'll be acting as an assistant.
- Sui: Um... sure.
- Yusanu: Works for me. I might already have some blueprints lying around somewhere...
- Syndra: Zeph and Rex, I want you to scout the city rooftops for potential spots where Rex and Yulie can provide aerial support... in case it's necessary.
- Zeph: Yeah, I c- c- can do that.
- Rex: Copy that.
- Syndra: Quill and Yulie, you two know your way around the city. I'll need you to scout out potential escape routes from the city... again, in case things go badly.
- Quill: Ah, that should be a breeze.
- Yulie: ...yes. I think I have a few places in mind already.
- Syndra: Finally. Player, I want you to be adaptable. Help out wherever it's needed - I'm sure your skills will come in handy.
- Yuman: Hey, if you're helping out wherever, you should come with me and Mora! Guard positions would be handy to know before finding escape routes.
- Syndra: I was about to suggest the same thing. Then let us adjourn this meeting. Good luck, everyone.
- Mora: Hum. Player and Yuman, let us go  our plans then.
Mora and Yuman leave the meeting room.
Meet up with Mora and Yuman at [-2100, 6, -695].
Talking to Mora and Yuman:
- Yuman: Alright, guys! So, any plans? What're we cooking with here?
- Mora: Hm... I am... unsure.
- Yuman: Hey, man, everything good? I'm uh, not that horrible to work with, am I? Haha.
- Mora: Ah! My apologies. No, it is not you... I simply do not like Syndra's plan.
- Mora: You must understand, I would trust her with my life... but that is precisely the issue. She will do anything to avoid putting us in danger.

- Mora: She treats us as her own children, but she is only a decade older than I am! She would put herself through all the suffering in the world, if only to avoid letting us help where it is most needed!
- Mora: She is willing to take the fall if the plan goes awry. But, this time... this time, I will not back off. I am not allowing her to put herself through that danger alone.
- Yuman: Yeesh. Didn't think you guys were that messy! I think I get it though.
- Yuman: My bros... they mean well, yeah, but they never ask for help. They're always trying to do everything themselves, and... and it drives me nuts!
- Yuman: Like, man, just let me do something!! Anything!! It's so frustrating.
- Mora: Ha! I did not think we had this in common. Well then... perhaps we can both prove ourselves to our families, eh?
- Yuman: Yeah!! I like the sound of that!!
- Yuman: Okay, well, I know where the guards' outpost is in Timasca. Let's just go to it and take it from there!
- Mora: Ha, settle down a little. I think we need to be a bit more prepared than that. But, yes, time is of the essence, so let us head there first. I will attempt to think of a plan on the way.
- Yuman: Whatever, man! Too much planning often spoils the results... but, sure! Let's meet  in Timasca. First tunnel to the right leads there!
Meet up with Yuman and Mora in Timasca at [-1787, 41, -630].
Talking to Yuman and Mora in the hideout again:
- Yuman: Meet y'all there, then!
Talking to Yuman and Mora:
- Mora: Good grief, this town's a mess. How does anyone live here?
- Yuman: Eh, ya get used to it. Here, .
Yuman and Mora walk over to a staircase at [-1774, 40, -637].
- Yuman: See, Timasca utilizes all the space it has... stacking things atop each other. For example, this so-called "skyscraper" is mainly an apartment building!
- Mora: Then... what exactly are we doing here?
- Yuman: I said mainly, man. The top floors serve as the offices for the local commander and constables. That's also why we've got to climb this staircase!
- Yuman: Hope you guys are in shape!
Yuman starts to walk up the staircase before Mora stops him.
- Mora: Stop! Where are you going?!
- Yuman: Uh... we're on a mission, right? Trying to prove ourselves? Schedules are up there, so...
- Mora: We cannot just... walk in there and grab the schedules! You do realize that, right? Player and I are wanted by the crown! Even showing ourselves here at all is a risk.
- Yuman: Hey man, these soldiers see hundreds of people every day! If you don't give 'em a reason to pay attention, your faces won't stick out at all.
- Mora: Yuman, we were going to make a plan before rushing in. Did you forget about that?
- Yuman: Riiight. Right. Sorry, I got excited. I am right though - it wouldn't be hard for me to just talk us through this!
- Mora: Sigh... here, I have a better plan. Let us take some guard uniforms and put them on, and reach the schedules that way. We'll stand out even less, then.
- Yuman: Ohh. A sneak mission! That's good. They should definitely have some spare uniforms in the tower... *and*, it should be pretty empty this time of day. Everyone's out patrolling.
- Yuman: So, good plan, man! I like it! Let's get to it!
''Yuman and Mora walk up the staircase to [-1774, 65, -633].
Find guard uniforms inside of the guard tower at [-1773, 65, -634].
Upon reaching the destination:
- Yuman: See? I told you, nobody's here!
- Mora: Ha. I suppose I should have faith in your knowledge. My apologies.
''Yuman and Mora walk into the building and into a storage room at [-1772, 65, -624].
- Mora: ...ah, is that really all? I thought they would be harder to find.
- Yuman: With how many guards have to come through here every day for uniform exchanges, this is just the easiest way. More efficient having it out here.
Yuman looks around the room.
- Yuman: Well, time to get changed!
Yuman searches through one of the closets.
- Yuman: Let's see...
- Mora: Oh, you are just going for it... I see. Player, let's wait outside until he's done.
Follow Mora outside the storage room to [-1768, 65, -629].
Shortly after the player and Mora leave the storage room, Yuman comes out wearing a guard uniform.
- Yuman: Well? Thoughts? How do I look?
- Mora: Like an average Roughworks soldier, I suppose.
- Yuman: Wonder what Zeph would think...
- Mora: Hm? What was that?
- Yuman: Ah- haha, uh, n- nothin! Your turn!
Mora goes into the storage room, gets changed, and walks back out.
- Mora: This uniform is so... uncomfortable. And to think, I nearly signed up for this...
- Yuman: Yeah, you'd think they'd complain about it more! But nah, they're all... stoic.
- Mora: Yes... well, Player, it's . Hurry, please. Someone could come up here at any time.
Right-click the closet at [-1769, 65, -624] to get the guard uniform.
The camera fades to black briefly.
Find guard schedules inside the guard tower at [-1772, 77, -631].
- Mora: Very well. Let us get this over with.
- Yuman: From what I heard from Yulie, the commander usually keeps the schedules in the . Let's get looking!
''Upon going up the stairs at [-1759, 69, -621].
- Yuman: So, you? A soldier? What's the story there?
- Mora: Sigh... the story is it was a choice between joining the military, and following in my parents' footsteps. And I did not especially want to do the latter.
- Yuman: What'd your parents do?
- Mora: They worked as woodcutters. A relatively common job in the Auburn Forest, but... I simply wanted to distance myself from them.
- Mora: The military seemed my best option... until I met Syndra, that is. Still... I regret I could not do more for Sui. She did not take my departure well.
- Yuman: Hey, you were doing what was best for you, right? And it looks like you and Sui are all good now, so it turned out alright in the end.
- Mora: Hmm. Perhaps.
''Upon reaching the room at [-1769, 70, -620].
- Timasca Soldier: Woah there! Eheh, sorry folks, didn't see-
- Timasca Soldier: Wait. You three - if you have your equipment, you should be out on the streets. State your business here.
- Timasca Soldier: ... Well? I'm not hearing an answer. State. Your. Business.
- Mora: I- ah. We... we were looking for...
A soldier steps into Mora's face.
- Timasca Soldier: Speak up, soldier!
Yuman steps up and pulls Mora out of the way.
- Yuman: Excuse my partner, fellas!
- Yuman: Ya know how the stress gets. Festival's coming up, lots to worry about! Not getting much sleep - all that.
- Yuman: Heck, I don't even remember what I last ate, hahaha!
- Timasca Soldier: Ha! Yeah, I've been feeling that. Commander's got us working overtime, it's a whole mess.
- Timasca Soldier: Oh, hey, why don't y'all join us for some drinks after the shift?
- Yuman: Sounds great, man! Guess we'll meet you boys then! You got the night shift too, right?
- Timasca Soldier: Yeah. Drew the short straw, unfortunately. The commander has us doing them the next few days...
- Timasca Soldier: At this rate, we'll be too damn tired to enjoy the festival! Like... give us a break, right?
- Yuman: Yeah, yeah. Same sorta thing here! I got paired up with these newbies, and the commander's got us on festival shift.
- Timasca Soldier: Ouch. That's rough. Good luck out there.
- Yuman: Ey, thanks! But yeah, I'm still showin' them the ropes, and all that. We only got the news, like, an hour ago, so we're going to check the schedules.
- Timasca Soldier: Ah, management... putting newbies on festival shift? I wonder what the commander's thinking? Well, good luck with that.
- Yuman: Thanks! See ya around, fellas.
The soldiers exit the room.
- Yuman: ...told ya I could talk us through it.
- Mora: That was... impressive. I did not think it could be done.
- Yuman: Ah, y'know... they're still people at the end of the day.
- Mora: I... suppose. I apologize, I do not know why I... froze up there. I should know what I'm doing...
- Yuman: Hey, it happens. For the record, I'm sorry for bein' a bit rough with ya. Had to convince them somehow.
- Mora: No worries, Yuman, I understand. Now, ah... let us find the schedules before someone else notices we are not supposed to be here.
''Yuman and Mora head up the staircase at [-1768, 71, -630].
Talking to Yuman in the room with the schedules:
- Yuman: Let's find the schedules!
Talking to Mora in the room with the schedules:
- Mora: The schedules were further up, yes?
Bookshelf at [-1772, 77, -622].
- The shelf is filled with recent reports on military activity...
- Nothing seems to mention guard schedules, though.
Interact with the schedule board at [-1772, 77, -630] to progress the quest.
After interacting with the schedule board:
- Mora: Ah, Player, did you find them?
- Mora: Start writing them down, would you?
- First Division - Stationed at the main entrance to the city.
- Second Division - Stationed by the gate to the Mistwoods. Low Risk - will assist in case of commotion.
- Third Division - Guarding Sovereign Soosu's mansion.
- You continue to write down the rest of the guard divisions' positions...
- Mora: It's more guards than we typically see in Auburn festivals, that's for certain... I hope Syndra anticipated this.
- Yuman: She seems like the kind of lady to have back-up plans for her back-up plans... I wouldn't worry too much.
- Mora: I suppose you're right. Now, we should make our way out of here before anyone else arrives.
Return to The Steel Feather using the tunnel at [-1800, 28, -520] and find Yusanu and Sui.
Talking to Yuman in the room with the schedules again:
- Yuman: I could really use a nap after that.
Talking to Mora in the room with the schedules again:
- Mora: Seems like our mission is done. Let's head back.
Talking to Syndra and Jiro in The Steel Feather at [-2099, 6, -699].
- Syndra: ...and we'll need to keep things calm back here while we're gone.
- Jiro: Of course, of course. Wouldn't want anyone to panic.
- Syndra: I'm less concerned about panic, and more about stress. I know Quill will stay behind during the festival itself, but it'll be good to have additional help.
- Jiro: Yes, ma'am. I can handle it.
- Syndra: Good. Oh, Player, hello!
- Jiro: Ah, I should get going. I'll see if I can track down Quill.
- Syndra: Alright, good luck.
Jiro leaves.
- Syndra: Sigh...
- What was that about?
- Syndra: Oh, Jiro was asking if there was anything he could do to help. I told him he could help Quill keep the peace down here while we're... performing the plan.
- Syndra: He's... been acting a little out of character, truth be told... though it might just be the stress of the upcoming festival causing it.
- Syndra: But either way - how are things going?
- Going alright so far.
- Syndra: That's good to hear. I know I placed a lot of responsibility on your shoulders...
- Syndra: In truth, you have the most experience out of all the youngsters. And to ensure this plan succeeds... it's good to have you keep an eye on things.
- The dialogue branches combine here.
- Getting a bit tired.
- Syndra: Mmn. I apologize for placing so much on your shoulders.
- Syndra: But you have the most experience out of all the youngsters, and we need to ensure this plan works... we have no choice.
- The dialogue branches combine here.
- Syndra: But, regardless - Mora gave me the guard positions you retrieved. I was working with Rex and Zeph on our next steps, based off that information.
- Syndra: They've gone off... somewhere, I don't know where. Until they return, you should go see if Sui and Yusanu need anything.
Talking to Syndra again:
- Syndra: Until Rex and Zeph return, you should go see if Sui and Yusanu need anything.
Talk to Yusanu and Sui at [-2116, 6, -694].
When apporaching Yusanu and Sui:
- Sui: Oh! Player, you're back! How did it, um, go?
- We got the schedules!
- Sui: Oh! Good! It, um, went smoothly, I hope? Mora and Yuman got along?
- Yusanu: If they got the schedules, it was probably fine. So, Player, are you here to help us out too?
- The dialogue branches combine here.
- Why do I have to do all the work?
- Sui: Hehe, I guess that's what happens when you show off all those skills of yours!
- Yusanu: Yep! Oh, speaking of... Player, are you here to help us out too?
- The dialogue branches combine here.
- Yusanu: We've been putting together those explosives Syndra requested. I think we've decided on an easily produced model.
- Sui: By, um, "we," he mostly means him. I can, ha, barely understand what he's going on about.
- Yusanu: Hey, don't sell yourself short! You've been helpful! I would've never thought to utilize water in the design if it weren't for your suggestion.
- Sui: Oh... thank you. Player, we were playing around the idea of hiding magical water inside the, um, explosive... but I, ah, don't know how to hold its power when I can't... see it.
- Yusanu: Magic or not, using water in the design will make the explosion look more dangerous and powerful than it actually is! It's genius!
- Yusanu: Now, we just need to put it together...
- Do you need me for that?
- Yusanu: Eheh. Maybe? I need to run some tests while it's being assembled, and Sui needs to stand guard in case it's about to actually explode.
- Sui: If things go awry, I'll, um, surround it in a ball of water.
- Yusanu: Yep! Okay, no more questions, we've got to get to it!  whenever you're ready.
Help assemble the explosives inside the workshop at [-2114, 6, -696].
Right-click to start the puzzle.
Instructions:
- - Every square has to contain a piece of the bomb.
- - Some pieces have special
- - Create  bomb pieces and later combine them into one.
- - Tip! Hover over a piece (after picking it up as an item in your inventory) and it will tell you its shape.
There are several item types placed on the logs in the area.
- Casing (Coal Block): Can only be placed on the outer tiles.
- Gunpowder (Dark Gray Concrete Powder): Can only be placed on the inner tiles.
- Fuse (White Wool Block): Must touch the orange chemical.
- Switch (Gold Block): Can be placed anywhere.
- Wrench (Bone): Can remove any block from the board.
- Bomb Piece: Collect all pieces by finishing 3 puzzles!
Completing all four puzzles will give you the Electrical Explosive item. Exit by walking through the back at [-2277, 5, 2485] to return to the workshop.
- Yusanu: Phew! All clear! Good work, Player.
- Yusanu: I think Sui and I will perform a few more tests... maybe a test run or two... but the construction went okay, so I should be able to produce some more.
- Yusanu: And, eheh, hopefully not blow up my workshop...
- Sui: Oh, no... Player, are you sure you, um, can't stick around, a bit longer? Just, in case?
- Yusanu: Nope, there's still stuff to do! On that subject - Player,  was looking for you earlier.
Meet up with Zeph and Rex for the next assignment at [-2088, 6, -712].
Talking to Zeph and Rex:
- Rex: Player, finally! There you are! I was getting restless.
- Zeph: I w- was quite comfortable... actually.
- Rex: Oh, are the nerves getting to you Zeph?
- It's okay to be nervous.
- Zeph: I- I know... But it f- fe- feels like everyone else is doing okay, while I- I'm not even doing an- any- anything, and I'm a- al- already panicking.
- Rex: Hey, everyone else is also feeling nervous, Zeph. Some of us are just... better at hiding it than others.
- The dialogue branches combine here.
- I'm nervous too.
- Zeph: Re- really? For some reason, that m- ma- makes me feel a lot better... uh, n- no offense!
- Rex: We're all nervous, Zeph. It's a risky plan. But we know what we're doing. We have to trust we'll succeed.
- The dialogue branches combine here.
- Grow up, Zeph.
- Zeph: Ha ha, v- ver- very funny, Player. I- I- I'm trying. I am! It's just... hard not to be an- anxious.
- Rex: You're fine, Zeph. I'd be surprised if you weren't anxious, honestly. Given what we're planning on doing...
- The dialogue branches combine here.
- Zeph: I g- guess... It's all just st- st- starting to sink in.
- Rex: Look, the more you think about it, the worse it'll get. Accept the feeling for what it is, then put it aside for now.
- Rex: We've got work to do, and... we really can't afford to screw it up.
- Zeph: I- I'll do my best.
- Rex: That's all I ask. Anyway, Player, Zeph and I looked over the schedules with Syndra earlier. We've marked a couple of spots we want to check out.
- Zeph: So- s- so let's go see them in person! Uh, Rex, I c- ca- can carry the arrows and electric ch- charges for you.
- Rex: Oh, what a gentleman.
Quill and Yulie are walking, and stop when they see Zeph and Rex.
- Yulie: ...and those are the faces I usually see around, so-
- Quill: Ah- Rex, Zeph, and Player! Rather auspicious timing.
- Rex: Oh. hey! Have you seen the guard schedules yet?
- Yulie: We have, yep. Quill and I were just talking about some of the escape routes I had in mind.
- Rex: Are you heading out for your assignment then?
- Zeph: We were j- just about to head to Timasca for ours, too. P- per- perhaps we could go there together?
- Quill: Hmm... yes, I suppose we could- though, I'll want Player's opinion on our ideas as well. Once you finish with Rex and Zeph, would you care to join us?
- Sure!
- Yulie: Then let's get going. No time to waste.
Find Zeph and Rex in Timasca at [-1734, 27, -570].
Talking to Rex or Yulie in The Steel Feather again:
- Yulie: Rex, please don't pick the highest rooftops.
- Rex: You better not pick out the highest roof tops. I'm not sure I can get up that far.
- Yulie: I'm just not sure I'd be able to climb up to them.
- Rex: Well, Yuman seems to do it just fine! But okay, I'll pick out something more accessible for you.
- Yulie: That's all I ask!
Talking to Quill in The Steel Feather again:
- Quill: Hm... Player, I don't suppose you would happen to have seen Jiro?
- Quill: Syndra told me he had gone looking for me, but I haven't seen him all day!
- Quill: Well, I suppose I can always find him after we're done here. No need to delay this any longer.
Talking to Zeph in The Steel Feather again:
- Zeph: Just one more day... a- a- and then it'll be done. I can m- make it that far.
Exit The Steel Feather using the fast travel at [-2196, 6, -671].

lines.title: Where to find the strong evidence
lines.text:
There are four different minigames and objectives that give strong evidence.

* Asking Demma about . A luggage puzzle must be completed to read the book on the table and get the strong evidence.



* Asking Maddison about . A crossword must be completed to get the strong evidence.



* Choosing Cemor's  dialogue option, and then choosing Telati's  dialogue option. This allows you to enter the kitchen to make food for Cemor to get the strong evidence.

* The master key found at [-19842, 10, 24329] can be used to unlock the Staff Only room next to the bathroom. A book inside can be interacted with to get the strong evidence.
Initial notes:
: A noble from the Highlands who booked the wrong date for his tickets and was late to see Espren's Festival. Not wanting to waste money, he is taking the trip anyway.
: A student of Aelumia University's prestigious Blossom house, travelling to Auburn Forest for a field study.
: An Auburn citizen who disliked their home and hoped to see a better region in the Roughworks. They now head home disappointed.
: A citizen of Aelumia Citadel, travelling the province to experience something different to her home.
: A Roughworks citizen who has had the rare opportunity to take a train to another region, in his case, Auburn Forest.
: A helpful attendant, working hard to appease all passengers. He the only staffer on this train, besides the driver.

- Maury: That works fer us!
- Maury: Hands behind yer back, bub, the train's about to arrive in Espren.
The scene changes to the station at Espren. Malic is taken away by the guards.
- Malic: I'm innocent!
Everyone else leaves the station.
The guards and the general can also be accused, however choosing them will only play a short dialogue without progressing the quest.
- Harvin: Come on, idiot. We're not going to let you accuse US, obviously.
- Maury: Even if it WAS me, there'd be nothing ya could do about it. We're the ones with power here. Now go and select one of the passengers, come on.
- Maury: ...You mean to suggest she... No, that's just not possible.
- Harvin: Yeah, why would she? She had important business to do...
- Maury: Well, Harvin, maybe she got tired of her job? That Majin bossin' her around all the time's gotta get tirin'...
- Harvin: Hm...
- Maury: You know what? Even if she did do it, I don't care; we need someone to blame. Now COME ON! Accuse someone already, preferably alive this time!

lines.title: The Guilty Patron
lines.text: Cemor is the one who murdered General Levi.
If you accused an innocent:
- ...Looks like that's all over.
- It doesn't seem like you judged the killer's identity correctly. Hopefully, that doesn't end up being a problem.
- ...And hopefully, the innocent person you just condemned to prison gets exonerated...
- At the very least, there is one silver lining. See, you snagged something pretty handy along the way.
- ''"TRAIN PASS: GENERAL OF THE PROVINCIAL GUARD"
- "Possession of this pass entitles its bearer to a train ride  they request,  of charge, by Her Majesty's orders."
- "Rejection of such a request is considered obstruction of the Crown's will, and a serious crime."
- How convenient!
If you accused the guilty patron:
- ...Looks like that's all- Huh?.
- ???: Hey! You!
Harvin walks back to the player.
- Harvin: That guy we just arrested? He was STACKED! LOADED! We're gonna be vacationing in the Highlands with this kind of money, haha!
- Harvin: Don't tell Maury, but I felt like you deserved a small cut of the profits, Y'know, for figuring it out, and all.
- Maury: HEY! HARVIN! Didn't I tell ya not to go and give 'em anything? Idiot!
- Harvin: ...Shoot. Guess that's my cue to leave.
Harvin leaves.
- ...Nice.
- Thank goodness he didn't stick around. After all, you wouldn't want him to see what you kept from the crime scene, would you?
- ''"TRAIN PASS: GENERAL OF THE PROVINCIAL GUARD"
- "Possession of this pass entitles its bearer to a train ride  they request,  of charge, by Her Majesty's orders."
- "Rejection of such a request is considered obstruction of the Crown's will, and a serious crime."
- How convenient!
Regardless of who is accused, the quest rewards 5  Liquid Emeralds upon completion.
Meet up with Sui outside Hyloch at [-1358, 108, -1194].
- Sui: ...Hyloch. Ha, the... the tourists really weren't lying when they kept saying it was a work of art.
- Sui: It must be nice, living here... being able to ignore everything going on everywhere else...
- Sui: Player, we need to find that... that so-called "number one" Sovereign! If we can do that, then... ha, then we can save Rex and Zeph.
- We can't just rush this.
- Sui: Why not?! You're the one who wanted to- to rush into Deraj and free everyone without even stopping to think about it!
- Sui: So why can't I?! The longer we wait, the more chances there are for s-something to happen!! We need to go already!
- The dialogue branches combine here.
- We need a plan first!
- Sui: Yeah, I have one. Find the Sovereign. Free Rex and Zeph. And get out of there!
- Sui: I'll... f-fill in the details as we go. I will! We just need to go already!
- The dialogue branches combine here.
- Sui: ...we don't have time to argue.
- Where will we bring them?
- Sui: ... I don't know.
- Sui: I guess... the Canopy? We can bring them to the Canopy! That... that works...
- The dialogue branches combine here.
- Do you know where they are?
- Sui: Um... n-no, I guess not. But- but we can find someone who does, and- and force the information out of them!
- Sui: We can do that. Captain Fuhue, she... told me about some of her methods! I just... need to find someone who... knows...
- The dialogue branches combine here.
- And you're just going to fight Majin?
- Sui: If- if that's what it takes!! We were able to k-kill Gikyo, weren't we?
- Sui: Even if it was hard... and Majin is... probably stronger...
- The dialogue branches combine here.
- Okay. Let's go then.
- Sui: Good. Okay! To start with, we...
- Sui: We just have to... um...
- The dialogue branches combine here.
- Sui: Okay, fine, maybe you're right! Just... ugh!! We have to do something!
- Let's get clothes to blend in.
- Sui: ...right. That's... smart. Word's probably spread from, um, Fort Hegea, hasn't it...? We'll need to blend in better.
- Sui: And... we don't know how long it'll be until we... find the information we need. So... a place to say, too?
- Sui: Okay. Find , and find . That's a plan. We can do that.
Find clothes in Hyloch.
The Clothes Merchant is found at [-1332, 106, -1276]. There are also various NPCs found throughout Hyloch that can be talked to.
Hyloch Citizen at [-1356, 106, -1234].
- Hyloch Citizen: Ah... tourists.
- Hyloch Citizen: Looking for something?
- You from around here?
- Hyloch Citizen: Indeed, I am. I was raised here in Hyloch.
- Hyloch Citizen: Though, in truth... I've never really left. I'm planning on enlisting in the military once I've completed my provincial tour.
- Hyloch Citizen: I've been saving up for years for a round-trip ticket throughout the province... I'd like to see all of the less-fortunate regions firsthand.
- Hyloch Citizen: I'm leaving just after the festival. Exciting, isn't it?
- The dialogue options return.
- Are there any hotels nearby?
- Hyloch Citizen: Hotels... hm. I know of several, though most have probably filled entirely for the upcoming festival.
- Hyloch Citizen: There is a fancy hotel north of the bank... The Crown Jewel, I believe? It's probably far too expensive for you, however.
- The dialogue options return.
- What should we check out?
- Hyloch Citizen: A fine question. I'm not too certain, honestly... growing up here has made me overlook things.
- Hyloch Citizen: I know tourists typically travel here to look at all our mansions and castles, though. Perhaps you'd be interested?
- The dialogue options return.
- Goodbye.
- Hyloch Citizen: Enjoy your stay.
- The dialogue ends here.
Hyloch Citizen at [-1344, 106, -1249].
- Hyloch Citizen: Praise be to her Majesty.
- Hyloch Citizen: How might I help you this fine day?
- How are you?
- Hyloch Citizen: As fine as one may be! Thank you for your inquiry.
- Hyloch Citizen: I have been graciously afforded an hour off from my work, so I have chosen to take the time and... smell the roses. To admire the beauty of our city.
- The dialogue options return.
- It's my first time here, any tips?
- Hyloch Citizen: Ah... tourists from the lower districts, I take it? A fine use of your travel allotments.
- Hyloch Citizen: You will want to visit the bustling market on the west side, it would be a shame to miss it!
- Hyloch Citizen: And if you wish to leave the bounds of the city, I have heard one may find tour guides which will bring you to see the mountains!
- The dialogue options return.
- We're looking for some hip new fashion.
- Hyloch Citizen: Yes, Hyloch is known for its high fashion, isn't it? I'm certain you've heard about it... wherever you come from.
- Hyloch Citizen: The famous House Til has placed a pop-up clothes shop to the , if you're interested.
- The dialogue options return.
- Goodbye.
- Hyloch Citizen: I wish you the best on your stay! Praise be to her Majesty!
- The dialogue ends here.
Auburn Tourist at [-1349, 106, -1250].
- Espren Tourist: Oh... darn it...
- Espren Tourist: I should have thought about where I'd be staying... I've never taken a train before, so all my thinking went towards making sure that went well!
- Espren Tourist: And now all the hotels except the Crown Jewel are fully booked! Will I... will I have to sleep on the street?
- Espren Tourist: Oh, what am I going to do...?
- Espren Tourist: Oh, thank you, thank you! The Queen herself must have sent you my way!
- Well.... I wish you good luck!
- Espren Tourist: ...short on emeralds too, are you? Maybe we can share a comfy bush together! Ha...
After giving the tourist money:
- Espren Tourist: Oh, I'll remember you forever! You've truly made this festival the best one yet!
- Espren Tourist: I can't wait to tell my old folk all about it! How the Queen had blessed me with this miracle...
- Sui: But, it wasn't the Queen that... oh, nevermind.
Newspaper Merchant at [-1325, 108, -1270].
- Newspaper Merchant: Hello, hello! Care to buy any of our fine papers? Perhaps a magazine is up your alley today- quite the juicy bits of gossip I've heard.
Roughworks Tourist at [-1335, 106, -1279].
- Roughworks Tourist: Hm... Do I want the Crown of Seraphim collection, or the Peacock Couture...
- Roughworks Tourist: Oh, this is important... a whole year's paycheck is going towards this!
- Clothes Merchant: Heya! Tourists?
- Sui: Something like that.
- We need some clothes.
- Clothes Merchant: Well, it seems you're in luck! Considering this is a pop-up clothes stall, and all.
- Clothes Merchant: I'm here representing House Til today. The new fashionable spring line has almost sold out, so shop now if you're interested!
- Sui: Um... is this the fashion around here?
- Clothes Merchant: Oh, yes. People from all across the province come to shop at these pop-up events.
- Clothes Merchant: House Til is known for incorporating the designs from peacock feathers into their most extravagant garments!
- Clothes Merchant: They come in a wide variety of available colours- all from the district's local dye production!
- Sui: We don't need anything fancy. Just... show us the cheapest stuff you have, okay?
- Clothes Merchant: My goodness! You must know fashion does not come cheap, miss! Please, allow me to recommend-
- Sui: No. Just let us buy the cheapest stuff you have.
- Clothes Merchant: Uh huh... well, alright. If you insist...
- Clothes Merchant: Here, the cheapest I have available. In total, that will cost you... .
- Alright, we'll pay.
- Clothes Merchant: Very well. Here you are. Now, please leave, your attitude is not good for business!
- Sui: Okay... that's the clothes. Now we just... need a place to, um, stay. A , maybe...
- The dialogue ends here.
- I... don't have that.
- Clothes Merchant: Well! As I said, fashion is not cheap!
- The dialogue ends here without progressing the quest.
Talking to the Clothes Merchant again after leaving without paying:
- Clothes Merchant: Ah, you're back. As I said, the clothes will cost you .
- Alright, we'll pay.
- Clothes Merchant: [?] (This interaction does not currently work)
- I... don't have that. (Ends the dialogue.)
Talking to the Clothes Merchant again after buying the clothes:
- Clothes Merchant: Ah... Listen, I still need to sell all of my stock, or I won't receive my bonus!
- Clothes Merchant: So, unless you're interested in buying more clothes... please, leave.
Find a hotel in Hyloch.
The hotel entrance is found at [-1370, 109, -1254].
- Receptionist: Why, hello and welcome to the Crown Jewel! How may I assist you?
- Sui: We're looking for a room.
- Receptionist: Well, do you have a booking?
- Sui: Um.. n-no. But-
- Receptionist: Hm I see. In that case, allow me to quickly check out listings...
The Receptionist turns around to check the available rooms, then looks back at Sui and the player.
- Receptionist: Aha! You're in luck! It seems we have a spare double room available! But that may not last long- let me tell you, they are selling fast!
- We need a bigger room.
- Receptionist: A... bigger room? You're certain? From where I stand, I only see the two of you, and-
- Sui: We're... going to have friends with us. They just... haven't, um, arrived yet.
- Receptionist: I see. I see That certainly complicates things...
- The dialogue branches combine here.
- We're expecting company.
- Receptionist: Company? Well, whatever sort? If you're just looking to socialize, the double room should serve your purposes well en-
- Sui: No, they'll... be staying with us.
- Receptionist: Mmn. Yes, that would certainly put a damper on things. Hm...
- The dialogue branches combine here.
- Receptionist: Well. I suppose we do also have the luxury suite available. Though, it's quite the hefty price...
- Sui: We- we'll take it. I'll pay.
- Receptionist: You're certain? Apologies if I am making assumptions here, but you do not seem the sort who would have-
- Sui: Yes. I am. Here.
Sui goes up to the counter and pays.
- Receptionist: ...huh. Well, everything seems in order then. Here are your keys, madame.
The Receptionist hands the room key to Sui.
- Sui: ...thanks.
Sui turns to look at the player.
- Sui: Player, I'm... going up to the room.
- You don't want to look around?
- Sui: No. We're... not here for pleasure, Player. We're here to... to... to save our friends.
- The dialogue branches combine here.
- Let's get some food or drinks.
- Sui: I'm, um... not hungry. And I'm, ha, definitely not in the mood for a drink.
- The dialogue branches combine here.
- Sui: ...you can, um, take a look around though. If- if you want. Just... don't take too long.
- Sui: We're in... room 5, apparently. I'll... leave the door open for you.
Sui goes up the stairs to the right of the lobby.
Head to your room and discuss what to do next.
Sui is found in Room #5 at [-1159, 11, 5511]. There are also various NPCs and interactable objects found in the hotel.
Hotel Receptionist at [-1170, 3, 5510].
- Receptionist: Ah! What can I do for you today?
- Any tourist recommendations in Hyloch?
- Receptionist: The Highlands are known for thier very scenic walks and hikes! I would recommend walking around the lakes or hiking up to the mountains.
- Receptionist: Hyloch is also known for their very rich alcohol culture. We brew a lot of different beverages that can be enjoyed at our local taverns.
- The dialogue options return.
- Do you host any events here at the hotel?
- Receptionist: We are not hosting any particular events at this moment because of the upcoming festival.
- Receptionist: Usually, we host game nights and quizzes in our bar!
- The dialogue options return.
- I want to make a complaint.
- Receptionist: Oh, are things not up to your standard?
- Receptionist: What have you experienced issues with?
- The beds are uncomfortable.
- Receptionist: I apologise for that! We will send in a cleaner later to fluff em up for ya!
- Receptionist: Thank you for your feedback.
- The first dialogue options return.
- The room is dirty.
- Receptionist: Oh I will let our cleaners know to do a better job.
- Receptionist: Thank you for your feedback.
- The first dialogue options return.
- It is too expensive!
- Receptionist: Unfortunately there is nothing we can do to help with that.
- Receptionist: Thank you for your feedback.
- The first dialogue options return.
- Bye!
- Receptionist: Let me know if there's anything I can do to make your stay better!
- The dialogue ends here.
- Rules of The Crown Jewel
- - No noise after 9 PM.
- - No entering other guests' rooms.
- - No vandalizing the property.
- - No pets allowed.
- - No weaponry or blessed equipment in common areas.
- - Late checkout will come with a 64 LE fine.
Vending Machine at [-1170, 3, 5503].
- There's a note attached...
- "ATTENTION CUSTOMERS: No, despite the beer-like design of this vending machine, it does not serve alcoholic beverages! Please go to the bar for those! And stop asking us about it!"
- The vending machine's selection becomes available.
Elevator at [-1173, 3, 5503].
- There's a sign on the elevator door.
- "The elevator is currently out of order. We apologize for the inconvenience." Signed, The Crown Jewel Management Team
Timasca Tourist at [-1163, 3, 5521].
- Timasca Tourist: A year of saving... f-finally payed off!
- Timasca Tourist: A... a giant meal, and a nice hotel... and I have it all to m-myself!! Best! Week!! Ever!!
Timasca Tourist at [-1152, 3, 5507].
- Timasca Tourist: *buuurp*
- Timasca Tourist: ANOTHER ONE!!
- Timasca Tourist: MORE *burp* WHISKEY!!!!
- Do you want to play a song?
- Status

- Now playing:

- Now playing:

- Now playing:

- Now playing:
Hyloch Citizen and Espren Tourist at [-1162, 3, 5501].
- Hyloch Citizen: ...I had heard that about the Auburn Festival!
- Espren Tourist: I can't say I expected word to reach Hyloch from over there. Though, let me say... so far, I am very impressed by how Hyloch handles festivities.
- Hyloch Citizen: Why, the real festivities haven't even begun! You're in for a treat, my friend.
- Hyloch Citizen: ...by chance, would you let me show you around when the festival starts in full? I've enjoyed our talks so far.
- Espren Tourist: I'd love that. I've never been outside the Auburn Forest before... so it would be nice to have someone to guide me, wouldn't it?
- Hyloch Citizen: Wonderful! Then it's a date!
The Auburn Tourist only appears in the hotel if you donated 2 Liquid Emeralds previously. (See stage 2 Optional Dialogue for the interaction)
Auburn Tourist at [-1178, 11, 5517] in Room #1.
- Espren Tourist: Ah, I'm so glad we meet again!
- Espren Tourist: Even though you... barged into my room... er, isn't that against hotel policy?
- Espren Tourist: ...oh, well, I won't tell them. You did help me pay for the room, after all! I wish you all the best.
- Espren Tourist: Maybe we'll meet again! Perhaps I could buy you a drink at the festival?
Ice machine at [-1148, 11, 5512].
- Do you want to get some ice?
- Get ice.
- The machine shakes and makes a loud noise.
- It appears to be out of order.
- Leave.
Talking to Sui at [-1159, 11, 5493].
- Sui: ...oh, you're here. Are you done looking around?
- Sui: So, um. I've been... planning our next steps. Finding a place to stay was... a good idea, I guess. You were right. I shouldn't... rush into it.
- Sui: But this is a good place to regroup once we... once we get Rex and Zeph back. We should, ha, act as early as possible, though.
- What if we're too late?
- Sui: Stop that. You k-keep doing that, acting as if... a-as if the worst is inevitable! It's not helpful!
- Just being realistic.
- Sui: Well... don't!! I know already, I know they might be gone, but I- I can't think like that. I can't. I have to believe they're still... fighting!!
- Sui: ...um. Anyway, we should... l-look around the town. To try and figure out where they're being held. If we can figure that out, then...
- The dialogue branches combine here.
- Okay. What do we do?
- Sui: Look around the town, I guess... try and figure out where that Sovereign is keeping them. If we can figure that out, then... we can save them.
- The dialogue branches combine here.
- Sui: We should start right away. Come on.
- We should rest first.
- Sui: I can't, I can't, I can't. If I stop for... for even a second, I'll... I'll shatter. I have to keep moving. I have to.
- The dialogue branches combine here.
- Are you doing alright?
- Sui: What do you think?! NO, I'm not doing alright!! But I have to do something about it, or... or... I'll shatter.
- The dialogue branches combine here.
- Sui: You can... stay here and rest if you, um, need to. But I'm going to search the city for clues. By myself if... if I have to.
- I'll come with you.
- Sui: ...okay. Thank you. Let's go.
Sui leaves the hotel.
Meet up with Sui outside the Crown Jewel at [-1370, 109, -1248].
Sui is directly outside the hotel, staring at a wind chime.
- Sui: Hm.....
- What's wrong?
- Sui: This... this wind chime. Look at it.
- The dialogue branches combine here.
- Admiring the city?
- Sui: ...what? No, I'm looking at a wall. What do you think I was looking at?
- The dialogue branches combine here.
- Sui: These wind chimes. They're... a symbol of resistance in the Auburn Forest. S... um, Syndra told us about them.
Sui looks back towards the wind chime.
- Sui: The wind represents... freedom, and free will. But I wouldn't have expected the chimes to have made it all the way here...?
- Sui: Could... could this mean what I think it does?
Sui walks over to the chimes and touches them.
- Sui: I was right... I was right! It's a symbol of resistance, th-that means Hyloch must have its own resistance!!
- Sui: We... we need to seek them out, Player!
- Shh!
- Sui: ...oh. Right. Um, sorry. I just... got excited.
- The dialogue branches combine here.
- I think the whole city heard you.
- Sui: ...oh. Oops. Let's um, hope I wasn't too loud...
- The dialogue branches combine here.
- Sui: A-anyway. I think there's... an inscription on the wind chime.
- Sui: "The winds of change blow from the west, crashing waves of truth unto our shores."
- Sui: ...that must be where the resistance is! Let's- let's find them!
Find the location specified on the wind chime in Hyloch: The winds of change blow from the west, crashing waves of truth unto our shores.

lines.title: Solving the riddle
lines.text:
The next wind chime is at [-1437, 124, -1256], on the side of a house by the water.

Interacting with the wind chime:
* Sui: ...oh. There... doesn't seem to be a resistance here. Just another wind chime.
* Sui: Does this one also have something written on it?
* "Rooted deep atop the house of wealth and greed, the branches hear the whispers on the breeze."
Find the next location: Rooted deep atop the house of wealth and greed, the branches hear the whispers on the breeze.

lines.title: Solving the riddle
lines.text:
The next wind chime is on top of the bank at [-1382, 153, -1237].

The easiest way to reach the top of the bank is from the building at [-1403, 118, -1280]. Use the ladder at the back at [-1401, 119, -1256], then use movement spells to get onto the bank.

Interacting with the wind chime:
* "The whispers speak of unity, called forth where regions meet through lines of burrowed steel."
Find the next location: The whispers speak of unity, called forth where regions meet through lines of burrowed steel.

lines.title: Solving the riddle
lines.text:
The next wind chime is at [-1285, 84, -1213], on the side of the ticket booth for the train station.

Interacting with the wind chime:
* "Day after day, the voices greet the seekers. Identify the truth, and read the secrets printed."
Find the next location: Day after day, the voices greet the seekers. Identify the truth, and read the secrets printed.

lines.title: Solving the riddle
lines.text:
The next wind chime is at [-1324, 110, -1263], outside the newspaper shop.

Interacting with the wind chime:
* "May we unearth the truth long buried and bring forth change."
* Maybe you could ask the merchant inside about the wind chime?




Newspaper Merchant at [-1325, 108, -1270].
* Newspaper Merchant: Hello, hello! Care to buy any of our fine papers? Perhaps a magazine is up your alley today- quite the juicy bits of gossip I've heard.
** Yes, please!
*** Sui: What? Player, what are you doing? That's not...
**** The dialogue branches combine here.
** Uh... no.
*** The dialogue branches combine here.
* Sui: ...um. We're very interested in your... um, your wind chimes.
* Newspaper Merchant: Windchimes? I'm sorry? I haven't the foggiest idea what you mean. I've certainly heard of them down in the Auburn Forest, but here? What an odd thing to say.
* Newspaper Merchant: But still, perhaps I can get you a paper. Out of curiosity... ? I don't think I've seen you around here before!
** Where regions meet... (Choosing this option progresses the quest)
** The train station.
*** Newspaper Merchant: Haha, oh dear. I asked where you were from, not the way you got here. So, let's try that one again! Where are you two from?
**** The dialogue options reappear.
** The Mistwoods, actually.
*** Newspaper Merchant: Ah, yes, and I found a gold bar in my mailbox today! Haha, you'll have to try harder to pull one over on me like that- no one's lived in the Mistwoods for ages! Now, be serious! I was genuine in asking.
**** The dialogue options reappear.
** I... spawned in. From nothing.
*** Newspaper Merchant: So too we all do- from nothing but milk and love, as I've heard it's said, but if we were to talk about the origins of the universe we'd be here all night. So, where are you really from?
**** The dialogue options reappear.


After choosing the "Where regions meet..." dialogue option.
* Player: Where regions meet through lines of burrowed steel.
* Newspaper Merchant: Ahaaa, I see! So you're looking for the people who seek the truth. A noble endeavour, certainly.
* Sui: We'd, um, love to meet some more of these... truth... seekers...?
* Newspaper Merchant: There's many a like-minded individual if you know where to look. So allow me to catch your eye with the Aelumia Times! It's the best way to keep up with current events.
* Newspaper Merchant: Column 9 will often print the phrase of the day. Read up, and pay close attention! Things will kick off here at midnight.
* Newspaper Merchant: I wish you two good luck on your endeavours. May we unearth the truth long buried and bring forth change.
* Sui: Th-thank you. Um... may we unearth the truth long buried and bring forth change!
** What she said!
*** The dialogue ends here.
** May we...
*** Player: May we unearth the truth long buried and bring forth change.
*** The dialogue ends here.
Leave the shop and discuss the next steps.
Talking to the Newspaper Merchant again:
- Newspaper Merchant: May we unearth the truth long buried and bring forth change. Never forget that.
Leave the shop to the west in order for Sui to talk.
The following dialogue plays automatically.
- Sui: Finally! Finally, finally, something good is happening!
- Sui: I didn't even think there'd be a resistance in Hyloch... it just seems so... idyllic, here. Like... um, like they don't really have... issues.
- Sui: But... I guess we don't know what life is like here... um, either way, if they're a resistance, they have to have intel.
- Sui: Here, hand me that newspaper. Okay... Column 9... looks like today's phrase of the day is... "No such thing as a green Squirmle Pot?"
- Sui: Weird. But... I guess nobody's going to guess it!
- Sui: Okay. Okay... th-this is happening! Majin Thalas, "number one" Sovereign, we're coming for you...
- Sui: I'm feeling a lot better now. Um... what should we do now, then? While we... wait for midnight.
- Sui: Yes... um, thinking about it now, I guess I am kind of starving...
- Sui: I remember seeing a restaurant earlier! .
- Sui: I... I guess I could use a nap...
- Sui: Okay. I'll meet you in our room.
Head to the restaurant and wait at [-1344, 113, -1266].
Restaurant
The restaurant is directly above the Item Identifier.
The following dialogue plays automatically when standing in the chair:
- Sui: Oh... this is quite cozy, actually. It... it, ha, doesn't really... compare to the Red Fox... but it works.
- Sui: Maybe it's... better that it, isn't the same. I'm not sure I could...
The Waiter walks up to the table.
