- Fuhue: Perhaps if it can be cut off at its source...
- Rurie: What, you mean passing through it into whatever it is on the other side? All in the hopes of chasing down the Queen? Who would be insane enough to even consider-
- I would.
- Rurie: Right! Of course, how could I forget! We have you. Well, I suppose that's all sorted then - not a problem I need concern myself with. What a relief.
- Fuhue: Hm. Leaves us more time to finalize the stabilizing plan for the province, to deal with the chaos that comes after this chaos concludes. Joy.
- Rurie: Yes, yes... we can get to that. Player, before you set off on yet another dangerous mission, you'd best go speak to everyone here. Alleviate some concerns, yes?
Talking to Zeph, Yuman, and Yulie at [-1558, 129, -768]:
- Yulie: ...and you're alright? No injuries- nothing?
- Yuman: Ughhhhh... yeah, bro, I'm fine! Quit hovering!
- Yulie: Well, sorry for being worried under these circumstances! The SKY is broken, Yuman, so let me hover at least a little, okay?!
- Zeph: Well, a...at least the soldiers have b- ba- backed off a little... so, that's s- something.
- Yulie: Sigh... yeah, that is something. I'm almost out of electrical charges...
Everyone notices the player.
- Zeph: ...Player! Y- you're back!!
- Yuman: Ey, you made it!!!
- I made it!
- Zeph: S...so does that mean you... y- you stopped her?
- Yuman: Is she dead?!
- Auburn is safe...
- Yuman: Hell yeah!!
- Yulie: ...I hear a "but" added on to the end. Where are Rex and Sui?
- Tell them.
- You tell them about fighting Tasim. And then the Queen.
- You tell them about the aftermath - the Queen's transformation, the rifts opening.
- You tell them about how the dam broke, about how Sui singlehandedly kept the water from flooding the Auburn Forest.
- You tell them about Zhiraok and Soosu arriving on the scene, about Soosu fixing up the dam.
- You... tell them about Rex. About how she saved you, about how she lost her arm, about how she... died.
- You tell them about Zhiraok, using his revival charm to save her. About the cost of doing so.
- Zeph: ...
- Yuman: ...
- Yulie: ...
- Zeph: B...but she's... sh- she's okay, now...?
- Yuman: ...man. Man. That... that really sucks, huh?
- Zeph: Her... h- her bow... she's n- ne- never gonna be able to... use it ag- again...
- Yuman: I didn't even consider that... man. So, then... Sui's with her still?
- Yes.
- Yulie: She's... in good hands, at least. Multiple Sovereigns, turning to our side... it's a little hard to believe.
- Yulie: But this is good. If they've turned against the Queen... it'll make things easier for us once this is all over.
- Yuman: Guess so... WAIT! So Zhiraok broke Soosu out of prison?! Was that-
- Zeph: -wh- what we saw? It was a- a flash of s- so- something, going into and out of the p...palace! Just before the sk...sky broke.
- Yuman: It must've been! That explains some things! Hey, no wonder the soldiers were so confused!!
- Zeph: Ha... y- yeah...
- Zeph: ...Player. The Queen isn't d...dead, is she?
- Zeph: Then... y...you're going after her. Right?
- Yuman: Zeph... you're not thinking of going in there too, are you?
- Zeph: ...
- Yuman: You are.
- Zeph: I- I have to... Rex won't be in any sh- shape to fight, a- and- and it's my turn to do my p...part anyway!
- Yuman: ... Fine. But you have to come back, princess! We've got plans, remember? I still have to show you where I grew up, and-
- Zeph: -and sh...show me your favourite food stand from when you were gr...growing up, I- I know. I'll be b- back.
- Yulie: Okay, lovebirds, that's my signal to get out of here. There's schedules I have to organize...
- Yulie: ...but yeah. Zeph, Player, I expect to see you two again. Understood?
- Yulie: Good. Just making sure.
Talking to Quill and Azael at [-1554, 129, -812]:
- Azael: Player, I'm glad to see you're back.
- Quill: I heard from Zeph that you and the girls decided to challenge Her Majesty.
- Quill: How... how did it go? I can't help notice the lack of companions by your side.
- We stopped her...
- Player: We stopped her. But she destroyed the dam in the process. Luckily, Sui, with the help of Soosu, managed to stop the water from reaching Auburn. However, Her Majesty escaped into her realm.
- Azael: Sui has grown into quite the powerful cursed one, huh?
- Quill: Did I hear that right... Soosu?
- The remaining Sovereigns have joined us... I think...
- Azael: That... is an unexpected turn of events. However, you may accept their change of heart but for the rest of us...
- Azael: They are an extension of her Majesty. All the pain and suffering they have caused is because of them.
- Quill: Actually...
- Quill: We have been thinking about how to handle the aftermath; in case we were successful. The larger populous knows of us as only terrorists. They would never accept us to rebuild Fruma.
- Quill: But. With the Sovereigns on our side, the people might, they just might, hear them out.
- Azael: Ugh. You're right. This is the best option we got.
- Quill: We will need to arrange a meeting with them to discuss moving forwards. I expect it to be tense, even hostile. But, but we can do this.
- Azael: I'll get Fuhue to draft up our plan, then.
Talking to Rurie again:
- Rurie: Need anything from me?
- How did it go on your end?
- Rurie: Went without a scratch, of course.
- Rurie: Well, we did have a lot of issues... I wasn't worried but I'm glad Zeph and Cileon returned with us.
- Rurie: Fuhue's talismans were doing a lot of the heavy listing in their absence.
- The dialogue options return here.
- What's the plan after this?
- Rurie: The Canopy will be helping with the aftermath. I don't care for becoming a public figure after this is over. though.
- Rurie: The trees are calling my name and the Highlands is definitely not the place for me.
- Rurie: Besides, could you ever see such a hunk like me become a politician... Pshh, at least I can't.
- The dialogue options return here.
- Rurie: Good luck out there.
- The dialogue ends here.
Talking to Cileon again:
- Cileon: ...hm?
- How did it go on your end?
- Cileon: Foxes and I cleared them out.
- The dialogue options return here.
- What's the plan after this?
- Cileon: I want to return to the forest.
- Cileon: Need to hunt, run and stay away from... cities.
- The dialogue options return here.
- Cileon: Best of luck.
- The dialogue ends here.
Talking to Fuhue again:
- Fuhue: ...yes? What do you need?
- How did it go on your end?
- Fuhue: My talismans did the trick. Managed to keep up a temporary barrier for some time.
- Fuhue: Unfortunately, they only last for some time and my schedule has not allowed me to create more. It was a miscalculation on my side.
- Fuhue: I have completely, utterly failed as the Deer's captain. I totally underestimated how many barrier talismans we needed!
- The dialogue options return here.
- What's the plan after this?
- Fuhue: The Canopy will remain. Master has asked me to document everything that has transpired in the past coupl of weeks. It will take me at least one week and three days to compile it all.
- Fuhue: Besides, without the Queen a new government will have to be established. I am planning to be of assistance, there as well.
- The dialogue options return here.
- Fuhue: Okay.
- The dialogue ends here.
Talking to Zeph again:
- Zeph: W-what's up?
- How did it go on your end?
- Zeph: When we got- got back we had almost been c-completely overtaken.
- Zeph: I'd like t-to -to believe I helped but... to be honest Rurie did most of the w-work.
- Zeph: I felt guilty that I- I left you guys.
- Zeph: But I will n-not back down for this final showdown!
- The dialogue options return here.
- What's the plan after this?
- Zeph: For o-once I'm... hopeful?
- Zeph: It's, it's weird. After everything we've g-gone through, after everyone we- we- we lost. I have hope for the future.
- Zeph: I promised myself when... when I was captured that if I- I made it out, I would not let my life fly by. I will l-live for Syndra and Mora. I will k-keep Syndra's legacy going.
- Zeph: And I made a p-promise to Yuman. I w-want to explore the world with- with him.
- The dialogue options return here.
- Are you truly ready to take the Queen down?
- Zeph: I don't think I- I will n-never be ready but, I want to do all that I c-can.
- Zeph: I won't be a hinderance to you. I k-know you and Sui are strong but... I'm not h-helpless.
- The dialogue options return here.
- Zeph: I'll follow you whenever you're r-ready, friend.
- The dialogue ends here.
Talking to Yuman again:
- Yuman: What's up?
- How did it go on your end?
- Yuman: Things were looking veeery hairy for a bit. Luckily, Rurie brought back up just in time.
- Yuman: Those Canopy people can be quite scary, I must say.
- The dialogue options return here.
- What's the plan after this?
- Yuman: I know that chaos is sure to ensue with Her Majesty gone but, I don't think I'm the best at... cleaning up a province.
- Yuman: I would honestly love to see the world. Traveling the world with someone you like sounds... nice.
- Yuman: I also miss the Steel Feather. I don't know what will happen to that place, or what has happened for that matter, but that place will always be my home.
- The dialogue options return here.
- Yuman: You guys better be careful!
- The dialogue ends here.
Talking to Yulie again:
- Yulie: What's on your mind?
- How did it go on your end?
- Yulie: I'm just glad we managed to sort the situation.
- Yulie: My electric charges almost ran out and I would have been useless without them.
- The dialogue options return here.
- What's the plan after this?
- Yulie: Honestly, I'm ready to deal with the fall out of this revolution.
- Yulie: I want to make a difference. I want to make sure the new Fruma is a good place. It will for sure take some time. But, I'm ready to spend the rest of my life bettering the province.
- The dialogue options return here.
- Yulie: I better be seeing you later.
- The dialogue ends here.
Talking to Quill again:
- Quill: Anything on your mind?
- What's the plan after this?
- Quill: I intend to make up for my past mistakes. I don't think I told you this before but, the wall that separates the Mistwoods from the Roughworks was designed by me during my university stay.
- Quill: I thought- I thought I was protecting the people of the Roughworks from the dangers of the Mistwoods. But in reality, all I did was separate the people.
- Quill: Fruma needs all the help it can get once this is all over. Everyone will need to cooperate to save the province from destroying itself without a ruler.
- The dialogue options return here.
- Quill: I'll see you around, Player.
- The dialogue ends here.
Talking to Azael again:
- Azael: Anything on your mind?
- What's the plan after this?
- Azael: I might hand the responsibilities for liberating Fruma to the young ones.
- Azael: I've lived long enough and honestly, retirement sounds rather nice.
- The dialogue options return here.
- Azael: Good bye, Player.
- The dialogue ends here.
After talking to all three groups, Sui arrives in the safe zone.
- Sui: ...Player. Hey.
Zeph runs over to Sui.
- Sui: I'm... ready to go.
- Is Rex alright?
- Sui: She, um... she is. S-Sovereign Zhiraok, he, um, took her to a medic. And... went to try to get control of the army.
- Sui: ...I don't want to think about him. Or- or Soosu. I don't... like that everything's just- j-just okay now. Because of a common enemy.
- Sui: So... later. I'll think about it later. After we're d-
- Zeph: Sui!!! I- I- I heard about what you g...guys did!! You st- st- stopped the Queen!!!
- Sui: ...yeah. Rex and Player did. I... didn't.
- Zeph: What? Sui, you he- held back the lake's water from fl- fl- flooding the Auburn Forest!! If it wasn't for y...you, then-
- Sui: It doesn't MATTER! While I was stuck h-holding back the flood, I- I couldn't help fight!! Again - AGAIN!!! - someone got hurt because I COULDN'T BE THERE!!!
Zeph hops back in shock.
- Sui: Rex. She... she died, Zeph, I felt it. For a minute, I was holding her- her cold, LIFELESS BODY in my hands, and- a-and it was like I was there again. With... M-Mora.
- Sui: ...I failed again. I told myself, if I was STRONGER, if I was BETTER, it WOULDN'T HAPPEN AGAIN!! And it DID!!! Even if she got better, even if she's not dead, it's still MY FAULT!!!
- Zeph: ...
- Zeph: A- and if you were able to s...save Rex, but the dam broke... and all th- those people died instead... would that have been b- be- better?
- Zeph: I've b...been thinking about it, ever since Player t- told me... if- if I had been th- there, a- and not here, could I have st...stopped it...? A- an extra pair of eyes...
- Zeph: B- but I was here, instead, a- a- and because of that, I was able to m...make sure Yuman survived! If it were the other way around... I'd feel the same!!
- Sui: She's still out there. Through that rift. We're going to kill her, Zeph.
- Zeph: ...right now? Sui, are you s...sure? Controlling that much water, it mu- must have drained your mana... can you st...still fight?
- Sui: ...yes. I... it doesn't feel like I've used any magic at all. I, um, don't feel tired at all.
- Sui: Ever since the Mistwoods, the ocean's... grown. Or... no, that's wrong - it was always this big, I just... couldn't see it before.
- Sui: It's... mana, but it's not mine. It's... all the strands, the threads, tied up in everything. And I can, um, use as much as I want.
- Zeph: ...okay. So y- you- you're going now...?
- Sui: Yes.
- Zeph: Th- then let me join you! Things are c...calmer here, now, so- so they should be fine w- with- without me!
- Sui: ...okay, Zeph. We could use the help.
Yusanu runs out of the bank.
- Yusanu: Sui, Player, Zeph!
- Yusanu: I- I did it! I finally, finally, FINALLY did it!!!
- Sui: Um... did what?
- Yusanu: The Resonance Weaver - I had theories before, workable theories, but I wasn't sure. But I am now!!
- Yusanu: It was in the glyphs! They don't just call upon the five elements, they ARE the five elements! Like Soosu's writings about matter - building blocks of reality!
- Yusanu: The Weaver pulls on these strands - the physical makeup of our reality - and uses them to... well... do mostly anything.
- Yusanu: I used it before to make that... corruption visible. But with enough experimenting, you could do more than just visualizing it.
- Yusanu: Thread it into something else, or change the course of its flow, or... or even bind it to something physical!
- Is that what the Queen did?
- Sui: ...I didn't see her transform. What did it look like?
- Fractured shards of porcelain stone. Seeping red chaos flowing from the cracks in the shell.
- Zeph: S...so, what, that's how she b- became... human?
- Sui: ...I don't really care. Yusanu, can it help with our... um, our rift problem?
- Yusanu: Uh... maybe. To- to be clear, the Weaver is still... hard to use. If we had people more familiar with the glyphs... it could be very powerful. But we don't.
- Yusanu: In theory... it should be able to close the rifts. Would just- ha, need to weave reality shut again. But... I don't know how.
- Sui: Um... S-Soveriegn Soosu might know. She and- a-and Zhiraok are... no longer against us. F-for now, at least.
- Yusanu: ...got it. I'll see what I can do..
- Yusanu: You're... heading in to deal with the source, aren't you?
- Zeph: We are.
- Yusanu: Then... good luck. Don't die. Be careful. We'll hold the fort while you're gone, until everything stabilizes, at least.
- Sui: ...yeah. We should get going. See you when it's all over.
Head to the Royal Palace at [-1601, 128, -772].
Talking to Sui again:
- Sui: Hm?
- How do you feel?
- Sui: It's fine. My mana has never been stronger. You don't have to worry about me.
- No, how do you feel?
- Sui: Awful, empty, sad, enraged... Does that paint you a clear picture? But I can't afford that. Not, now.
- The dialogue options return here.
- What's the plan after this?
- Sui: I... I still haven't given it much thought.
- Sui: I'll think about it if- when we kill her for good.
- The dialogue options return here.
- Sui: I'll be right behind you.
- The dialogue ends here.
Talking to Yusanu again:
- Yusanu: Yes, any questions?
- How did you figure it out?
- Yusanu: To be honest. If it weren't for your information about worlds beyond ours, I would never have figured it out. Besides, Sui taught me a lot about magic which helped...
- Yusanu: At the end of the day, Soosu has taught me to... think outside of the box and I have gotten quite used to how she builds her inventions.
- Yusanu: I haven't been able to test my theory on the use but I'm 98.6% certain it will work.
- What's the plan after this?
- Yusanu: I have a lot I want to do. I feel like a world of opportunity has opened for me. I want to travel the world, explore the other provinces and share research.
- Yusanu: But more importantly, I heard from Quill that Soosu is alive. I think- I think she should join me on my travels. Once the aftermath has calmed down a bit.
- Yusanu: Stay safe out there.
- The dialogue ends here.
After approaching the destination, Tasim walks into the path:
The interaction changes depending on which dialogue option was chosen when Tasim asked the player to kill him, and if the Player told Tasim about Aledar's death in  Queen's Recruit.
"I can't. Not again", "I won't lose another friend", "It's not too late for you", or "Live with your mistakes" =
- Sovereign Tasim: Player.
- Tasim.
- Sovereign Tasim: I've.. done what I can. Reached as many people as I could, with the time I had. The rest...
- Sovereign Tasim: The gendarme won't listen to me... their commander's disappeared somewhere, and they won't tell me anything about it.
- Did not tell Tasim:
- Sovereign Tasim: ...I thought she understood me. I still think she did, but... it doesn't make up for this. Any of this.
- Sovereign Tasim: The cracks are finally showing... I always knew they were there, I just. Told myself they weren't the end of the world. Ha.
- Told Tasim:
- Sovereign Tasim: ...it's strange. For all that I thought she understood me... maybe she never really did. How much of what she said was real? How much of it wasn't?
- Sovereign Tasim: The cracks had been showing for a while, I just... chose to push them aside. I didn't think I would make it out of this, so... why push back on it?
- Sovereign Tasim: ...I still think her plan would have worked to stop the end of the world. She had the method and the means...
- Sovereign Tasim: But it was never her priority. She was always focused on... this. Keeping Fruma perfect, and under her control.
- Sovereign Tasim: ...does any of this matter? I guess not. We've found ourselves here, either way. Nothing to do but... keep moving forward.
Sui walks through the wall and sends out a trail of icy spikes at Tasim.
- Sui: YOU!!! Player, what is HE doing here?! After he- he- he KILLED Rex, so why is he HERE?!
- Sui: I should... I should kill you. You- you'd DESERVE it, for everything!!!
- Sovereign Tasim: ...
Sui runs up a hits Tasim with a water-powered punch. Zeph walks out of the wall and stands nearby.
- Sovereign Tasim: ...maybe. Maybe I do. But I can't just leave my mistakes for other people to deal with.
Sui summons a single icicle in front of herself, aimed directly at Tasim.
- Sovereign Tasim: I'm here to help with the Queen. I have to see it through, or... or I've made these mistakes for nothing.
- Sui: ...right. Of course you want to help, what else would you do? Sigh. Everyone who hurts me, always... out of reach.
Sui gets rid of her icicle.
- Sui: Fine. Fine. Until this is done... I'll... ignore it.
- Sui: I can't wait for this nightmare to be over...
- Sovereign Tasim: ...for what it's worth, I
- Sui: I don't want to hear it. I don't care what you have to say for yourself.
- Sui: Come on. Let's go.
- Sovereign Tasim: ...
- Tasim.
- Sovereign Tasim: Player. I'm here, aren't I? Sigh... Look at it all. What a mess. The sky itself is cracked and broken!!
- Sovereign Tasim: Everything she said... it was true. She had a plan to stop the end of the world. She had the method and the means...
- Sovereign Tasim: But she was always focused on this, wasn't she? Fruma was her priority. Keeping it perfect and under her control...
- Sovereign Tasim: Maybe I should have seen it. Maybe I did. But it doesn't matter, does it? We've found ourselves here and now either way.
Sui walks through the wall and sends out a trail of icy spikes at Tasim.
- Sui: YOU!!! Player, what is HE doing here?! After he- he- he KILLED Rex, so why is he HERE?!
- Sui: I should... I should kill you. You- you'd DESERVE it, for everything!!!
- Sovereign Tasim: ...
Sui runs up a hits Tasim with a water-powered punch. Zeph walks out of the wall and stands nearby.
- Sovereign Tasim: ...I would, wouldn't I? But there are bigger things to worry about right now.
Sui summons a single icicle in front of herself, aimed directly at Tasim.
- Sovereign Tasim: You're going after the Queen, right? I want to help.
- Sui: Help. You want to... fine. Fine!! Of course you get to just... turn around and be good now. Of course...
Sui gets rid of her icicle.
- Sui: It's fine. It's fine! Until this is done... I'll... ignore it.
- Sui: I can't wait for this nightmare to be over...
- Sovereign Tasim: ...I just want to make things right.
- Sui: Well... you CAN'T!! Her arm is gone, FOREVER, and it's YOUR fault. She would have been DEAD, if it weren't for- f-for Zhiraok!
- Sui: So... so I don't care. If you're going to help with the Queen... fine. But I don't want to see you ever again after we're done.
- Sui: Player, Zeph, come on. Let's go.
- Sovereign Tasim: ...
- Tasim?
- Sovereign Tasim: I've been thinking. About all of it. After everything that's happened, everything she's done - everything I've done - it wouldn't be right to turn away.
- Sovereign Tasim: It's all broken, breaking... and maybe it always was. And this is just the truth finally being visible.
- Sovereign Tasim: ...I just wanted to do something about it all. About the realms... but also about Fruma. But... I was never going to make any real change, was I?
- Sovereign Tasim: I'll help you take her down. It's only right. After that... I don't know.
Sui walks through the wall and sends out a trail of icy spikes at Tasim.
- Sui: YOU!!! Player, what is HE doing here?! After he- he- he KILLED Rex, so why is he HERE?!
- Sui: I should... I should kill you. You- you'd DESERVE it, for everything!!!
- Sovereign Tasim: ...
Sui runs up a hits Tasim with a water-powered punch. Zeph walks out of the wall and stands nearby.
- Sui: W-well? What do you have to say for yourself?!
Sui summons a single icicle in front of herself, aimed directly at Tasim.
- Sovereign Tasim: ...you're right.
- Sui: Then- th-then... I'll...
Sui gets rid of her icicle.
- Sui: ...I can't. I... I can't do it.
- Sui: After everything... after EVERYTHING, I get a CHANCE to- to- to get back at s-someone who's hurt me, and- and- a-and I CAN'T DO IT?!
- Sui: ...whatever. WAHTEVER!! Let's just go deal with the STUPID Queen!!
- Sui: I can't wait for this nightmare to be over...
- Sovereign Tasim: ...I'm sorry.
- Sui: I don't care.
- Sui: Player, Zeph, let's just... go.
Enter the Royal Palace at [-1624, 143, -707].
Talking to Sui:
Talking to Tasim:
- Sovereign Tasim: ...no more excuses.
Talking to Zeph:
- Zeph: How is- is this going to go?
Upon approaching the destination: Two can be seen standing in the entrance with her back to the stairs. Tasim, Sui, and Zeph also head up to meet her.
- Sovereign Two: ...
- Sovereign Two: And so, the cards fall. The shards collapse as decisions are made and paths are chosen. What a destructive end it has turned out to be.
Two turns around to face the group.
- Sovereign Two: In retrospect, it seems an inevitability... each decision branching out from the last. What was the weight that sent it over the edge? The tournament? The selection?
- Sovereign Two: Would you have been the better choice? No. Having seen now what I have, I am only more certain. But perhaps it could have saved us all this mess.
- Sovereign Two: Oh, Anathema... what a mess you've left in your wake...
- Sovereign Two: You will face no resistance from me. I do not have a death wish.
Two walks to get closer, and Tasim takes a step back.
- Sovereign Two: So go on, fellow Scion. Put an end to this.
- Sovereign Tasim: Don't call me
- Sovereign Two: Sovereign, then? Deny it all you like, but you chose to take on that role.
- Sovereign Two: As with each of us, that mark remains. It cannot be so easily discarded. It cannot be forgotten.
- Sovereign Two: Her power gifted, drawn through the mark... and she has given much away in pursuit of this freedom, hasn't she...
- Sovereign Two: How much of it remains now, I wonder? Enough to guarantee her victory? Or, perhaps... little enough to grant you a chance of success...?
- Sovereign Two: Hm! I cannot say for certain. Of all things, this variable yet eludes me. The shards are inconclusive - equally favourable and not.
Two looks at Sui.
- Sovereign Two: But you... an unexpected variable, though not unwelcome. A naturally-born manaweaver! I thought I'd never see the day.
- Sui: Wh... what?
- Sovereign Two: ...naturally, you do not know the gift you possess. That knowledge was lost with the old world, after all. Will you grow into that power? Or will you allow it to consume you?
- Sovereign Two: Only time will tell.
Two looks at the player.
- Sovereign Two: And you. Do you remember what I asked you? If not Her, then who?
- Sovereign Two: ...
Two looks back at the group.
- Sovereign Two: From here, there are no easy paths - your decisions have buried all of those. For Fruma, for the world... each step towards a better future will be a bitter, hard-fought victory.
Two looks back at the player.
- Sovereign Two: But perhaps it will prove worthwhile, after all! You've surprised me once already - who's to say you won't do it again? An uncertain future... what an exciting prospect.
Two summons a mirror behind herself.
- Sovereign Two: I hope to see you all once more, somewhere down this winding road of ours.
Two departs through the mirror.
Talk to Merloni in Nemract at [210, 37, -2150]
Explore the pit at [356, 58, -1914] and find the shrine

lines.title: finding the hidden shrine
lines.text:
Jump into the pit. You will be taken to an underground area; you must reach the end to find the shrine. First, you must do some simple parkour across stone platforms, although it is easy to skip it using movement spells. You will then be taken to a room with a river of lava and the shrine in the center, avoid the mobs and jump into the shrine. 
The mobs will then be appeased and the river will change to normal water; you can exit through the way you came in and return to Merloni.
Go back to Nemract and tell Merloni that you succeeded
Talk to Voer at [-2103, 59, -5427].
Dialogue:
- Voer: Hello! Hmm, armour, weapon, look of grim despair... You must be from the Wynn province!
- Voer: My name is Voer, and I'm an exotic plant merchant. I sell all kinds of, uh, perfectly legal goods to the magicians of Gavel.
- Voer: Lately, this Decay has been making business rather tough. The magical plants that used to grow here are dying.
- Voer: The need for magic has never been as big as it is now, and without supplies, the magicians of the swamp simply cannot operate!
- Voer: I need Death Whistle in particular. It's not as deadly as it sounds, I promise- the name's just archaic, if I recall that from that- er, my book.
- Voer:  It is a rather rare plant with all sorts of mystical properties, so much so that it can animate objects around it!
- Voer:  Look for the highest mountain in the swamp south-east from here. The Decay hasn't reached the peaks yet, you see!
Find the mountain at [-2064, 56, -5190] and a way up on it.
Go to the top of the mountain and get 1 Black Whistle Leaf.
There will be a Death Whistle item mob that you must kill, and then there will be a Cyclone Blue flower that will send you to an area near Voer.
Return to Voer at [-2103, 59, -5427] with [1 Death Whistle Leaf].
Dialogue:
- Lari: You, Voer! Inconsiderate thief!
- Lari: You've no idea what you even have done, do you? Your thoughtless actions will cost lives!
- Voer: Uhm... Excuse me? What do you want, elf girl? We're in the middle of a deal here?
- Lari: You sold Pink Pelulite! Have you forgotten its enraging properties? Or shall I read from that herbology book you "found" in my camp?
- Voer: Wait, wh-what? A Pink PELULITE!? I sold that woman a Pink PELUTE for her luck charms! How dare- wait... wait, Pink Pelute has rounder petals... Oh no.
- Lari: You can't even say for certain. This kind of carelessness has no place! If you refuse to exercise the proper thought and caution, then those around you suffer.
- Lari: I must... make a difficult choice, and leave this job to you. I've other things to tend to, though it pains me to leave a life in another's hands. Remember this, villager!

- Voer: Aaah, this is a disaster! Human, please, Pink Pelulite acts quickly and intensely... Follow the pink trail on the ground, the flowers shed their petals. Get it back before something bad happens!
Follow the path of residue to the buyer’s cave.
- Witch: Ah, um, come back later please! Something strange is happening!
- Witch: My body is a bit, um, not-in-my-control right now! I'd rather not hurt anyone!
Remove the flower from the woman in the cave.
- She dropped the Pink Pelulite flower! You need to return this to Voer immediately.
Dialogue:
- Voer: You're back, I see... and you're shedding petals! You got the Pink Pelulite back?
- Voer: And what of the woman who bought it? Was she...?
- Voer: Oh, thank goodness! You got in there in time. She's a regular of mine- and a bit of a looker, too. That Lari was right, to some extent, at least...
- Voer: I did take her book, and I should be more careful in the future, regarding this... but I can't just quit selling the herbs.
- Voer: I need an income, and the swamp isn't exactly the most resource-rich region here! Especially not any more.
- Voer: And how dare she just walk away like that! It's a good thing you were around, human, otherwise... well, I would not think about it.
- Voer: Regardless, you helped me greatly. Got me my supplies and saved the life of a regular of mine, so I've got a gift for you!
- Voer: I'll offer you a sampler of my stock. Everything here is pre-primed to be safe for brewing, so there won't be any mishaps like today!
Talk to Twendle at The House of Twain at [12, 79, -456]
Bring 1 Twain Journal to Twendle

lines.title: how to find the journal
lines.text:
- Enter the house, walk into the dining room on the right and then to the servant's area right by the table. Press the wooden button on the wall at [123, 75, -367] to open the iron trapdoor at [128, 74, -358]. Quickly jump down the hole opened under the trapdoor to reach the cellar.
*In the cellar, place items on 2 wooden pressure plates behind the barrels, at [129, 63, -345] and [115, 63, -376], to access the secret room through the doorway at [105, 63, -360]. Inside the secret room, there is a sign saying "Pay tribute to the eyes of the beast, it shall guide you".
*Exit the secret room and return to the entrance of the mansion.
*For the next part of the puzzle, you will first need to get a Ghostly Cap. To do this you must find three ghosts in the mansion (prepare for jumpscares with each one):
**The first is on the third floor, across from the stairs you go up to get to this floor, at [120, 84, -392].
**The second is at the end of the hall on the third floor, in the last room, at [118, 84, -332].
**The third is in the front left "garden" area of the mansion, at [97, 77, -378]. To get there, you have to go up the main stairs and then walk down the hall to the left, and go through the door behind the stairs that lead to the third floor. 
*Once you have all three items, take them to the cauldron room on the third floor and drop the three items in the hopper in the middle of the room, at [128, 86, -358]. A skeleton will then appear and drop an unidentified Ghostly Cap.
*Identify the Ghostly Cap right outside the mansion to wear it for the next section.
*Note: If you already have a Ghostly Cap, you can wear that one and do not have to do any previous steps in order for the quest to work. 
*In the dining room, the carpets near the fireplace resemble the face of a wither skeleton, with the two eyes marked by dark red particles. As the sign from earlier suggests, insert emeralds (by right-clicking) into both eyes to open the secret room behind the fireplace.
*Once in the secret room, walk to the back and into the painting at [112, 75, -295]. The sign says "Give the riches you hold to the man whos house he once owned, and it will open a grave that does not belong".
*As the sign suggests, click with an emerald on the soul sand at the grave in the room. Then, quickly run out of the mansion and turn to the left to the small graveyard in front of the mansion (not the large one in the back). The quartz grave (the one that does not belong) at [66, 71, -314] should be open. You must be wearing the ghostly helmet at this point in order to enter the small graveyard.
*Jump into the hole at the quartz grave and follow the cave down.
*At the end of the cave you will reach a room labelled "The Prison Of Souls". A sign near the exit of the room states "The obsessions of the souls are the keys to freedom. -Mael". You must find the code to exit the room based on the number of decorative block items in each cell.
**Cell 1 "Retenal" has 5 glowstone lamps, cell 2 "Gitsag" has 7 leaves, cell 3 "Nnebrian" has 3 ender chests, and cell 4 "Kal-el" has 2 emerald ores. Put in order, the code is thus 5732.
*Once you enter the code, a door opens and you can fight the Phantom Twain to obtain the journal. Step on the quartz block in the back to leave the cave.
Talk to Wirt in Troms at [-820, 94, -1040]
Dialogue:
- Wirt: Not so fast, you!
- Wirt: My dad said I can't let any strangers through this passage!
- Wirt: If you want access, talk to him, he's the recruiter of the town! His name is Ildan. He's just southwest of here.
Find Ildan in Troms at [-870, 94, -1034] and ask to be a member of the town
Dialogue:
- Ildan: Oh! So you want to become a member of this town?
- Ildan: You will have to help us first, of course!
- Ildan: I'm sure you've noticed, but there is a tribe camp not too far from here.
- Ildan: They used to have a powerful chief, but he eventually died in battle.
- Ildan: The tribe couldn't bear the fact that he was dead. They performed some unethical necromancy spell on him.
- Ildan: They quickly realized that is was a bad idea, so they locked him in a tomb.
- Ildan: He keeps reviving his minions and it's causing quite some problems to our army.
- Ildan: You can access the tomb from a sacrificial shrine, I've heard, but I'm not sure how. There are probably hints nearby the shrine.
- Ildan: Bring me back 1 Antic Bead as a proof of its death, and I will let you become a citizen.
- Ildan: I've marked the direction to the shrine in your book. Remember, there should be hints right nearby the shrine. Good luck.
Search for clues near [-712, 57, -628] and bring back 1 Antic Bead to Ildan.

lines.title: Spoiler
lines.text: Go to the herb cave and kill Dead Miner until you have 4 Zombie Eye
Dialogue:
- Ildan: Impressive! You got the bead!
- Ildan: Well, welcome to this town, adventurer! You are now officially a citizen.
- Ildan: Oh, but before you go! I do have a few things to say. First, about the beads here.
- Ildan: The tribesmen accept these as currency, so if you collect enough, I've heard they can offer you powerful masks.
- Ildan: Second, about the shrine. Now, this is just a rumor, but apparently that tomb is not unique.
- Ildan: There are supposed to be a bunch of these altars scattered around the province, even in Gavel too!
- Ildan: If true, you should look for them. While the fights will be tough, I would imagine great rewards could be gotten from them!
- Ildan: Anyway, I've talked enough. I'm proud to have such a powerful fighter join our town! I wish you luck, friend!

intro.text: Tower of Ascension is one of the most difficult quests in Wynncraft, and arguably the most difficult in the province of Wynn. It will test the player's skills throughout series of fights that might require the player to request help from others. The quest starts at Tower of Ascension where they have to talk to Ankou, who gives you the task to clear every single floor of the tower. (Note: Some enemy health points may be outdated)

lines.text: Ankou is the NPC who starts and ends the quest, and provides the only dialogue.  The floormaster on each level of the Tower will only tell you that it needs tokens, or that you can proceed.
First
- Ankou: Hehehe... Hello there.
- Ankou: Welcome to the Tower of Ascension!
- Ankou: I challenge you to reach the final floor!
- Ankou: Have you got what it takes to conquer it?
- Ankou: Perhaps you would like to know the layout of the tower first? Hehehehe...
- Ankou: There are 7 floors in this tower, each with ten levels.
- Ankou: Each floor has nine regular levels and one boss level.
- Ankou: To pass a regular level, you must collect five tokens from the challenge on that level, and one token from boss levels.
- Ankou: After you beat a whole floor, you will return here and you can begin the next one...
- Ankou: So, what do you say? Hehehe...
- Ankou: Turn left and head to the first floor...if you dare...
Intermediate Stages
Intermediate Stages have the following pattern:
- Begin the Xth Floor
- Collect 5 tokens and hand them to the Floor Master [Floor X, Level Y] (Repeats 9 times per set)
- Collect the boss token and hand it to the Floor Master [Floor X, Level 10]
- Floormaster: Well done, adventurer, you have successfully completed this floor! You may proceed.
Final Stage
- Ankou: You have completed my tower, I see...
- Ankou: Did you enjoy Death? Many challengers certainly did. Her power is... unmatched, hehehe...
- Ankou: And you... You are unlike all of them, yes? Few have managed to ascend these floors.
- Ankou: A tower of madness, fueled by Death herself... Quite a challenge, yes?
- Ankou: You have joined us now, champion... Few can claim this victory as their own. Fewer still have held their mind.
- Ankou: For this honor... A reward, for you. You have truly earned it... Hehehehe...

There are 7 floors each of them containing 10 levels, for a total of 70 rooms in the tower. At the first 9 levels for each floor you have to kill mobs to receive 5 tokens, which you'll have to give to the Floormaster to let you ascend to the next level. In the tenth level of each floor is a powerful boss, which must be killed once to unlock the next floor. If you die on a given level for each floor, your progress will be saved and you can skip each level by just walking to the teleport point on the far side of the room.
Floor 1=
- The XP reward of the Tower of Ascension quest scales with your level and is supposed to be finished at around level 70-75. You will get significantly less XP if you finish it at level 40.

- Floors 1's Boss, Snow Bear, has an attack interval of 1s and only does an arrow storm every 25s. Strafe the boss to avoid the normal attacks and use your mobility spell whenever you see the boss charge up their skill—indicated by white particles surrounding them and a red timer appearing above their head.

- Floor 2's boss, Argaddon, lacks ranged attacks and has a very slow charging meteor. Kite the boss around and try to keep your distance and don't immediately go back to where you were previously standing as the meteors take a bit to land.

- Floor 3's boss, Witch Doctor, will be strafing around you in a counter-clockwise fashion and will create a clone every once and a while. Keep in mind the boss's clones can heal ~20k of the boss's health and can do so in quick succession. Since the boss strafes around you its very easy to get it stuck on the walls where you can dish out your spells safely. It's reccomended to get it stuck in the spawn space as the boss has a harder time charging out of there.
- Floor 4's boss, Guardian, is very mobile and charges very often. To counter this, strafe around the center of the arena and attack the boss whenever it gets near you.

- Floor 5's boss, Chained Beast, is a lot faster than the previous bosses so it is suggested that you have some walk speed from your gear/ability tree. Kiting around the arena and moving towards the center whenever you see the boss charge up its skill to dodge its charge will make the fight a lot more comfortable.

- Floor 6's boss, Alkevo, has an absurdly short attack interval, moves incredibly fast and will self-destruct if not defeated in a timely manner. This makes it hard to outrun and require you to deal a decent amount of damage. The boss itself gets stuck very easily so if you hug the left wall of the spawn chambers immedietly when spawning in, the boss will get stuck in front of it allowing you to damage it through the wall with your spells. The boss will also be able to damage you with its explosions so take a few steps back while still hugging the wall if possible.

- Floor 7's boss, Death, will very slowly strafe around you in a clockwise manner and will summon bosses from the previous chambers as the fight goes on. Only one of each boss from the previous chambers can be summoned at once. However, since there are 6 other bosses, her fight can get a bit overwhelming. Death herself can get stuck on the walls of the arena fairly easily, but moving too far from her will cause her to no longer be stuck. You will need to kill her minions before trying to kill her since they will prove to be quite the challenge to ignore. Try to get Death to hit the other bosses enough to draw agro away from you if you cant get rid of all of them together, otherwise just spam spells to kill the minions while slowly whittling away at Death's health bar.

- Some easy to get armour for this fight would be: Clearsight Spectacles, Morph Steel, Morph Iron, Morph Gold, Morph Topaz, Morph Emerald, any Bracelet and Morph Ruby. This makes you fairly tanky allowing you to worry less while about getting hit while dealing damage.

- Good weapon choices for this fight would be, no matter the class, Bob's Mythic Weapons if you have already completed the Reincarnation quest. Other than those weapons there are also a few more weapons more specific to your class.
- For Archer use, Corrupted Witherhead's Elbow, Maelstrom or Redbeard's Hand Cannon.
- For Warrior use, Nightmare or Scythe.
- For Mage use, Depth, Warden or Stave of the Legends.
- For Assassin use, Amadeus, Regar, Relic Daggers or Sharpened Seaglass.
- For Shaman use, Ghorme Ndaizma, Paranoia, Infernus Aeterna or Rusted root.
- Though the Champion Armour set is received upon completion of the quest, the rewards display doesn't include it.
Category:Quests
Talk to Zhight of Zhight Island at [-542, 38, -2755]
Dialogue:
- Zhight: Hello, esteemed tourist sir or madame! I see you have found my illustrious resort, Zhight Island!
- Zhight: Normally, you'd need a reservation to stay here, but our human visitors are ALWAYS welcome! Ehm...
- Zhight: ...w-well, actually...wait, no, it's nothing, nothing, friend! I guarantee you'll enjoy your stay here!
- Zhight: Even if m-my usual supplies haven't arrived in weeks, I, um, I'm TOTALLY sure we can accommodate for you!
- Zhight: We can just...um...w-well, I won't impose on you, dearest most welcomest traveller, no sir! Or madame!
- Zhight: B-But, if, perchance, you were to, um...happen to find my supplier, Phief, who hasn't come around in weeks the bas-
- Zhight: I! I mean! Nothing, nothing! Just, ehm, our extra reliable supplier often stops by Mage Island for supplies...
- Zhight: S-So, if you just happen to stop by there after your lovely stay here, and tell him to get off his sorry butt and send me my supplies that'd be just peachy!
Look for Phief at Mage Island
Dialogue:
- Phief: Hello there. I see Zhight has sent you, correct?
- Phief: I do hope he isn't mad at me. I fully intended to bring the supplies to him.
- Phief: But things took a turn for the worst quickly, and I no longer have access to my ship.
- Phief: A madman jumped onto my ship, overpowered me, and held me hostage!
- Phief: He was telling me how he wanted to "take back what was stolen from him", and it looked like he was heading to Maro Peaks.
- Phief: I have no clue whether he was deranged, paranoid, or if someone really did take something from him.
- Phief: I am certain of one thing. Nobody is going to sail my boat but me. I took my first chance to escape, broke the controls.
- Phief: And I swam back to land, here. Problem is, I haven't exactly decided how I'll get the ship back for myself.
- Phief: Maybe you can help me with that. The ship should still be stuck, due north of here. I'd love to get my sea legs back.
Find Phief's ship, and return it to its rightful owner
Dialogue:
- Tirt: He told you what?! That fumbleknuckle...
- Tirt: We didn't steal the ship from Phief, we were taking back what he stole from us years ago!
- Tirt: He attacked us on our way home to Maro Peaks, kicked us off the boat, and sailed it to who-knows-where.
- Tirt: We didn't think we would ever get it back, until we started seeing him sailing to that doofbumble Zhight.
- Tirt: Luckily, he decided to claim an island so close to Maro Peaks, or else we would have never seen him.
- Tirt: My father started following him with a small sailboat he made, and decided on the perfect place to attack.
- Tirt: But then Phief just had to throw a hissy fit and leave us stranded here.
- Tirt: My father took a paddleboat back to Maro Peaks to gather supplies. He took the cargo the ship had with him.
- Tirt: If you need that, you should go talk to him. His name is Czytash.
Get Zhight's supplies from Czytash at Maro Peaks
Dialogue:
- Czytash: Ah, yes, I did find plenty o' supplies on that ship.
- Czytash: I assumed it was more of Phief's thiefed goods, so I took it home to use it myself.
- Czytash: It is Zhight's supplies you say?
- Czytash: Aye, of course it had to be that idiot's.
- Czytash: I guess me thinking he's dumber'n a box o' rocks is no reason for me to let him starve... Here, take the crate.
- Czytash: I haven't opened it yet, so everything is left exactly how he ordered it.
- Czytash: I wonder what is on that numbskull's menu, that crate smelled rancid. Almost threw it off me boat.
- Czytash: Anyways, good luck on your adventure matey.
- Czytash: Sorry, what was that? My son?
- Czytash: Ah, I figured it is about time he learned how to maneuver a boat. I fixed everything before I left.
- Czytash: When he returns, he will return a man.
- Czytash: Wait, why am I telling you this? Butt out of my personal life, and just bring the man his crate.
Give Zhight his supplies
Dialogue:
- Zhight: Ahaaa, esteemed sir! Or madame! I can't actually tell under all that armour...
- Zhight: ER! I MEAN! N-No trouble at all, esteemed visitor! We at Zhight Island Resort are always welcoming!
- Zhight: ...wait, is that the... Oh my! The supply crate! You went out and found Phief?! What an upstanding fellow you are!
- Zhight: Wait, he was a boat thief? Well, good thing you've told me, we can't have pirates here at our resort! I'll blacklist him ASAP!
- Zhight: You're only a visitor but you've been more help today than anyone else, really, I'm honestly in your debt.
- Zhight: So here! The repairs at the Zhight Grand Exchange and Zhight Treasure Tour have just finished, so you can head in and see the fruits of your labor!
- Zhight: And, as a token of my thanks, some exclusive currency for our resort, Zhight Money, on the house and just for you! I hope you enjoy your stay!
Speak to Burtur at [-1025, 47, -5302]
Some Rejuvenated Corpses will appear and start attacking the town during the rest of the dialogue.
Once Burtur finishes speaking, the player and Burtur will have to fight waves of zombies to defend Gelibord. After surviving for 30 seconds, the zombies will be defeated.
Check in with Burtur about the attack at [-1025, 50, -5302]
To continue the dialogue, walk over to the pyre around [-998 47 -5273].
Talking to Burtur again:
Find the body of the Order's mage in Gelibord's graveyard at [-999, 49, -5340]

There is a Rusty Shovel near the graveyard's entrance that can be used to dig up several graves in the graveyard. There are five graves that can be dug up; the first four will always release a regular Rejuvenated Corpse or Revived Gelibord Farmer, while the final grave that is dug up will have the mage.
- It looks like the revived mage dropped some kind of talisman...
Locate the chapel mentioned by the talisman, or return to Burtur for assistance.
Note: Visiting Burtur will play the following dialogue and update the quest step.
Talking to Burtur again:
-> Investigate the Order's chapel northwest of Gelibord at [-1125, 45, -5489]
Interacting with the door will show the following message:
- The door shakes slightly, and an inscription appears on the wood...
- Burtur mentioned something about the water from the Pit leaking into the river... Perhaps you could collect some from a stream nearby?
Solve the crypt's riddle to 'bring the water of life anew' to the graves.
Go to the nearby shack at [-1099, 42, -5456] and get a bucket from the floor. Right-click the water outside to obtain a pail of Lazarus Water.
- Perhaps you could use this water to revive some of the graves around the crypt...
Revive the people in the tombs with the Lazarus Water and complete their tasks.
The dead in the graves around the crypt can be resurrected in any order.
Blue-Flag Grave
Go to the grave at [-1132, 43, -5511] with the  Lazarus Water to revive Lord Plaatic the Kind.
Talking to Lord Plaatic again:
- That's most of the ghouls killed, you should .
Interacting with the grave again:
- Lord Plaatic's tomb is cold and empty.
Red-Flag Grave
Go to the grave at [-1124, 44, -5465] with the  Lazarus Water to revive Sir Pigglesworth the Thirty-Fifth.
Talking to Sir Pigglesworth again:
Go east to the Lich's Tower. The Wedding Band is found in a hole outside at [-1068, 40, -5494].
Interacting with the grave again:
- Sir Pigglesworth's tomb is silent and still. Seems he thought that "Til death do us part" was for quitters.
Green-Flag Grave
Go to the grave at [-1172, 44, -5470] with the  Lazarus Water to revive Uggword Pollywaggon the Murderous, who will instantly spawn as a hostile boss.
- Well, you'll just have to hope that putting Uggword to rest counts as his blessing to open the crypt.
Interacting with the grave again:
- There's no sound from within the bloodstained grave... Looks like Uggword's getting his...beauty...death.
Yellow-Flag Grave
Go to the grave at [-1160, 44, -5511] with the  Lazarus Water to revive Poclo Wabblebuff of Gelibord. She will ask you to feed her cat.
Talking to Poclo again:
Poclo's house is found by Hans at [-1105, 42, -5381]. Mrs. Fluffles is found in the basement.
- Looks like this was the house Poclo was talking about... you should check inside.
- Mrs. Fluffles doesn't look to be in the best of shape...
- [1] Use the Lazarus Water on Mrs. Fluffles
- [2] Leave her be
The quest is unaffected by the option chosen here.
- [1] [She's fine]
- [2] [She's dead]

The task is finished after telling Poclo that Mrs. Fluffles is fine. Alternatively, telling Poclo that Mrs. Fluffles is dead causes her to become a hostile enemy that must be defeated to complete the task.
Interacting with the grave again:
- Poclo's grave is eerily silent.
Open the crypt door at [-1125, 45, -5489]
- That's all of the tasks finished... You should .
Investigate the crypt's inner chamber at [-1150, 34, -5489]
- It's an old book, rather ripped and torn...
Find the entrance to the Lazarus Pit at [-957, 47, -5438]
- Looks like there's some debris blocking the path, but perhaps you could blast it away with a  up close?
Use any spell near the debris to open the path.
Follow the path to the Lazarus pit at [-957, 47, -5438] and enter the Pit.
- This must be the entrance to the Lazarus Pit... Seems like it goes down rather far. Better jump in.
Follow the cave to find the Lazarus Pit.
Kill the 3 waves of mobs that spawn to open the way.
- Looks like the way down to the Lazarus Pit has been opened up...
Find a way to block off the water pillar in the Lazarus Pit.
Dialogue:
- Is the water going... upwards? You should look around for a way to cut it off.

lines.title: solving the water puzzle
lines.text: Pressing the red, pink, and purple buttons once each will create a path through which the water can flow.
Tell Burtur that you have blocked off the Lazarus Pit at [-1025, 47, -5302]
- Looks like you managed to block off the Pit from the river... You should tell Burtur what you've done.
Talk to Kelight at the entrance of the Temple of the Legends, close to Troms at [-693, 68, -993]
- [1] I'm very, very stubborn.
- [2] I have a lot of money.
- [3] Well, I'm already a Legend. So you should just let me in.
- [4] If you think I'm not impressive, why should I bother convincing you?
- [5] I guess you shouldn't.
Stage 1.5
-> Find a way to get Kelight to allow you entry into the Temple of the Legends at [-693, 68, -993].
- [1] I'm very, very stubborn.
- [1] I'm still very stubborn.
- [1] I'm not going to quit.
- [2] I have a lot of money.
- [3] Well, I'm already a Legend. So you should just let me in.
- [4] If you think I'm not impressive, why should I bother convincing you?
- [5] I guess you shouldn't.
Talk to Jorkin in Elkurn at [-15, 79, -1135] about Light Dust.
Find the lightdust cavern located near the Portal at [261, 39, -1359].

lines.title: finding the lightdust cavern
lines.text: The light dust cavern is located to the left of the Corruption Portal.
Retrieve Light Dust from the cave at [261, 39, -1359] and bring it back to Jorkin at [-15, 79, -1135].
There will be three sections of the cave containing three waves of mobs each. At the end, you will have to fight three minibosses simultaneously in under 180 seconds.
- This is the Light Dust that Jorkin mentioned! He said to bring it back to him...
Visit Rayshyroth on Mage Island at [846, 87, -2906] to purify the dust

lines.title: how to get to Rayshyroth
lines.text: Rayshyroth is located on a floating island above the main Mage Island, at [846, 87, -2906]. To get up, you can do a parkour starting at [885, 49, -2925].
Find the cave on Mage Island where the Sky Flux gathers at [864, 31, -2916].

lines.title: how to find the cave
lines.text: The Sky Vapor cave is just below Rayshyroth, at [850, 17, -2910].
Give Sky Vapor to Rayshyroth at [846, 87, -2906].

lines.text: Garull is located in the Creeper's Hideout in the Pigmen's Ravine. To get into the hideout, you will need to wear a Creeper Mask from Creeper Infiltration. Once you get into the hideout just like in Creeper Infiltration, you can find Garull in his room at [-918, 81, -1222].
Bring the Old Touroto Hide, Aseado Leaf, Maro's Eye Jewel, and Coral of Nelfors to Garull in the cave at [-849, 97, -1211].
Bring the Helmet of the Legends to Kelight at the entrance of the Temple of the Legends at [-692, 63, -975].
Kill the Corrupter of Worlds in the cave at [-714, 61, -963] and bring proof of its death to Kelight at [-692, 63, -975].
Once you enter the main cave, passing the second pair of Legend Guards, the following dialogue will play:

Continue through the cave. As you do, you will be able to see the Corrupter of Worlds flash by a few times; one of these times is while you are stopped at a barrier, and some Corrupted Soldiers will spawn behind you. Continue either way around the pillar, until you reach a gray leaf wall. Once you do, go through it and jump down, which will trigger the next dialogue:

Jumping down will also trigger another short appearance of the Corrupter of Worlds, and cause a large horde of Corrupted Soldiers, Warriors, Assassins, Mages, Archers, and normal Corrupteds to spawn in the room. You do not have to kill these to progress, although it can be difficult to get past them without doing so. Either way, the tunnel out of the room leads straight to the boss fight - once you stand on the soul sand at the end, the Corrupter of Worlds will walk up and break the soul sand, knocking you into the boss room.

intro.text: The Qira Hive is a long level 80-101 special quest in which the player goes through six different divisions, the first five representing each element and the last division representing Qira’s boss room. This quest will take not the standard amount of time to finish, but rather it is to be completed as the player levels since each division is based around certain levels (look in the Hive Shop to see what levels you should challenge each division at). This quest is Gavel's version of the Tower of Ascension, a quest in the Wynn Province. It takes place in the Canyon of the Lost, specifically in The Qira Hive.

There are a total of 5 division containing 10 levels (9 normal rooms and one boss room), with the 6th division being a single battle against Qira herself. For the first 5 divisions, you collect 5 tokens from killing the mobs on that level. Then, you talk to the token collector to proceed. At the boss room, you must collect one token from the boss to finish the division.

Most enemies in the Hive, particularly the bosses, tend to have pronounced elemental defenses and weaknesses. For example, Solar Vanguard is practically immune to Fire, Thunder, and Air damage, but has a massive Water weakness.

Spawn rates generally cap at 2 or 3 mobs per room, and often there is a gap between clearing out those 2-3 before the next few spawn. Regular mobs in the earlier divisions often use only one or two spells, but higher-level mobs - particularly in the Water and Fire divisions - often use multiple spells that synergize with their attack modes.
Thunder Division
The Thunder Division, ranging from level 80-83, represents the Thunder element and is the first division. Enemies here have a wide variance of attack abilities, often with high damage ranges.
A full list of the mobs in the thunder division can be found here.
Air Division
The Air Division, ranging from level 84-87, represents the Air element and is the second division. Enemies here tend to move very quickly, despite having below-average damage.
A full list of the mobs in the air division can be found here.
Earth Division
The Earth Division, ranging from level 88-91, represents the Earth element and is the third division. Enemies here generally do not move fast, but hit extremely hard. Don't get caught.
A full list of the mobs in the earth division can be found here.
Water Division

The Water Division, ranging from level 92-95, represents the Water element and is the fourth division. Enemies here often have tricky gimmicks, such as shooting invisible projectiles or sudden shifts in ability.
A full list of the mobs in the water division can be found here.
Fire Division
The Fire Division, ranging from level 96-99, represents the Fire element and is the fifth division. The enemies here are extremely powerful in all regards. Prepare your gear accordingly.
A full list of the mobs in the fire division can be found here.
Master Division

The Master Division, which is recommended for people who are level 100+, is the final division. This is a boss battle, and not like the last floor in Tower of Ascension where bosses from previous floors spawn alongside the final boss. It is advisable to bring some teammates along as it will be a tough battle against Qira, Mistress of the Hive.
A full list of the mobs in the master division can be found here.
Hive Grounds=
- The XP reward of the Qira Hive quest scales with your level and as it is supposed to be finished at around level 95-100. You will get significantly less XP if you finish it at level 80.
- If you can't find The Hive, you should walk down the trail outside of Thanos, where you should go down straight down from there and then you should take a left and you should find it.

- The tokens required to progress can be transferred between characters, which means that you can skip the fighting by using tokens that you obtained on another character on which you have already completed the quest.
- Thunder Division:
- Use a build with high mobility as the Psychomancer teleports a lot.
- The real Psychomancer always has a health bar above his head.
- Look up or down while blinded and go into second or third person view to avoid looking at clones.
- Air Division:
- Keep a good distance from Gale to avoid taking high damage from her Arrow Storm.
- Use third person view or high FOV to see where Aerial Bombardment hits and where Gale charges at.
- Earth Division:
- The Genesis-Revorse has an unavoidable instant-kill attack (Full Collapse) that happens a minute after it is below 35% HP.
- Use a movement spell the moment Genesis-Revorse uses Collapsing Arena as a falling rock appears wherever a player is at.
- Water Division:
- Move alongside the whirlpools to avoid getting hit by them during the Oceanic Judge's fight.
- Fire Division:
- Minimize DPS during the Solar Vanguard's fight to avoid overcrowding the arena with magma pillars.
- Move in a triangle-shape to avoid getting hit with the Solar Vanguard's Explosion and Charge attacks.
- Master Division:
- Use a build that has high rainbow defenses.

intro.text: is a  secret discovery located in the Highlands, focusing on the history of House Nasin, particularly the event of Gale’s flight from the Fruma province.

lines.text: Speak to the House Nasin Butler at  to obtain the keyring. The library can be found behind the large chair in the main room.
The first time interacting with the Butler will show you the following dialogue:
- Good day. Welcome to House Nasin.
- Say, you seem the industrious sort. Could I ask a favour of you?
- You see, our library is terribly disorganized. The lad whose job it was to reorder the thing walked out halfway through.
- If you would be so kind as to finish that up for me. I’d be greatly appreciative. And perhaps you’d learn something along the way, too.
- The books are meant to be sorted in chronological order. I’m sure you’ll be able to figure it out. Thank you in advance.
- Here’s the key to the library.
- The butler hands you a keyring with a single key on it: the key to the library. You can’t help but notice that it looks like there’s space for three more keys…
- +1 House Nasin Key
- [+1 Worn Keyring]
Sort the library's books like so:
- Book Three in Shelf One
- SALASAH NASIN IN 1RA
- House Nasin has always been drawn to power and truth.

- We were founded by Salasah Nasin, and we became one of Her Majesty’s earliest allies in those dark days, to join her cause in liberating Fruma from the pits of despair, bringing about the start of the Royal Age and recorded history.
- Book One in Shelf Two
- SOVEREIGN GITEPHE IN 5KA

- Sovereign Gitephe of House Nasin was the first Sovereign appointed to the seat of the Highlands in the fifth year of the Knowledge Age, becoming the Marshal of the Provincial Guard and bringing further glory to our House.
- In contrast, the ignoble House Thalas produced the unremarkable Sovereign Xima appointed to the lowly region of the Auburn Forest.
- Book Five in Shelf Three
- RANGER OF THE MISTWOODS IN 100KA
- Around the hundredth year of the Knowledge Age, the great Sovereign Gitephe was also appointed to the prestigious position of Ranger of the Mistwoods, the first ever Sovereign to do so.
- He swiftly and effectively dealt with the crises experienced in that region, continuing House Nasin’s legacy of loyalty and efficacy.
- Book Four in Shelf Four
- SOVEREIGNS GITEPHE AND RIEKE IN 205KA-75NA
- The illustrious Sovereign Gitephe finally retired after his storied career in the two hundred fifth year of the Knowledge Age.
- His mantle was passed down to Sovereign Rieke, a highly successful Sovereign in her own right, who herself retired in the seventy-fifth year of the New Age.
- Book Two in Shelf Five
- SOVEREIGN ZHIRAOK IN 98IA
- After a brief period of inconvenience to our House, our legacy of glory was renewed through the rise of Sovereign Zhiraok of House Nasin in the ninety-eighth year of the Industrial Age.
- His career as a Sovereign has been extremely successful, and with his guidance the Auburn Forest has flourished.
- Sovereign Zhiraok has also taken on the monumental task of simultaneously overseeing the Roughworks region as it’s Sovereign has been negligent.
- We predict that he will continue to bring House Nasin honour far into the future.
Follow the central staircase into the mansion's underground cemetery. Interact with the left coffin at  to obtain the third key.
Head back up the side stairs to open the middle room and steal the fourth key from the Sleeping Scribe at .
Use this key to open the room on the left hallway at  to unlock the discovery.

intro.text: Aldwell Library is a secret discovery located in The Mistwoods. This discovery reveals insight into ancient Aldwell literature.

- Aldwin: And I do mean ancient!
- Aldwin: I'd love to let you in straight away, but it would be great if you could do a little something for me first.
- Aldwin: Would you be interested in helping a fellow citizen out?
- Aldwin: Amazing! It's quite simple, really.
- Aldwin: Around Aldwell, there are four trees that have served as essential parts of our area's history.
- Aldwin: Flowers grow at their bases too, and they're used in everything from decorating our homes to making helpful remedies.
- Aldwin: My personal supply is running low right now, so I'm in need of a new bouquet...
- Aldwin: My task for you is to go and bring me one of each flower!

intro.text: Birth of Efilim is a secret discovery that takes place in and around Efilim. The discovery shows the founding of Efilim by a group of exiled elves.

lines.text: Interacting with the inscribed stone at the shrine will show the following dialogue:
- Two elven sisters were casted away from their homes, far into the mystical forest. All alone with their followers, hope dwindled as so did the warmth.
- To a fairy of joy, they bumped into, dancing in the middle of a crowd. Together the sisters danced in the night, animals singing and trees waving.
- Soon they brought the fairy with them, and the shivering elves found comfort once again.
- In the darkness of the second night, a lonely fairy weeped in a farm. Abandoned, lost, just like the elves themselves.
- But as the sisters guided the fairy with them to the newly formed party, it gained joy once more.
- The third fairy, scared within, was surrounded by flames. Multiple beasts hopped around the open fire, hungry and desperate to devour it.
- Soon that hunger turned to fear, and only dust was settled clear. Through a medicinal herb the fragile wing fixed itself and fairy joined the somber singing of the others.
- After the sun rose on the fourth morning, a mighty surprise the three fairies had in mind. To a sacred shrine they brought the sisters, and soon the cold of the night was nothing but a memory.
- The story ends there.
In order to activate the shrine you must bring the three fairies mentioned in the poem to the site.
Joyful Fairy
The Joyful Fairy can be found wandering around Efilim.
Scared Fairy

The Scared Fairy can be found trapped by fire in the minotaurs' sacrificial pit. Find a nearby bucket [-957, 45, -5063], fill it with water, and extinguish the flames. Then, you will need to heal the fairy with Medicinal Herbs. After the heart particles appear, the fairy will follow you back to the shrine.
Medicinal Herbs are purchased from the Medicinal Merchant in Efilim at -1029, 42, -4992.
Lonely Fairy

intro.text: Fate of the Olm is a Secret Discovery that takes the player across the Silent Expanse, from the Ruined Olmic City to the Toxic Wastes. It is the longest and most complex discovery in the region, and completing it requires cooperation between two players, both of whom must complete each step.

The discovery involves retracing the path of an ancient oracle of the Olm, who hid a powerful, mysterious "light artifact" to be used against the oncoming Darkness. Completing the discovery as intended involves translating large amounts of Wynnic text, in which case the  Ancient Wynnic Transcriber rewarded for discovering the Wynn Plains Monument is an invaluable resource.

lines.text: To begin the discovery, you must first find the first of three Stone Tablets. It is located in the highest room of the ancient Olmic manor near the north edge of the Ruined City; this location is west of the broken bridge and just off the main path taken during A Journey Further, and therefore many players stumble across this discovery and find the first Tablet by accident during the quest.

The Stone Tablet is engraved with several sentences of Ancient Wynnic text, which when translated (using the Transcriber or otherwise) read as follows: ''"The monster from beyond has found us. Our only chance is the light artifact. The key to the hiding place is in the runemaster's basement. His house is in the forest. If you find this note it is already too late for me. Please seek out the artifact."''

The text directs the player to the next location, in the Eyeball Forest. Note that in order for the next step to be accessible, the Tablet ''must'' be collected first. Each step in this discovery must be completed in order.

The house you are directed to by the first Tablet is the only building on the western edge of the Eyeball Forest. To uncover the basement, first climb to the ruined upper floor of the building, find the wooden crates suspended by a rope at the south side, and break the rope by left-clicking it. The crates will fall, breaking open a hole in the ground and giving access to the basement. The second Stone Tablet will be located on the floor near a table.

The Wynnic text on the Tablet translates as follows: ''"If you find this note, you must be seeking the key to the light artifact. It had to be moved to prevent it falling into the wrong hands. It is protected beneath a shrine north of here."''
The next location is some distance north of Lutho, in the Toxic Wastes; proceeding beyond this stage requires partially completing A Journey Further.

The shrine is found in the northwestern hills of the Toxic Wastes, beneath a distinctive overhang dripping in green stalactites. In order to access the hidden part of the shrine, you must collect three shards scattered around the area:
- The Sapphire Shard is located atop a partially-collapsed pillar at the western edge of the area at [887, 97, -981].
- The Quartz Shard is located next to one of the pillars of the stone pavilion at the eastern edge, at [925, 90, -983].
- The Ebony Shard is located in the shadows beneath a small ledge at [909, 90, -994], north of the Quartz Shard.

Once you've collected all three shards, place them on the altar inside the aforementioned eastern pavilion. A hole will open in the ground, and you can jump down to enter a partially-flooded underground temple. Complete the simple parkour at the end of the room to reach the Engraved Stone, and interact with it; the Wynnic inscription will appear in chat (unlike the others, this one cannot be taken with you). It reads: ''"The creators of darkness are encroaching. I had to move the key once more. I have sent it back to the family house armory via the tunnels. If you seek the artifact then you must make it there."''

Take the Ancient Pickaxe embedded in the pillar left of the engraving, and return to the lower level of the underground chamber. The blocked eastern tunnel can be cleared with the pickaxe to leave the area; after climbing a spiral staircase you will find yourself aboveground back in the Ruined Olmic City, just outside the mansion that is your next destination.

This is the section that cannot be completed without two players, both of whom have followed the steps to reach this point. Re-enter the mansion, and this time you will be able to find two keys throughout the building:
- Kaen's Key is found downstairs upon the altar in the large chapel-like room, at [529, 92, -797].
- Adan's Key is found upstairs in the small room with an iron door, at [512, 109, -783], which.

Once each player has one of the keys, both must go to the chamber at [519, 100, -744], with a large set of doors and two golden pressure plates. Each pressure plate also has a keyhole and a sign: the right is marked ''"Kaen"'', in Wynnic, and the left is marked ''"Adan"''. The player with Kaen's Key must stand on the right pressure plate and open the right keyhole, and the player with Adan's Key must do the same on the left, simultaneously.
When both keys are inserted, the doors will open to the manor vault and armory. Inside is the Tomb Key, which will unlock the final stage of the discovery.

The third and final Stone Tablet is also found in this room; unlike the others, this one does ''not'' have to be taken for the final step, but its message is important nonetheless. It reads: ''"The beast's follower is here, looking for the artifact. It's too late, it was buried with our grandmother yesterday. If you are in dire need of light, please seek it out. The tomb is north of the mansion. The is likely our last moment, but it doesn't have to be yours."''

Your final destination is the tomb of the Olmic oracle who originally started this journey, Anya. As long as you collected the Tomb Key in the armory, you no longer need to work in tandem with another player at this point. Travel the short distance up the road north to the large tomb, and use the key on the door to open it. At the end of the long hallway inside is a grave. Reaching it is enough to complete the discovery, granting you 1.5 million Experience Points.

The true reward, however, is the light artifact itself. Pressing the button on the grave will open it, revealing Anya's corpse; click on it to retrieve Anya's Penumbra, an untradable level 100 Fabled Bracelet.

lines.text: To gain access to the library the player has to search for and find a key hidden in the Gert camp that is being watched by the Gylia Watch. Entering the Gert camp requires the player to equip the Hungry Gert Mask given as a reward for completing the quest Hunger of the Gerts Part I.
- Reach the tower overlooking the Gert camp and climb the ladder to the top. Collect the key.

intro.text: The Lost Avos City is a Secret Discovery located in the north of Corkus Island, near the Avos Territory. It involves locating and exploring an ancient, buried city of the Avos built 350 years ago, and expands on the lore and history of the Avos following the arrival of the humans. In addition, at the end of the city is a secret boss battle and extra reward. A minimum level of 85 is required to gain the Discovery's experience reward.

lines.text: Unlike most Avos settlements and homes, there is one abandoned Avos hut outside of the Avos Territory, on the ground level mostly dominated by the Corkian Humans. This site is mentioned as unusual by a Corkus Citizen in Corkus City.

To begin the process of finding the Lost City, just enter this hut (be wary of the many hostile rogue Mechs that spawn nearby, as you could get trapped inside by them). A ghostly Avos simply called ??? will appear behind you, in the doorway; right-clicking it will cause it to vanish and reappear some distance away, to the north. Keep following this ghost north, right-clicking it each time to make it appear at its next location, until you reach a cave in the cliffs.

This cave is also full of dangerous mobs, so be prepared to fight them off. After interacting with the Avos ghost at the cave entrance, follow it twice more into a large room with a ledge, where it will now be found. This chamber also holds two Tier III Loot Chests. Right-click the ghost one more time to make it disappear and open a secret passage in the wall, which will teleport you to the subterranean Lost Avos City. Simply walk forward to achieve the Discovery, and gain 1060000 experience points.

Although you will now have reached the Lost City, there is still much more to explore within it. The city is a somewhat labyrinthine, dungeon-like ruin, and you will often have to take in your surroundings carefully in order to find the way forward; it is rarely obvious, and there are many dead ends. In addition, the ruin is haunted by level 93 Fallen Avos Warriors and level 91 Fallen Avos Shamans, who use melee and ranged attacks respectively, and who can be very dangerous in the tight corridors and chambers of the city. The Shamans especially can be annoying during the brief parkour areas.

Despite its vastness, there is a correct path through the Lost City that will take you deeper into the ruins. In addition, you will get bits of dialogue from a mysterious voice as you progress; this dialogue slowly reveals the history of the Avos and the city itself, as well as the arrival of the Corkian settlers (see below). Over time, the voice will reveal itself as the immortal Phoenix Prince of the Avos.

At the far edge of the city is a great ruined palace, overgrown and empty, that belongs to the Phoenix Prince. On its roof is a dark passage that leads to the grand throne room where the boss battle with the many forms of the level 120 Phoenix Prince takes place; the final lines of dialogue appear as you enter the chamber. Defeating the Prince is the final challenge of the Lost City, and he drops a powerful level 90 Legendary helmet, the Phoenix Prince's Crown.
[1/12] ???: It was 350 years ago when I last saw a human. And I will never forget.
[2/12] ???: Your kind had already dominated Wynn and Fruma. But you decided to come to this island. Our island.
[3/12] ???: I will never understand why some Avos decided to let you live here. Those who welcomed you stayed on the surface.
[4/12] ???: But I, Prince of the Avos, led the rest of my people down here, where no human could disturb us. And so, we lived here... for a while.
[5/12] ???: But avians like us are not suited to living underground. We became ill and lost our feathers. And eventually, my people died out.
[6/12] ???: Their souls still wander and cry throughout the ruins of my city.
[7/12] ???: However, I have remained here, still alive, hearing the plight and torment of the lost souls. For I am cursed to never die, only to be reborn.
[8/12] Phoenix Prince: Because of this endless cycle of reincarnation, I am only known as the Phoenix Prince.
[9/12] Phoenix Prince: After the death of all my people, your kind sealed the city, they likely didn't want anyone to know about what happened down here.
[10/12] Phoenix Prince: But unbeknownst to them, I was still here. Trapped forever, without even the escape of death. And it is all the fault of the humans who drove us here.
[11/12] Phoenix Prince: You're an invader, just like the rest of your people. They do not deserve to live on this island... on ''our'' island.
[12/12] Phoenix Prince: Prepare for our revenge. Prepare to DIE!
- It can be difficult to locate the Avos ghost after leaving the abandoned hut, but follow the nearby road north and you'll see it.
- If the ghost despawns or doesn't reappear while you're following it, you'll have to restart the process by switching to a different server.
- Inside the Lost City, paths of grey, brown or red carpets will sometimes show the correct path.
- The Phoenix Prince is a reference to Phoenix King/Fire Lord Ozai from Avatar: The Last Airbender.
- His primary elements are fire and air.
- The last two lines of dialogue he says is similar to what Ozai says when he corners Aang in the episode Sozin's Comet Part 3.
