intro.text: The Gwanari, also known simply as the Carnivorous Creature in its World Discovery, is a Cave found in the Eyeball Forest. It is one of the caves required to unlock the Silent Expanse Expedition lootrun.

lines.text: The Gwanari's entrance is right into its maw. There are four paths going in each of the cardinal directions, alongside three chambers with Tier 2  Loot Chests and a Stomach Dweller inside them. The southwest chamber is the chamber that allows you to exit the cave, which also contains a Tier 3  Loot Chest that requires the Stomach Dweller inside that chamber to be killed.

intro.text: The Heartwood is a Cave found in the Dernel Jungle.

lines.text: The cave immediately starts off with a split path, the left one being labeled as dangerous and the right one not having any whatsoever. The left path immediately starts off with a Tier 1  Loot Chest. A Tier 2  Loot Chest found across a pond. The left path ends with a Tier 1  Loot Chest being found on the top of a mushroom. The right path simply leads to the point where both paths converge. Once Ironwood Guards start to appear, a Tier 1  Loot Chest can be found on top of a mushroom. There will be a seal at the end of the room, which requires 4 Ironwood Hearts to open, dropped from the aforementioned mob. The final room of the cave has several Ironwood Guards and Electrogaea Apparitions; 3 of the latter must be slain to open a Tier 4  Loot Chest.
Rarely, a Suspicious Spot will spawn at the end of the cave.

intro.text: The Lantern Keeper's Abode is a Cave found in Void Valley. It is one of the caves that must be completed in order to unlock the Silent Expanse Expedition lootrun.

lines.text: The cave in its entirety is a boss cave. The main miniboss of the cave is the Lantern Keeper. Several of the Igniteds will serve as the main minions in the fight, although a mob called the Rekindled Unsurmountable will serve as a constant threat with an inability to die. The Tier 4  Loot Chest found in the center of the arena will be opened once the Lantern Keeper is killed.

intro.text: The Place Coalesced is a Cave found in the Toxic Wastes. This cave is required to be completed in order to unlock the Silent Expanse Expedition lootrun.

lines.text: The first section is a passage to the second section. Several Invading Toxins can be found in this part of the cave.

The second section of the cave is a large open room with several mobs inside, along with the main miniboss of the cave, That Which Coalesces, which must be killed in order to open the Tier 4  Loot Chest found in the center of the room.

intro.text: The Place Condensed is a Cave found in the Eyeball Forest. It is one of the caves required to unlock the Silent Expanse Expedition lootrun.

lines.text: The cave is a simple path to the end. At the end of the cave, there is the main miniboss of the cave, That Which Condenses, which must be killed to open at Tier 4  Loot Chest.

intro.text: The Place Conglomerated is a Cave found in the Void Valley.

lines.text: The cave is first entered through a Void Hole which then leads to a tunnel filled with Glow Blossoms, which will pelt the player with projectiles. Eventually, a room will be reached containing several Lichenous Almanars and That Which Conglomerates alongside a Tier 4 Loot Chest which requires the latter to be killed.

intro.text: The Sacrificial Altar is a  Boss Cave found in Time Valley at the bottom of the Sanctuary Bridge.

lines.text: The cave is a simple circular boss arena. Several melee Dark Cultists (Lv. 20) can be found around the entrance to the cave. The Sacrificial Altar miniboss is in the center of the arena, and three ranged Dark Cultists (Lv. 21) appear around it. These Cultists respawn frequently and support the miniboss by using the Heal spell, which heals themselves and nearby mobs. Attacking the Sacrificial Altar will provoke it and initiate the fight.
Miniboss

The Sacrificial Altar fires ranged attacks and is immune to knockback, blindness, and slowness. Additionally, the Altar can use the Push spell to push the player away from it. Defeating the Altar will unleash the second phase of the fight, the Spirit of Vexation. This phase gains the ability to move, and begins to use the Pull spell to pull the player close, as well as the Heavy Teleport spell to teleport and deal damage if it passes through the player. Defeating this phase will release two of the next and final phase of the Spirit of Vexation, which have identical abilities to the previous phase. After killing the two second-phase Spirit of Vexations, the Tier 3  Loot Chest in the back of the cave will unlock. They also have a chance to drop pieces from the Vexing Set.
Category:Boss Caves

intro.text: The Warehouse is a Cave Complex found in the Scraplands. It is one of the caves that must be done in order to unlock The Corkus Traversal.

lines.text: Inside the maze are two keys that are used to progress, the Red Energy Key, and the Lime Energy Key. All the points of interest in the maze are listed below:
- Red Energy Key: -1797, 27, -2639
- Lime Energy Key: -1799, 27, -2661
- Tier 1  Loot Chest: -1791, 27, -2660

The Red Room is unlocked at the Red Door using the Red Energy Key. Several Energy Turrets will pelt at you when you enter, with a Tier 2  Loot Chest being found in the middle of this room. Following this is a partly scaffolded area, which then leads to the start of the control room.

The Lime Room is unlocked at the Lime Door using the Lime Energy Key. It is a parkour section that then requires you to explore to find a Cyan Energy Key, founded by doing the rest of the parkour near the door. There is also an optional Tier 2  Loot Chest that can be found by fully completing the parkour. Opening the Cyan Door will lead to the start of the control room.

At the start of the third room is an exit and a Tier 3  Loot Chest that requires 2 nearby mobs to be killed. If you don't take the exit and continue, you will be brought to a room that has three differently-colored Control Panels. All three of them must be killed to open the door. Several Energised Mechs will spawn from machines that line the walls opposite of the Control Panels. Once all Control Panels have been destroyed, the door is opened to the next room.

intro.text: The Thunder Grub Nest is a Cave found in the Troms Jungle.

lines.text: The cave is mostly a straightforward path to the end. Several Charged Eggs can be found in alcoves dotted across the cave. At the end is a Tier 3  Loot Chest that requires 14 nearby mobs to be killed to open it.

intro.text: Tidepool Terrace is a  Cave found on the Coastal Trail.

lines.text: Tidepool Terrace consists of a single long tunnel that connects to two different openings on the surface. These openings connect two stages of the Underwater Quest; the west side leads to Omango and the shipwreck, and the east side leads to Sayrr's ship. Cave Crabs and Waterlogged Zombies appear in the entire cave, while Tidepool Spitters only appear in small pools of water. In a small branch marked with gold blocks there is a Tier 3 Loot Chest which unlocks after slaying 3-6 mobs. Gudgeon gathering nodes can also be found throughout the cave.

intro.text: The Time Valley Aquifer is a  Cave found in Time Valley.

lines.text: The entrance of this cave leads to a room with a Tier 1  Loot Chest that is guarded by a single Loch Jaw. There is a path to continue on the left; however, there is also a shortcut directly to the bottom of the cave found on the right. Continuing to follow the path will lead to another Tier 1  Loot Chest and a Loch Jaw. Afterwards, there is a parkour. Falling here will lead to the bottom of the cave, but completing the parkour will lead to another Tier 1  Loot Chest with a Loch Jaw. At the end of the cave is a large pool of water filled with Cave Carnivores and a Tier 3  Loot Chest. The chest unlocks after slaying 10-12 mobs. The exit door is found in a ring of red rock and entering it will launch you very high upwards out of a small pond on the surface.

intro.text: Toads in a Hole is a Cave found in the Olux Swamp. It is involved in the quest Master Piece.

lines.text: The cave is mostly a straightforward path to the end. At the end is a Tier 3  Loot Chest that requires 6 nearby mobs to be killed.

intro.text: The Treasure Tomb is a  Cave found in the Almuj Desert.

lines.text: The cave is a single room. Near the entrance is a Sand Juggler and a Tier 2  Loot Chest. Inside the cave, 4 Sand Jugglers surround the room, and the Spiny Skeleton Guard is found near a wooden door at the back. Killing the Guard unlocks the door to a treasure room and the Tier 3  Loot Chest inside.

intro.text: The Tree of Light is a Cave found in the Realm of Light.

lines.text: The cave initially starts off as one singular path before diverging into two different paths. Choosing to do the parkour will lead to a climbing section that will give a Tier 2  Loot Chest at the end of it, which then leads to a path with several Ethereal Bodies. At the end of that path is a Tier 3  Loot Chest that requires 2 nearby mobs to be killed. Choosing to drop down will lead to a path with several Gnome Defenders. At the end of the dropper path is a small section with several Cave Woollies and a Tier 3  Loot Chest that requires 8 nearby mobs to be killed.

intro.text: The Troll Burrows are a Cave found in the Canyon of the Lost near Thesead.

lines.text: The cave is mostly a straightforward path to the end. After a while, there will be some parkour, followed by the first trolls appearing. At the end of the cave is a Tier 3  Loot Chest that requires 17 nearby mobs to be killed.

intro.text: The Troll Tower is a  Tower found in the Ocean near Mage Island.

lines.text: This cave long, winding parkour with many tight spaces to jump through. Unlike all other Caves found in the Content Book, there are no mobs that spawn here. At the top is an NPC named Troll alongside a Tier 3  Loot Chest that unlocks from doing the parkour. There is a short walkway that leads over a well; this is a safe landing spot to quickly descend from the tower.

intro.text: The Trunk Garrison is a Cave found in the Troms Jungle.

lines.text: The cave starts off with a split path. The left path will lead back to the right path, although there will be a Tier 2  Loot Chest found in the detour. The rest of the cave is a straight path to the exit, ending with a Tier 3  Loot Chest guarded by an Undead Commander that requires 8 nearby mobs to be killed to open it.

intro.text: The Visceral Remnant is a Cave found in the Kander Forest.

lines.text: The cave is mostly a straightforward path to the end. At the end of the cave is a Tier 2  Loot Chest and a Tier 3  Loot Chest that requires the miniboss of the cave, the Flesh Amalgam, to be killed.

intro.text: The Volcanus Pit is a Cave found on the Volcanic Isles.

lines.text: The cave is mostly a straightforward path to the end. At the end of the cave is a Tier 4  Loot Chest that requires 10 nearby mobs to be killed. A Tier 2  Loot Chest can be found in the stone structure near the end.

intro.text: The Voltaic Crag is a Cave found in the Canyon of the Lost.

lines.text: The cave has several Voltaic Animants attacking you as you enter the cave. At the end of the cave is a Tier 3  Loot Chest that can only be opened by defeating the enigmatic Voltaic Seal.

intro.text: The Vortex Complex is a  Cave Complex found near Time Valley.

lines.text: Dropping into the first section will put you in a pool of water with 4 Trout nodes. Continuing on leads to a brief parkour section around some wooden structures, followed by a muddy tunnel that slows your movement speed. Wooden platforms found on the ground can be used to navigate the tunnel faster than simply running through. Meanwhile, Dust Spawns rapidly fire projectiles and Mud Lurkers attempt to attack and make the parkour more difficult. Part of the way through the muddy section is an offshoot that leads to a Tier 2  Loot Chest. At the end of the parkour is the Complex's first exit door and a path to continue further into the cave.

The second section of the cave starts with a Tier 1  Loot Chest and a brief parkour up more wooden structures. Rotten Corpses are found at the top, alongside a fork in the road. The left path continues to the end of the cave, while the right path leads to an extra room marked by a warning sign that reads: "! WARNING ! ".
Right Path

In the dead end, four Rusted Time Turrets defend room filled with vibrant colored rocks. These rocks are similar to the more muted colored rocks found throughout the cave. Additionally, 2 Tier 2  Loot Chests are found towards the back of the room.
Left Path

This path leads to a parkour similar to the one found at the entrance of the cave. Completing the parkour unlocks a Tier 4  Loot Chest at the end next to a second exit door. There is also one final path to the left of the chest.
This is an incredibly short and easy section. No mobs spawn in this area, and there is a chasm that leads back to the first section of the cave. There is a Tier 2  Loot Chest near a final exit door.
Category:Cave Complexes

intro.text: The Watery Waterfall is a Cave found in the Canyon of the Lost.

lines.text: The cave starts off with some parkour. After the parkour is a fairly linear section with a Tier 2  Loot Chest being found halfway through it. At the end of the cave is a Tier 3  Loot Chest that requires 4 nearby mobs to be killed.

intro.text: The Wave Cult Temple is a  Cave found on Wave Cult Island in the Ocean.

lines.text: Wave Cult Initiates, Ocean Wakers, and a Wave Raiser guard the entrance to the cave. Inside, there is the temple hallway which heads straight forward. More Ocean Wakers are found throughout the temple, while a Storm Shaker is positioned behind the staircase to the lower floor. Two more Storm Shakers block the way to the end of the cave; a short parkour down a hall. Beside the exit, there is a Tier 3  Loot Chest that unlocks after slaying 8-10 nearby mobs.

intro.text: The Weird Wilds is a  Cave found in the Light Forest near the Light Portal.

lines.text: The cave starts off with a large amount of Hollow Weirds, as a well as some Rising Weirds, that can easily swarm you due to their high movement speed. There is also a Tier 1 Loot Chest on the right wall. The path forward is protected by 4 Steam Weirds that use the Wave spell in order to block you from continuing through the cave. Past these mobs is a split in the path.

The left path is guarded by 4 more Steam Weirds and leads to a very minor parkour section that leads to the end of the cave, along with a Tier 2 Loot Chest found under the first wooden platform. Some Prismatic Weirds, Formative Weirds, and Light Weirds spawn at the bottom of the parkour, and the top is guarded by a few Galeforce Weirds.
The right path leads directly to the end. Some Prismatic Weirds, Formative Weirds, and Light Weirds spawn here, and there are a several more Galeforce Weirds on this path than the left one.

2 Anima Weirds appear at the end of the cave, but only one must be killed to unlock the Tier 4 Loot Chest and finish the cave. There are also many Prismatic Weirds, and a few Formative Weirds and Light Weirds that spawn here. The Loot Chest and exit can be found in the abandoned building behind the mobs.

intro.text: The Weirding Ring is a Tower found in the Kander Forest. It also serves as a grind spot.

lines.text: The main central area of the ring is a grind area, but some mushrooms will be climbable, which lead to some loot chests. The western-most mushroom can be climbed to access a Tier 2  Loot Chest. The northwestern cluster of orange mushrooms has a Tier 1  Loot Chest on it. The eastern cluster of orange mushrooms has two Tier 1  Loot Chests on them, with a Tier 2  Loot Chest being found on a nearby rock. On the large northern cluster of mushrooms, there is a Tier 2  Loot Chest and a Tier 4  Loot Chest that requires 4 nearby mobs to be killed to open it. On the large southern cluster of mushrooms, there is a Tier 2  Loot Chest and a Tier 3  Loot Chest that requires 3 nearby mobs to be killed to open it. There is a series of platforms that will lead to the opposite cluster of large mushrooms. In between both afforementioned large clusters of mushrooms, there is a series of red and orange platforms connecting both of them, which is also where the rewards chest will spawn.
Category:Towers

intro.text: The Willow Crypt is a  Cave found on the border of the Savannah and the Nemract Swamp.

lines.text: This cave is a long tunnel though a crypt. There is a Tier 2  Loot Chest in the roots of the decaying tree found over the entrance. Crypt Parasites and Risen Skeletons can be found throughout the cave. There is a stone structure inside the tunnel that holds some tombs; another Tier 2  Loot Chest can be found in the bright-colored tomb on the left. At the end of the cave is a Tier 3  Loot Chest that unlocks after slaying 8-10 mobs.
Category:Cave

intro.text: The Windwalker Temple is a Cave found in the Sky Islands. It is one of the caves that must be completed in order to unlock the Sky Islands Exploration Lootrun.

lines.text: The start of the cave has two Sylphid Gatekeepers standing guard. Continuing into the temple will be a central room with a Sylphid Observer alongside 3 branches. The left branch has a hidden room with a Tier 3  Loot Chest that requires 3 nearby Sylphid Statues to be killed. Each branch has a Sylphid Statue that can be killed.

intro.text: The Winery Infestation is a  Cave found on the edge of the Detlas Suburbs and the Roots of Corruption.

lines.text: The first section of the cave has vegetation throughout and corruption covering the ceiling. There are large amounts of Infestors and Root Ingrainers throughout the tunnel, as well as multiple Root Infestations positioned up on top of wooden supports. A Tier 2  Loot Chest can be found near the entrance under a Root Infestation at [297, 64, -1371].

The end of the cave is the wine cellar that forms an open arena. The entrance is guarded by some Black Bats, while the larger arena is filled with Infestors, Root Ingrainers, and very strong Infested Zombies. There is a Tier 4  Loot Chest found in the back which unlocks after slaying 12-14 mobs. The exit is found on the right side, while the left side has a staircase to goes up to an overlook of the arena.

intro.text: The Wolf Den is a Cave found in the Nesaak Tundra.

lines.text: The cave starts with several Wild Snow Wolves and Icy Wolves attacking you before you plunge into a pool of water. Continuing on will challenge you with more wolves, before some parkour is reached. Once the parkour is complete, the main miniboss of the cave reveals itself, the Crazy Wolf Tamer, alongside all of their wolves they named. A Tier 3  Loot Chest requires the tamer to be killed to open it.

intro.text: The Arena of the Legends is a Boss Altar designed for players of around level 70. It takes place deep within the Temple of the Legends. To access the temple, and this altar, one must have completed the Temple of the Legends Quest.

lines.text: All five forms of the Magus have a combined total of 84000 health, and the fight can be very lengthy even at higher levels. Once the fifth form has been defeated, the boss is truly defeated. It drops a total of 192 emeralds upon death, and cannot be fought again unless the 5 Broken Amulets required to enter the arena are re-acquired. All forms of the Grand Magus utilize Heal, Teleport, Meteor, and Slowness, with different forms favoring certain spells.

The first form is based around the Fire element, and attacks as soon as the player enters the arena. It has 12000 health, and attacks by throwing a large burst of small fireballs towards the player all at once. It favors Heal spell, having a stronger version with a shorter cooldown, and uses it more often. This form is completely immune to Fire damage, is weak to Water, and deals Fire damage as well. In addition, it has minor defensive bonuses against the Thunder, Earth and Air elements.

The second form is based around the Water element, spawning after the first form has been killed. It also has 12000 health fights with very rapid standard ranged attacks, and uses many of the same spells as the first form, favoring Slowness instead of Heal. This form is immune to Water damage, deals Water damage and is weak to Thunder, and also has minor defense against the other three elements.

The third form is based around the Thunder element. It has 12000 health and attacks by throwing small, hard-to-see orbs in extremely quick succession, sometimes pausing for a few seconds before attacking again. This form of the Magus also uses the Heavy Teleport spell, allowing it to blind players in its path. It is immune to Thunder and deals Thunder damage, is weak to Earth damage, and has minor defense against the other elements.

The fourth form is based around the Earth element. It also has 12000 health, and shoots several leaf blocks at the player at once, in the same fashion as the first form. In this form the Magus favors the Meteor spell, using it more often and for higher damage than the previous forms. It is immune to Earth and deals Earth damage, is weak to Air damage, and has minor defense against the other elements.

The fifth and final form of the Grand Magus uses all four of the previous elements. It is much tougher than the other forms, with a total of 45000 health, and utilizes the strongest spells of all of the previous forms. Unlike the previous forms, the Magus deals no neutral damage in this one; instead it deals large amounts of Fire, Water, Thunder and Earth damage, with a significant amount of elemental defense in each of those. Thus, its attacks can be heavily reduced or even negated if multi-element defensive armor is worn. However, it also has no elemental weakness. It should also be noted that this form has no defense or weakness towards the Air element.

intro.text: The Bottomless Pit is a Boss Altar added in the 1.20 Gavel Reborn update, designed for endgame players of level 100+. It is located on an island in the deepest reach of the Silent Expanse, below the floating rocks leading to the Portal to Dern. In order to access the area, you must have completed the level 101 quest A Journey Further, and successfully completed at least one run of the Eldritch Outlook Dungeon.

lines.text: After giving the required Soul Essence to the altar, before you even face the boss, you will be dropped down an extremely long, pitch-black pit, before landing at the bottom and immediately taking unavoidable fall damage equal to 99% of your health. Continue down a short passage to the arena itself, which will at first appear to be empty. A brief dialogue ensues as follows:
- There's... nothing here?
- There has to be something down here, you can feel it watching you...
- You just took a huge fall, you're vulnerable, something's there but you can't see it where is it
- where is it where is it where is it you can’t find it where is it you’re going to die if you don’t find it find it FIND IT
At this point, the boss of the Bottomless Pit will appear at the far side of the arena: the level 140 Panic Zealot.
- IT’S THERE YOU CAN SEE IT AND IT’S TOO STRONG YOU’RE GOING TO DIE AND THERE’S NO WAY OUT WHY DID YOU COME DOWN HERE
- PANIC PANIC PANIC PANIC PANIC PANIC
- NONONONONONONONONONO YOU CAN’T DO THIS
- RUN AWAY BUT WHERE THERE’S NO PLACE TO
- CAN’T THINK STRAIGHT CAN’T CALM DOWN
- YOU HAVE TO STRUGGLE BUT IT WON’T BE ENOUGH
- STOP PANICKING YOU CAN’T STOP PANICKING YOU
- CAN'T STOP PANICKING YOU CAN'T STOP PANICKING
- YOU CAN'T STOP PANICKING YOU CAN'T STOP
- PANICKING YOU CAN'T STOP PANICKING YOU CAN'T
- YOU CAN'T YOU CAN'T YOU CAN'T YOU CAN'T YOU CAN'T

The Panic Zealot possesses a considerable 3 million health. While it can attack with melee if you get too close, it does not move very fast, and its main attacks are in the form of a wide variety of abilities. These include the dangerous offensive spells Explosion and Wave, as well as their more powerful “heavy” variants, plus the Push, Heavy Weakness, and Teleport abilities, the last of which it will occasionally chain several times in a row. It has some defenses against  and  damage, and a weakness to .

However, this fight is much more complex than a typical boss fight, and makes use of several unique mechanics. Most importantly: at all times while fighting the Panic Zealot, you will be unavoidably damaged for 99% of your current health every five seconds. Without a very large stock of Healing Potions or healing spells, you will effectively be forced to fight it at minimum health, and although the effect cannot kill you directly it can make any oncoming threat much more dangerous. This is the defining feature of the fight, significantly disadvantaging most players (but which can also be leveraged as an advantage using certain builds, such as Rage). While this effect is intimidating, the Zealot actually deals less damage than normal in exchange, so you may still be able to take one or two hits from it even at extremely low health.

Additionally, the Panic Zealot makes use of two other mechanics. Firstly, “snares” can appear throughout the arena, signalled by a ring of purple particles. These snares last for 15 seconds and will freeze any player stepping into them for 3 seconds. When you get snared, the following dialogue will play:
- CAUGHT IT'S CAUGHT YOU IT'S CAUGHT YOU
- WHAT ARE YOU DOING YOU NEED TO MOVE YOU CAN'T
- CAN'T MOVE YOUR BODY IT'S COMING FOR YOU GET OUT
- YOU'RE CAUGHT YOU'RE TRAPPED NO WAY OUT
- PANIC PANIC PANIC PANIC PANIC PANIC
- MOVE MOVE MOVE MOVE MOVE MOVE MOVE MOVE MOVE MOVE

Second, starting when the Zealot is reduced to 50% (750,000) health, “clones” of it will begin to appear, signalled by a line of particles, and rapidly run across the arena. If one of these clones catches you, you will be blinded for several seconds, and the following dialogue will play:
- IT'S EVERYWHERE IT'S EVERYWHERE YOU LOOK
- IT'S STARING AT YOU FROM EVERY DIRECTION YOU CAN FEEL ITS EYES
- ITS EYES CAN FEEL YOU IT CAN FEEL YOUR MIND
- WHY DID YOU COME DOWN HERE THERE'S NOTHING BUT DEATH AND DEATH AND DEATH
- YOU CAN'T SEE ANYTHING IT'S GOING TO GET YOU YOU'RE VULNERABLE
- MOVE KEEP MOVING BUT WHERE CAN YOU GO THAT'S SAFE THERE'S NO PLACE SAFE
- PANIC PANIC PANIC PANIC PANIC PANIC

Both of these mechanics can compound with one another and with the Zealot's regular abilities, such as the already-difficult to avoid Heavy Wave, and care must be taken to remain aware of your surroundings. Both the snares and the clones will appear more often over the course of the fight, peaking when the Zealot is at 30% (450,000) health.
The Panic Zealot also possesses “Crowd Control Immunity”, meaning it is immune to all special knockback and status effects (Ice Snake's freeze, Aura's pull, etc).
After being defeated, along with its other drops, the Zealot will drop a Tether to the Surface, which can be used on the far wall to leave the arena.
Tips and tricks
- Try to use an archetype that has self healing to make this boss a complete joke.

- If the archetype you are using does not have self healing, use a setup that has at least 100 lifesteal and melee the boss occasionally to outheal the bosses attacks. The boss main attacks deal less than 100 damage only so 100 LS or more is sufficient.
- To prevent getting hit by charge or snare traps attack, try to fight the boss in 1 of the 4 corners of the arena and avoid being at the center.

intro.text: The Challenge of the Blades is a Boss Altar designed for player that are level 70. It is located in the Kander Forest, on top of a hill south of the Lexdale Penitentiary.

lines.text: - Blade of Shade: Aha...you'll be a very interesting quarry to catch, human...

The fight consists of simply a melee boss, Blade of Shade. After defeating the first phase, the boss splits into two copies. Each copy will successively split into more copies until eventually being defeated permanently, up to a maximum of 16 copies. They have 15000 health in the first phase, with each successive phase having higher health - the final phase (16 copies) has 91,750 health each, with all clones of the Blade of Shade having a total HP of 2,446,500. This means that attempting to pick off one set at at time is very difficult, since the earlier phases tend to split even when focusing on the later phases. The player should keep their distance, as this horde can easily overwhelm them, especially since the boss often casts Teleport and Vanish. The last clones will drop the various altar rewards and a portion of the emerald rewards.

intro.text: The Magmastream Core is a Boss Altar added in the 1.20 Gavel Reborn update. It is located inside the largest volcano in the main island of the Volcanic Isles.

lines.text: - Something's dropping from the ceiling!
The Vulcor Adrenophage is the boss of the Magmastream Core. It is a melee enemy.

The boss does not have too much HP for a Boss Altar boss, and acts more as a mobile glass cannon. Most of the time it will spam Charges and Heavy Charges to dash around the arena, with it occasionally attacking by using Explosions and Flamethrowers. It does not have Crowd-Control-Immunity, which means that it can be affected by the knockback and slowing, stunning, trapping, etc. effects of spells like Ice Snake, Uppercut and Aura.

The minions of the battle, the Convec Monocytes, also move around using Charges and Heavy charges, and deal a decent amount of damage with their Flamethrowers. At maxium, there can only be a couple of these minions in the arena, so one should not fear of them swarming them over time.

lines.text: - The Beast: Escape... so close... need power...

Both bosses are fought simultaneously and have 2 phases. The Beast is burst ranged, firing a large inaccurate cloud of projectiles, has one spell chain and Knockback Resistance:

Once the Beast is killed, the second phase of it will begin as it transforms into the Unfettered. The Unfettered still has the original spell chain of the Beast, it also has a few new spell chains:

intro.text: The Unknown Area is a Boss Altar designed for players of around level 99. It is located beneath the Wybel Island in the Sky Islands.

lines.text: The Orange Wybel starts with 135000 HP. He has a pitiful speed of 65%. It is unwise to attempt to attack him with Thunder or Fire damage, as he has 870 defense in each. Along with his basic attack, the Orange Wybel can use Meteor and Heavy Charge. When he uses the latter, pay attention, as the impact deals significant damage.

After defeating his first phase, the Orange Wybel engages into a rage state. His speed jumps to 165% and he changes to a Charge AI. He continuously spams Meteor, ending with a Self-Destruct into the next phase. Do not try to manually defeat him, as his high health regen will heal him instantly.
This phase is nearly identical to his first phase, but his speed increases to 70%. A Heavy Push spell is added to his arsenal. Additionally, his Fire and Thunder defenses jump to 1350.
Phase 4 is essentially identical to the second phase (his defense is increased, but that does not affect his invincibility). His speed increases to 170%.

In the last phase, the Orange Wybel gains multiple buffs to his stats. His Thunder and Fire defenses increase again to a whopping 1740 (more than Qira). His health rises to 270000. His speed rises to 75%. Defeat this phase, and you will have vanquished the Orange Wybel. Keep the Teleporter Controller he drops and right click the enchanting table to leave the arena.
- Disintegrator: These have 2000 health and deal 998-1498 neutral damage, 1-1 fire and thunder damage. They can use Flamethrower and Self-Destruct spells.

- Disintegrator Core: These have 500000 health and are impossible to kill. They deal 1-5000 fire and thunder (as well as a measly 0-1 Neutral) damage per hit and have Pull and Self Destruct spells. They must be avoided at all costs.

- Rowdy Wybel: These have 9500 health, but they only spawn when you stand on a golden pressure plate in the arena. They deal 600-690 Neutral damage and have the spells Heavy Slowness and Heavy Heal. Additionally, they have 350 Fire and Thunder defense.

intro.text: Annihilation is the level 250 boss of the Prelude to Annihilation Major World Event, which was added in 2.1 Rekindled World. The event currently occurs around once every 3 days, and all players above combat level 30 are able to challenge it at once at the Corruption Portal in the Roots of Corruption, in parties of up to 10 players.
Among other rewards, players who defeat Annihilation have a chance of earning a Corrupted Cache, which is guaranteed to award one of five exclusive Mythic Weapons.

lines.text: Aside from the fact that it is a Devil native to the Realm of War, the origins of Annihilation are unknown. The earliest known emergence of the beast (or another like it) onto the physical plane occurred around 900 AP, when it was supposedly driven back through the Portal singlehandedly by Bob.

Nearly a century later in the winter of 985 AP, the year after Bob's death, earthquakes around the Roots of Corruption alerted the province to Annihilation's imminent reemergence. It was again repelled, this time by the combined armies of Wynn led from the front lines by Admiral Aegis of Detlas, Commander Takan of Nemract, and General Eveni of Troms, although not without massive loss of life.

Fifteen years after the previous attack, in 1000 AP, Annihilation has begun to regularly attempt to reemerge from the Portal. During the leadup to and following the release of the 2.1 Rekindled World update, soldiers in Wynn were rallied once more to repel it.

While the Player is in the Realm of War during the Wartorn Palace, multiple silhouetted Annihilations can be seen in the background. With there being several Annihilations, it is unknown if the Annihilation that Bob, Admiral Aegis, and the Player fought are all the same being or if they are different members of their species.

Annihilation's fight is meant to be fought with other players, due to its extremely high HP at level 105. While it can be attempted at lower levels, the rewards are primarily designed for endgame players.
Players are given 30 minutes to defeat Annihilation. It can use several abilities in its arsenal:
- Rake: Used when the player is in range, Annihilation will smack the player with its right hand for a notable amount of damage.
- Flense: Used when the player is in range, Annihilation will smack the player with its left hand for a large amount of damage.
- Secare: Used when the player is within range and below ?% HP, Annihilation will clap both of its hands, afflicting the player with a massive amount of damage.
- Cauterize Masses: Used when below ?% HP, Annihilation will raise its right index finger and cause 3 waves of 5 meteors to rain down.

- Cauterize Them All: Used when below ?% HP, Annihilation will raise its right index finger, causing 3 large meteors aimed at the player independently to rain down, exploding into smaller meteors upon impact for a massive amount of damage.
- Cleansing Inferno: This ability has three different variations, all of which involve Annihilation spewing out fire:
- Short-ranged: It will spew in an arc around itself. It will only use this when players are close to it.
- Bridge: It will spew down the center of the bridge.
- Long-ranged: It will spew far away at players in the back. It will only use this when players are far away from it.
- Stoke the Blaze: Used when at ?% HP, Annihilation will create a sigil between its horns, buffing its other abilities.

- Apocalpytic Sigil: Annihilation will summon a red ring that is on the player's current spot and will follow them around. Eventually, the ring will stop following the player right before creating a red beam that will chip away at players' HP rapidly if within.
- Exhort: Used when above it, Annihilation will shout in the air as players get knocked back and drained of their mana.

- Caustic Phlegm: Annihilation will summon several mobs which are each called Caustic Phlegm. While they act like standard Jumper AI mobs, they can sometimes perform an attack which gives their target -25% Healing Efficiency.

- Death Beams: Annihilation will lift its left hand and emit a loud noise, before 3 massive apocalyptic sigils with skull symbol are summoned in the central path of arena. They activate one after another. Players inside will get warning, before the beams are summoned dealing massive damage.

- Blossoming Chaos: Used when below 70% HP, Annihilation will raise its left hand as a sigil will appear in the palm. Mayhem Imps, Bighorn Devils, and Magma Hulks will spawn on the bridge, but most importantly an Infernal Subjugate will appear on the end of the bridge opposite to Annihilation. The Infernal Subjugate can heal Annihilation quickly for a large amount.

- Eyes of War: Annihilation will bow down and put his arms to the side of the portal as 2 Devil's Gazes and 4 Burning Irises are summoned to the sides of the arena symmetrically. They will constantly fire beams of fire at players.

- New Sun: Annihilation's ultimate ability. Used when its at 50% HP and again when at 20%, it will raise both of its arms and open its mouth as it summons a ball of light from itself that gradually grows. This enemy is called the New Sun that travels down the bridge, and must be killed quickly or else all players participating in the fight will instantly die once it reaches its full size. New Sun can also rapidly shoot fireballs after it reaches certain size. Additionally, Two Infernal Subjugates will also spawn at the far-left and far-right sides of the arena.
When Annihilation is defeated, it will collapse and reach its arms out in desperation as its pulled back into the Corruption Portal.
- Crafted Scrolls should be used in parties 20-30 seconds before the fight, alongside other consumables.
- Stay together as a team to receive supporting effects from other party members.
- During Cauterize Them All, move away from Annihilation to dodge the first set of meteors, then move closer to Annihilation to dodge the other two volleys.
- Move in a circle to prevent being hit by Apocalyptic Sigil.

- New Sun should be prioritized above all else. Aim for the center as the hitbox for the New Sun is small despite it getting bigger. After the sun is destroyed, the party should then prioritize the Infernal Subjugates on the left and right sides of the arena.
- Infernal Subjugates should be prioritized as they can heal Annihilation by massive amount.
- Annihilation was teased with various crude drawings during the buildup to the Rekindled World reveal.
- When Deusphage, the modeller of Annihilation, was creating the design and model for it, she based the texture off of an image of raw, ground ostrich meat.
- The word "HELL" is hidden in the muscle fibers.
- Due to Annihilation's long name, some community members have nicknamed it Annie or Anni.
- Annihilation has several death messages attached to it:
- "''Player'' became another casualty of War."
- "Hellfire burns ''Players corpse."
- "''Player'' succumbed to madness."
- "''Player'' was annihilated."
- "''Player'' fell to inevitable extinction."
- "''Player'' was reduced to ashes."
- "''Players soul was extinguished."
- "''Player'' was entirely corrupted."

- Annihilation is one of the only mobs in the game to have a red bossbar, which is often used for enemies that are closely related to Corruption and the Realm of War. The only other mobs that share this trait are the Bane of the Great Bridge, Her Majesty, Lesser Rifts, and Anathema.

- The appearance of a Tuffer is lightly based on the Midday Lycanroc from Pokémon.

- According to Deusphage, Tuffers are wolves native to the region that possess magical adaptations to take advantage of the shifting nature of the Canyon of the Lost. When buried by landslides they will enter a period of hibernation for hundreds or potentially thousands of years until they're uncovered again.
- Differentiating them from the other canid species present in the world are their saber teeth and far longer ears.

- Being based off the real life larger ancestors to the modern day wolf, dire wolves, the Dire Tuffer is one that has been in hibernation for likely hundreds of thousands of years, coming from a point in history where the species were far larger than their modern day counterparts.

intro.text: World Events are a mechanic added to Wynncraft in the 2.1 update. They can start in various areas in the world at any time and involve fighting waves of enemies culminating in a Boss. Once an event starts, the player and their party will have their own instance, with the mobs scaled to the highest-leveled player. The entire party wins as long as one or more players survive. World Events can reward players with various loots, including Dungeon Keys and Runes. Some World Events can also contain exclusive gears and Crafting Ingredients as rewards that cannot be found in normal way.

Some World Events are unique in that they are rarer in occurrence and also tougher than standard World Events, called Major World Events. As of 2.1 there is only one Major World Event, the Prelude to Annihilation.
Using World Event bomb will trigger all world events in that server to activate and start counting down, excluding Major World Events.
